summary: Manim supports precise, programmatic video generation, but a successfully rendered educational animation can still have visual defects, missing explanations, or incorrect content. Rendering does not directly identify the code changes needed to correct these visual failures, so feedback-driven revision is needed. Existing agentic frameworks use iterative rendering and revision but typically rely on large models, often proprietary. Existing Manim datasets primarily contain final programs and often lack quality verification and the trajectories of feedback and revisions needed to learn this refinement process. We introduce ManimData and ManimCode, a data and training framework for feedback-driven educational animation generation. We construct ManimData through a render-guided pipeline that iteratively generates, executes, reviews, and revises Manim programs with retrieved API documentation. Its 24,034 render-verified, quality-filtered records preserve intermediate programs, execution errors, visual critiques, and corrective revisions. We use role-conditioned supervised fine-tuning on these trajectories to train ManimCode, a single 4B model, to write, review, and revise animation programs. To improve correction of errors that differ from those in the collected trajectories, we then train the Reviser with reinforcement learning on self-generated states, using rendering outcomes and reference-free quality feedback. ManimCode achieves 96.6% and 97.0% render success on ManimData-test and ManimBench, compared with 52.6% and 82.0% for the untrained 4B model under the same inference setup, while also improving video quality scores from 2.48 to 2.94 and from 3.00 to 3.44. summary: Background and objective: Hyperkalaemia is common in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) treated with renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system inhibitors (RAASi) and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs). Although new potassium binders have demonstrated efficacy in clinical trials, evidence from real-world clinical practice remains limited. Materials and methods: We present a retrospective, observational, multicentre, non-interventional study aimed at evaluating the use of patiromer in patients with hyperkalaemia under routine clinical conditions in the Valencian Community. Patients who received patiromer for at least 3 months due to hyperkalaemia were included. The primary objective was to assess the evolution of serum potassium at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months after initiation of treatment. Secondary objectives included describing baseline patient characteristics, changes in RAASi and MRA therapy, and patiromer-related adverse events. Results: A total of 59 patients were included. The baseline serum potassium level was 5.72 mmol/L, showing significant reductions at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months (5.02, 5.17, 5.11, and 5.01 mmol/L, respectively; all P < .001). Patiromer treatment enabled continuation of RAASi in 94.9% of patients and MRAs in 98.3%. The most frequent adverse events were gastrointestinal. Patiromer was discontinued in 8 patients (13.5%), with adverse effects accounting for half of these cases. Conclusions: Our study provides real-world evidence on the effectiveness, safety, and RAASi/MRA maintenance potential of patiromer in patients with CKD and hyperkalaemia under routine care. In this setting, patiromer proved effective and well tolerated for managing hyperkalaemia and preserving RAASi/MRA therapy. © 2025 Sociedad Española de Nefrología Copyright © 2025 Sociedad Española de Nefrología. summary: Interpretability, AI auditing and assessments of machine consciousness increasingly rest on mechanism-level quantities: functionals of a system's causal transition law that describe how it computes, not what it outputs. Experiments see that law only through finite, partial and noisy interventions. We ask when such a quantity is identifiable from an experiment's access, continuous in the mechanism and certifiable from finite data, and answer exactly for a deliberately demanding case - the integrated information $\varphi$ of integrated information theory - in stochastic networks of four and five units with known ground truth. Behavior can be silent: a recurrent and a feed-forward network with identical input-output laws at their response delay carry 0.28 and 0 bits, yet internal recordings separate them within 4-53 trials. Partial access can be just as blind: in our examples, units left out of a one-step recording impose precision floors of 0.30-1.02 bits that no sample size lowers, and in all-but-self parity networks, recordings of any length see several hidden units only through the product of their fidelities - a symmetry that one intervention broke in exact checks. The measure has sharp edges: because $\varphi$ selects a partition, and the cause and effect it specifies, by one criterion and reports another, infinitesimal changes of mechanism that cross an edge change it by 25-100% at 99% of the edges we found in random networks, and about 1% of surrogate models that fit interventional data almost perfectly misreport it by more than 20%. One-sided claims survive: the same data certify a lower bound on both sides of an edge, and we prove $\varphi>1.004$ bits throughout a 64-dimensional region of mechanisms and certify it from about $10^7$ controlled transitions with false-certificate probability at most $α$. Measurability is thus a design question with computable answers.
title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information

summary: Knowledge distillation transfers predictions, representations, or other supervisory information between learning models and is increasingly investigated in quantum machine learning. Its applications extend beyond compression to cross-architecture transfer, circuit approximation, distributed learning, and classical deployment of models trained using quantum-derived supervision. This survey reviews these approaches using two complementary classification axes: teacher-student configuration and the role of quantum resources in the distillation process. Quantum-inspired methods are discussed separately from methods that simulate quantum computations classically or execute them on quantum hardware. We explain how measurement probabilities, expectation values, classical readouts, state overlaps, and circuit-level objectives support different transfer mechanisms. We then critically assess the presented results against baseline design, execution conditions, uncertainty, and resource costs. The evidence shows that distillation can improve selected quantum students, but benefits are task- and architecture-dependent, and several studies find negligible gains or even performance degradation. Evaluations on physical quantum hardware remain limited, with some testing individual quantum components rather than complete learning pipelines. Heterogeneous protocols and incomplete resource reporting prevent general conclusions about practical quantum advantage. We identify priorities for controlled benchmarking, noise-aware learning, reproducible evaluation, and efficient transfer between quantum and classical models.
title: Quantum Knowledge Distillation: State-of-the-art, Applications and Open Problems

summary: Standardised post-quantum cryptography (PQC) is critical for protecting software systems against future quantum threats, but standardised algorithms alone do not provide a pathway for their secure integration into software. This paper presents a Systematisation of Knowledge (SoK) of PQC integration in software development, synthesising existing approaches across implementation, migration, and developer education. We analyse these approaches against NIST PQC standards and PQC migration guidance, software development lifecycle coverage, cybersecurity practices, deployment maturity, and testing and evaluation evidence. Our analysis shows that existing work establishes important technical and organisational foundations but provides disconnected support across the software development lifecycle, with limited coordination between preparation, implementation, migration, deployment, maintenance, and developer practices. Evaluation evidence also remains concentrated in controlled or early-stage settings, providing stronger evidence of technical feasibility than operational readiness. We identify cross-cutting gaps and research directions for developing lifecycle-oriented, empirically validated approaches that connect technical, developer, and organisational requirements for secure PQC integration.
title: SoK: Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Integration in Software Development: Approaches, Gaps, and Future Directions

summary: We investigate the ultimate sensitivity limits for measuring small transverse beam displacements and identify optimal strategies that attain them, using the framework of mode parameter estimation. We contrast two families of states with different resource constraints, using Hermite-Gauss and Laguerre-Gauss mode pairs. First, for fixed total photon number states, the optimal state is identified and we show that it asymptotically approaches a rotated NOON state. The sensitivity bound is compared to that of an asymptotically optimal pure Gaussian state with fixed average photon number. Finally, we propose concrete measurement schemes using the method of moments and show that the twin-Fock state may provide a viable alternative to the rotated NOON state for this task. Our work provides a broader benchmark for developing practical strategies for spatial sensing at the quantum limit.
title: Quantum enhanced beam displacement estimation: sensitivity limits, optimal probes, and measurement schemes

summary: Discovering continuous symmetries directly from differential-equation data can reveal geometric structure for model reduction and scientific machine learning without symbolic determining equations or a closed-form representation of the governing system. We formulate intrinsic Lie point-symmetry discovery as an operator-theoretic problem on sampled jet-space data. Admissible generators are identified from a sampled determining operator and separated from redundant, solution-dependent, and geometrically trivial directions. The framework combines prolongation, sequential subspace restrictions, and a fixed nonlinear dictionary linear in trainable coefficients. A rank-stabilization preflight test diagnoses systems whose represented intrinsic symmetry algebra does not stabilize under dictionary refinement. On a controlled differential-equation benchmark with an analytically known 11-dimensional represented intrinsic symmetry algebra, the method recovers the complete represented generator set, reproduces its Lie-bracket structure to numerical precision, and approximates a known generator beyond the training domain. Here we show that explicit intrinsic continuous-symmetry generators can be recovered from data obtained from exact or approximate differential systems.
title: Data-driven discovery of intrinsic Lie point symmetries of differential equation systems

summary: Coding agents are among the most economically consequential deployments of LLMs to date, making reliable evaluation increasingly important. Yet even benchmarks that are carefully validated at release can become stale. As models improve, they can discover valid solutions that existing verifiers reject, while changes to evaluation infrastructure can invalidate assumptions embedded in tasks and tests. We call the resulting accumulation of defects benchmark maintenance debt: a growing gap between benchmark scores and the capabilities they are intended to measure. We introduce a continuous-validation workflow for agentic benchmarks that combines community reports, task artifacts, agent traces, automated oracle checks, and human-gated repairs. We apply this workflow to Terminal-Bench 2.0, a benchmark that underwent extensive human and LM-assisted review and red-teaming before release. Our audit identifies issues in roughly 30% of the benchmark, and we release the resulting repairs as Terminal-Bench 2.1. These repairs change evaluation results: accuracy increased by over 10 percentage points and leaderboard positions move by up to three ranks, even as the overall ranking remains highly correlated (Spearman rho = 0.958). We evaluate how resource allocation shapes benchmark conclusions. We show that fixed wall-clock can materially change agent performance: For example, extending the time limit closes a 20pp harness gap on GPT 5.4 and shrinks a 30 pp gap on GPT 5.4 mini to 5 pp. Benchmark maintenance is therefore not only about repairing task artifacts: resource budgets are part of the measurement specification and must be validated alongside the tasks themselves. More broadly, benchmark maintenance debt is not just accumulated implementation bugs: our results show that as models improve, both evaluation assumptions and resource settings may need to be revalidated.
title: Benchmarks as Software: Terminal-Bench and the Case for Continuous Benchmarks

summary: The growing use of AI in mathematics raises a question: can we detect AI involvement in proofs, separately from AI assistance with writing? summary: Analog compute-in-memory (CIM) enables energy-efficient AI inference by performing in-situ matrix multiplication. The growing demand for deploying larger models motivates chiplet integration to expand CIM capacity. However, simulation abstractions based on local operator costs and aggregate communication metrics obscure the impact of weight-mapping topology when CIM system scales up. We develop a phase analysis that quantifies how strongly mapping topology affects system performance across hardware configurations and how mapping optimization translates into latency gains. To evaluate and exploit this design space, we present Isobar, a simulation platform integrating CIM decompositions, heterogeneous execution, and resource modeling. Validated against silicon measurements and cycle-accurate simulation, Isobar provides reliable cost estimates that enable effective mapping search across model and hardware configurations. For Gemma-7B prefill, Isobar-guided mapping reduces communication time by 23.3% and end-to-end latency by 18.6% relative to the strongest baseline. Isobar's system-level modeling show that analog CIM retains energy-efficiency potential relative to GPU when scaled to thousands of dies, and identify topology-aware mapping as a key design dimension for efficient execution.
title: Scaling Up Analog CIM: A Simulation Framework for Topology-Aware Mapping

summary: Latent communication enables agents to collaborate efficiently by directly exchanging intermediate model representations rather than raw sensor data or text messages. Existing approaches, however, are primarily designed for LLM agents and do not consider the bandwidth constraints and heterogeneous task deadlines faced by cyber-physical agents. In this work, we propose SCALE, a real-time latent communication method tailored for cyber-physical agents. Motivated by the spatio-temporal continuity of the physical world, SCALE matches tokens across consecutive latent messages using similarity scores to identify reusable information and avoid redundant transmission. It then profiles the semantic gain and communication cost of transmitting different amounts of latent information. Based on these profiles, SCALE employs a real-time scheduler that jointly determines which pending messages to transmit and how many latent tokens to send, subject to available bandwidth and task deadlines. We evaluate SCALE across three cyber-physical benchmarks and a physical spider robot case study under diverse network conditions and heterogeneous task deadlines. Our results show that SCALE significantly improves both task performance and on-time delivery in bandwidth-constrained networks. Our code is available at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/SCALE-4E80/.
title: SCALE: Real-Time Latent Communication for Cyber-Physical Agents

summary: We present an analysis of JADES-GS-BD-5, an extremely cold Y dwarf identified in the JADES/GOODS-South field. Using multi-epoch JWST/NIRCam imaging spanning a $\simeq2$-yr baseline, we calibrate the JWST astrometry and obtain the first robust parallax measurement for a brown dwarf discovered in a JWST extragalactic deep field. We measure a proper motion of $μ_{\rm tot}=49.8^{+0.3}_{-0.3}$ mas yr$^{-1}$ and a parallax of $\varpi=15.7^{+1.4}_{-1.3}$ mas, corresponding to a geometric distance of $d=64^{+6}_{-5}$ pc, $\sim3\times$ further than that of the previously known most distant Y dwarfs with parallax-measured distances. We hence determine a tangential velocity of $v_{\rm tan}=15.0^{+1.4}_{-1.3}$ km s$^{-1}$, consistent with a Galactic thin-disk object. We find no evidence for binary acceleration, significant photometric variability, or a plausible host. The $J$-band spectral morphology of JADES-GS-BD-5 is consistent with existing Y-dwarf templates, while its extremely faint luminosity and overall near-infrared spectral profile confirm that it is one of the coldest dwarfs discovered to date. We therefore adopt a classification of $>$Y1, consistent with a NIRCam colour-based proxy of cY1.5. The robust parallax-determined distance allows us to determine its bolometric luminosity, $\log(L_{\rm bol}/L_{\odot})=-7.08^{+0.09}_{-0.09}$. Evolutionary modelling places JADES-GS-BD-5 in the planetary-mass regime and makes it a rare benchmark for the study of cold giant-planet atmospheres. Current atmospheric models fail to reproduce its SED in detail, pointing to the importance of disequilibrium chemistry and vertical mixing. Finally, we also report additional proper motion measurements for eight of the other nine known JADES Y-dwarf candidates, highlighting JWST extragalactic surveys as a powerful route to building a statistically useful, parallax-calibrated sample of Y dwarfs.
title: The cold substellar frontier in JWST Extragalactic surveys: a robust parallax measurement yields the most distant known ultra-cold Y dwarf

summary: In hierarchical galaxy formation, supermassive black hole binaries are a ubiquitous consequence of frequent galaxy mergers, yet subparsec binaries remain difficult to be confirmed. Periodic flux modulations may arise from the orbital motion of black holes in close binaries, while relativistic jet precession can provide an additional source of periodic variability. Such periodic signatures therefore motivate us to identify close binary candidates. Here, we report an optical periodicity of $269^{+13}_{-14}$ days in both Zwicky Transient Facility g and r bands of the blazar PKS 0301-243, with corrected global significances of $2.75σ$ and $2.18σ$, respectively. This signal persists over 7 cycles across a baseline of ~2000 days. We interpret this period as a possible modulation associated with the orbital motion of a supermassive black hole binary. A longer optical periodicity of $889^{+47}_{-46}$ days is identified in Katzman Automatic Imaging Telescope, with corrected global significance of $1.97σ$. The longer periodicity spans approximately 5 cycles over a baseline of ~4500 days, potentially associated with jet precession. Both periodicities are independently identified using multiple methods. A supermassive black hole binary incorporating a relativistic jet and a circumbinary disc could reproduce the observed light curve ensemble. For a total mass of $10^{8.95} M_\odot$ and a mass ratio q = 0.1, the derived milli-parsec separation and a short gravitational wave driven coalescence time, $t_c = 1122^{+144}_{-144}$ years, imply that PKS 0301-243 may be a rare source of nano-hertz gravitational waves and a potential multimessenger laboratory for the terminal stages of supermassive black hole coalescence.
title: The complex periodic variability of PKS 0301-243: hints of a supermassive black hole binary candidate

summary: The Quantum Internet is commonly envisioned as a network that transports quantum states and distributes entanglement as the key resource underpinning distributed quantum applications. This view is necessary but incomplete if quantum phenomena are confined to what the network carries or manages, while network functionalities remain grounded predominantly in classical abstractions. This Perspective advances a broader thesis: quantum phenomena can also participate directly in the realization of network functionalities. We first establish the architectural baseline by introducing entanglement as a stateful network resource whose operational condition is non-locally distributed across remote nodes, evolves through manipulation or consumption, and degrades over time through decoherence. Its evolving state must therefore remain visible to the functionalities acting on it. We then move beyond resource visibility and use two mechanisms as proof points of a broader quantum-native functional design space: entanglement generation during propagation through coherent spatial-path superposition, and operational connectivity induced by shared entanglement that can depart from the physical graph. These examples show that paths, neighbors, or participating nodes may become operationally relevant in ways determined by quantum coherence and shared entanglement, rather than by physical connectivity alone. We identify Quantum Addressing as a transversal abstraction capable of representing such relations while complementing, rather than replacing, classical addressing and signaling. The resulting perspective broadens the Quantum Internet from transporting quantum information and distributing entanglement to exploiting quantum phenomena in network functioning, opening a coupled frontier spanning routing, forwarding, control, and functionality placement.
title: Beyond Quantum Messages: Toward Quantum-Native Network Functioning

summary: LLM-based medical assistants that follow a patient across visits need a memory that keeps the patient's clinical state correct as it changes. We examine the errors of five memory systems on longitudinal medical dialogue and find three recurring causes: the retrieved evidence gives an outdated state, includes another person's health facts, or lacks a safety fact the answer depends on. We present MedGraph, a graph memory built for these three cases. Construction extracts dated facts from each session, attributes each fact to the person it describes, and links medication, diagnosis, and measurement records into chains that keep earlier states. Retrieval ranks the patient's chains as units, reads each chain at the time the question asks about, and adds the original dialogue text; a patient profile lists every recorded safety fact with every question. On MedMemoryBench, MedGraph has the highest overall accuracy with both a GPT and a Qwen backbone, 10.5 and 10.4 points above the strongest of five baselines, with efficient memory construction and answering in the GPT setting.
title: MedGraph: Maintaining Patient State with Graph Memory for Long-Term Medical Dialogue

summary: Landing-phase safety-event prediction requires the detection of rare abnormal approaches within strongly imbalanced multivariate flight data. Capturing coupled temporal behavior while distinguishing event-specific signatures across airport operating contexts remains a central modeling challenge. This study proposes an interpretable hybrid feature-fusion framework for multiclass landing-phase safety-event prediction. A long short-term memory (LSTM) autoencoder trained on nominal flight windows characterizes deviations from routine approach behavior. Its continuous reconstruction-error descriptor is fused with parameter-specific statistical flight-history features and supplied to a class-weighted XGBoost classifier to distinguish Normal, Speed High, Path High, and Flaps Late windows. The framework is evaluated using 53,750 NASA DASHlink approach windows from three arrival airports. Pooled and airport-specific learning strategies are compared alongside component-level benchmarks, repeated pipeline retraining, and feature-attribution analysis. The results demonstrate strong class-balanced detection, with mean macro recall above 0.90 across all airports under repeated partitioning and retraining. Component comparisons establish the importance of class weighting and show that continuous feature fusion outperforms reconstruction-error-only and hard-gate alternatives. Airport-level comparisons reveal benefits from local specialization at the two airports with larger datasets and from pooled training at the airport with the smallest dataset. Feature attributions associate predictions with operationally relevant vertical-path, configuration, speed, and approach-context variables. The framework provides an interpretable approach to rare-event detection and practical guidance for adapting flight-data monitoring models to airport-level data availability.
title: Hybrid Machine Learning for Imbalanced Landing-Phase Safety Event Prediction from Flight Data

summary: Linear attention compresses context into a fixed-size key-value state for linear-time training and constant-memory inference. Gated delta-rule models decay this state and erase its prediction for an incoming key before writing a new value; Gated DeltaNet-2 (GDN-2) generalizes this with channel-wise decay and decoupled, full-rank erase and write gates. However, we show that state updates are far less sensitive to erasure than to writes: key activation and unit normalization concentrate key energy onto a sparse subset of channels, whereas value writes scale all channels, so the erase gate can be parameterized at lower rank. Furthermore, slow-decaying state rows accumulate much larger norms than fast rows, dominating unweighted readout and forcing stronger write-time erasure to suppress interference. Guided by this analysis, we introduce Muir, which fuses all gates into a sensitivity-allocated low-rank projection, re-weights state rows with a matched-filter readout gate, and reinvests the saved parameters in a wider feed-forward network. Because standard chunkwise algorithms become numerically unstable at the large chunk sizes needed to saturate wide matrix units, we design a parallel update for stable, efficient training. summary: Reconstructing turbulent flow fields from sparse and irregular measurements remains challenging because the underlying inverse problem is severely underdetermined. Here we present MANTRA, a manifold-based tensor framework that represents each velocity component in a continuous tensor-product space while constraining its coefficient tensor to a low-rank Tucker manifold. This structure provides a compact, data-adaptive representation without requiring gridded observations or governing equations. Riemannian optimization and adaptive selection of rank and basis complexity enable the model to exploit coordinate-wise spatiotemporal correlations. In simulations of forced isotropic turbulence and flow over a cylinder, MANTRA recovers multiscale structures at sampling densities orders of magnitude below the underlying grids and remains accurate under Gaussian noise up to 20% of the peak velocity. It also recovers leading coordinate-wise correlation structures from sparse observations. Applied to experimental particle-tracking velocimetry of an oscillating impinging jet, MANTRA reveals time-evolving structures that are not apparent from the scattered measurements alone.

summary: Two-phase designs provide a cost-effective framework for biomarker studies and have been widely used to reduce the burden of collecting expensive biomarker measurements. Most methodological research has focused on efficient Phase II sampling and estimation of biomarker--outcome associations. A natural subsequent step, however, is to incorporate identified biomarkers into risk prediction models, where measures of predictive performance become important inferential targets. Even for binary outcomes, methodological developments for two-phase designs that jointly address association parameters and predictive performance remain limited. Building on classical case-control and matched case-control designs developed primarily for association inference with binary outcomes, we propose a risk-matched case-control (RMCC) design that uses a scalar disease-risk score constructed from Phase I variables to define matching strata and guide Phase II sampling. To address the limitations of existing likelihood-based approaches, which typically require correct specification of the nuisance distribution of biomarkers, we develop a unified design-based inference framework based on inverse probability weighting for both association parameters and predictive performance measures, including positive predictive value and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. We further introduce target-specific weight scaling and calibration procedures and derive variance estimators that account for sampling variability in both phases. Simulation studies demonstrate the efficiency and robustness of the proposed design and inference procedures, and an application to a Taiwanese oral cancer cohort illustrates their potential utility.
title: Risk-matched case-control sampling and semiparametric weight calibration for efficient biomarker assessment with binary outcomes

summary: We study the coherent transfer of circulation between two weakly coupled lattice rings of ultracold bosons, in which a persistent current initially prepared in one ring oscillates back and forth between the rings without net transfer of particles. Combining Bose--Hubbard simulations with their Gross--Pitaevskii and quantum phase model limits, we show that similar current oscillations arise from two distinct microscopic mechanisms. At weak interactions, particles in each occupied momentum mode tunnel independently between the rings, leading to a transfer time inversely proportional to the inter-ring tunnelling, extensive particle-number fluctuations and entanglement distributed over many Schmidt components; this mode-exchange dynamics is suppressed by self-trapping as the interactions increase. At stronger interactions and large filling, in the phase-dominated regime, circulation is instead transferred through a second-order collective process between many-body persistent-current states, with a transfer time scaling as the inverse square of the inter-ring tunnelling in the weak-link limit. Number fluctuations then remain of order one instead of growing with the particle number, and within each number sector the system evolves into coherent superpositions of two many-body configurations, distinguished by which ring carries the circulation. The entanglement accessible under number-conserving operations therefore reaches up to approximately one bit. We propose a quench protocol to prepare the initial state and estimate transfer times within reach of current ring-lattice experiments, identifying coupled rings as a platform to study coherent quantum phase slips and to manipulate persistent-current states.
title: Coherent phase slips in coupled rings: from weak to strong interactions

summary: Semantic communication (SemCom) using a relay node is considered, where the relay assists in conveying task-relevant information from a source to a destination, with meaning defined by classification labels. summary: This work identifies a fundamental, controller-independent limitation in reusable launch vehicle powered descent: a sudden $180^\circ$ phase transition in the open-loop transfer functions from the control inputs to the lateral drift and drift rate. The transition occurs inside the flight envelope, reverses the effective control direction, and can destabilize the closed loop system under uncertainty. An analytical condition governing this transition is derived, its physical mechanism is established, and its dependence on vehicle mass, aerodynamic properties, and geometry is characterized. An Incremental Nonlinear Dynamic Inversion (INDI)-based control architecture is then developed to inherently address this limitation and is tuned via $\mathcal{H}_\infty$ Closed Loop Shaping to provide local robustness and performance guarantees. The internal dynamics introduced by the INDI inversion are analytically derived and proven to be stable throughout the flight envelope. The proposed controller is compared against a robust gain-scheduled baseline controller through linear stability analysis and an extensive nonlinear Monte Carlo campaign. Both controllers achieve 100% success across the considered Monte Carlo campaign, though the INDI-based controller provides improved tracking performance, superior nominal and dispersed stability margins, requires fewer controller design points, and reduces controller tuning complexity.
title: Overcoming Fundamental Control Limitations in Powered Descent Flight through Robust Incremental Nonlinear Dynamic Inversion

summary: Bacterial cellulose biofilms are complex networks of strong interwoven nanofibers that control transport and protect bacterial colonies in the film. Design of diverse applications of bacterial cellulose films also relies on understanding and controlling transport through the fiber mesh, and transport simulations of the films are most accurate when guided by experimental characterization of the structures and the resultant diffusion inside. Diffusion through such films is a function of their key microstructural length scales, determining how molecules, as well as particles and microorganisms, permeate them. We use microscopy to study the unique bacterial cellulose film structure and quantify the mobility dynamics of various sizes of tracer particles and macromolecules. Mobility is hindered within the films, as confinement and local movement strongly depend on void size relative to diffusing tracers. The biofilms have a naturally periodic structure of alternating dense and porous layers of nanofiber mesh, and we tune the magnitude of the spacing via fermentation conditions. Micron-sized particles can diffuse through the porous layers, but can not penetrate the dense layers. Tracer mobility in the porous layers is isotropic, indicating a largely random pore structure there. Molecular diffusion through the whole film is only slightly reduced by the structural tortuosity. Knowledge of transport variations within bacterial cellulose networks can be used to guide design of symbiotic cultures in these structures and enhance their use in applications biomedical implants, wound dressings, lab-grown meat, and sensors.
title: Molecular and colloidal transport in bacterial cellulose hydrogels

summary: Bacterial cellulose is an important class of biomaterials which can be grown in well-controlled laboratory and industrial conditions. The cellulose structure is affected by several biological, chemical and environmental factors, including hydrodynamic flows in bacterial suspensions. In this work, we explore the possibility of using well controlled turbulent flow to control the bacterial cellulose production. Turbulent flows leading to random motion of fluid elements may affect the structure of the extracellular polymeric matrix produced by bacteria. Here we show that two-dimensional turbulence at the air-liquid interface generates chaotic rotation at a well-defined scale and random persistent stretching of the fluid elements. The results offer new approaches to engineering of the bacterial cellulose structure by controlling turbulence parameters.
title: Turbulence-assisted formation of bacterial cellulose

summary: Hydrogels provide a solution-mimicking environment for the interaction with living systems that make them desirable for various biomedical and technological applications. Because relevant biological processes in living tissues occur at the biomolecular scale, hydrogel nanopatterning can be leveraged to attain novel material properties and functionalities. However, the fabrication of high aspect ratio (HAR) nanostructures in hydrogels capable of self-standing in aqueous environments, with fine control of the size and shape distribution, remains challenging. Here, we report the synthesis of nanostructures with a HAR in bacterial cellulose (BC) hydrogel via directed plasma nanosynthesis using argon ions. The nanostructures in BC are reproducible, stable to sterilization, and liquid immersion. Using in-situ surface characterization and semi-empirical modeling, we discovered that pattern formation was linked to the formation of graphite-like clusters composed of a mixture of C-C and C=C bonds. Moreover, our model predicts that reactive species at the onset of the argon irradiation accelerate the bond breaking of weak bonds, contributing to the formation of an amorphous carbon layer and nanopattern growth.
title: Ion-induced nanopatterning of a bacterial cellulose hydrogel

The structural characterization using x-ray diffraction and electron microscopies indicates the presence of only Ni and cellulose with no other phases. The uncontrolled growth of Ni in cellulose matrix results in the formation of nanoparticles with 3 different size distributions - 10 nm particles mainly distributed along the length of fibrils, 50 nm particles present in the intermediate spaces between the fibrils and 100 nm particles present in voids formed by the reticulate structure. At room temperature the composites exhibit a weakly ferromagnetic behavior with a coercivity of 40 Oe which increases to 160 Oe at 10 K. The transition from weakly ferromagnetic state at room temperature to a superferromagnetic state at low temperatures is mediated via a superspinglass state at intermediate temperatures. A temperature dependent microstructural model has been developed combining the structural and magnetic results obtained from the two composite aerogels.
title: Interparticle interactions mediated superspinglass to superferromagnetic transition in Ni-bacterial cellulose aerogel nanocomposites

summary: Background: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are persistent, hydrophobic and in several cases carcinogenic pollutants of soils and sediments. Bacterial degradation of high-molecular-weight PAHs is slow because of their low bioavailability, which has directed attention to ligninolytic fungi that attack pollutants extracellularly. Scope: This narrative review, based exclusively on published secondary data (1983–2024), examines the diversity of ligninolytic fungi, their enzyme systems, the biochemical mechanisms of PAH transformation, the factors that control degradation in soil, and the evidence from pilot- and field-scale applications. Key findings: Lignin peroxidase, manganese peroxidase (including lipid-peroxidation chemistry), versatile peroxidase and laccase–mediator systems oxidise PAHs to quinones and ring-fission products, while cytochrome P450 monooxygenases and unspecific peroxygenases form dihydrodiols and phenols. Fungi mineralise only part of the oxidised carbon, but their polar products are readily mineralised by soil bacteria. Field trials – from US demonstrations with Phanerochaete sordida to tonne-scale Finnish piles inoculated on pine bark and Danish trials with spent oyster-mushroom substrate – confirm that inoculation and colonisation are feasible, but improvements over indigenous microbial activity have been inconsistent and strongly site-dependent, limited by bioavailability, competition and logistics. Conclusion: Ligninolytic fungi are most promising for soils dominated by high-molecular-weight PAHs and as partners in integrated fungal–bacterial treatment. Soil-competent strains, low-cost lignocellulosic carriers, attention to bioavailability and standardised metabolite and toxicity monitoring are required for reliable field deployment.

title: Ligninolytic Fungi in Bioremediation: Mechanism of Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon (Pah) Degradation and Field Applications

summary: Grant-free uplink access in low-Earth-orbit (LEO) non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) poses a coordination challenge when multiple UEs share a satellite channel without real-time centralized scheduling under long propagation delays and time-varying channels. Conventional random access does not exploit peer context, leading to collisions and inefficient channel use as contention increases. To address this problem, we propose IRIS, a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for decentralized grant-free direct-to-satellite (D2S) uplink access, with A2A-IRIS as its sidelink-assisted Agent-to-Agent (A2A) realization. Each UE executes a shared binary transmission policy using local traffic/channel information augmented by compact peer states exchanged over UE-to-UE sidelink, while Vanilla-IRIS serves as a local-only ablation. Evaluations in rural and suburban LEO D2S deployments use TLE-based trajectories propagated using the Simplified General Perturbations 4 (SGP4), with a Walker-Delta constellation as fallback. A2A-IRIS achieves 2.1579 and 5.4478 Mbps, corresponding to 99.9% and 96.1% of the respective scenario-specific upper bounds. Relative to Vanilla-IRIS, throughput improves by 40.8% and 325.0%, with collision rates of 0.0000 and 0.0433, while one- and two-epoch delayed centralized schedulers are outperformed by approximately 51--130%. A2A-IRIS also improves fairness, service coverage, and transmission efficiency with moderate Deep Q-Network (DQN) inference overhead. Active-UE load scalability results further show sustained performance over the evaluated load range. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of sidelink-assisted A2A coordination for decentralized LEO D2S uplink access under propagation delay and delayed channel feedback.
title: IRIS: Intelligent Random Access with Integrated Shared Learning for Decentralized LEO Direct-to-Satellite Uplinks

summary: Wellbore stability analysis is an essential part of well planning where mechanical characteristics of rocks and the state of in-situ stresses are determined to evaluate the likelihood of borehole failure during drilling. In this study, natural and drilling induced fractures were characterized using image logs for a fractured reservoir located in Southern Iran. Mechanical Earth Modeling (MEM) and wellbore stability analysis were also carried out by the combination of wireline log data and in-situ measurements for a vertical well drilled in this field. The obtained results indicated the presence of several major/minor fractures in the studied interval but majority of them were found to be closed fractures. According to the MEM, formations would suffer from breakout (shear failure) in several intervals which might be linked to their low strengths, huge stress anisotropy and inappropriate selection of the mud weight. Give then fact that the break-out failure obtained from the Mogi-Coulomb criterion had a match with the borehole failure captured by the caliper log, the geomechanical parameters estimated through the methodology proposed should have sufficient accuracy and can be used for the stability analysis of other wells drilled in the same field.
title: Natural fracture characterization and wellbore stability analysis of a highly fractured southwestern Iranian oilfield

summary: Thermal Quantum Annealing (tQuA) is a quantum architecture in which a system coupled non-adiabatically to a thermodynamic reservoir evolves toward the ground state of a target Hamiltonian . This paper provides a rigorous and honest foundation for tQuA and its extension to Quantum Intelligent Matrix Methods (QIMM). We distinguish carefully among Theorems (proved in cited literature), Propositions (proof sketches with explicitly identified gaps), and Conjectures (claims with open steps). This work delivers three principal contributions: Convergence Proof Chain: We present a five-pillar proof chain establishing that tQuA converges to the global minimum from any initial state, without adiabatic scheduling, without eigenstate knowledge, and with a strictly positive escape rate from every local minimum at any . Honest Scaling Benchmarks: We present scaling benchmarks for the Liouvillian spectral gap   on gopherhole Hamiltonians, reporting a key finding: fixed-schedule tQuA achieves a perfectly flat gap ( , independent of   up to ) when the number of local minima   is fixed and small, but experiences steep polynomial decay ( ) when   grows proportionally to . Adaptive Policy Framework: Third, we outline a rich adaptive annealing policy framework using observed function evaluations and prior probability distributions   over problem classes, framing it as a primary research direction for future empirical tuning.   The framework applies broadly to nonconvex optimization in artificial intelligence, signal processing, and imaging, with specific application to "seeing the sky" technologies described in the companion paper on intensity-correlation interferometry (Hyland & Werbos 2024).

summary: In standard multi-head attention, every head uses the same query, key, and value (QKV) projection matrices for every token. We study a simple variant in which, in every layer, a subset of the heads are token-specific: their QKV projections depend on the identity of the input token, while the remaining heads keep ordinary shared projections. Token-specific projections are parameterized as a shared matrix plus a per-token low-rank correction stored in a hashed lookup table, so the extra computation is small, although the parameter count grows. In GPT-style language models trained on FineWeb, with 2 of 4 heads per layer token-specific, every run had lower validation loss than every standard-attention run, at both of the scales we tested. At the larger of two scales (6 layers, width 512, 300M training tokens, 3 seeds per method), validation loss fell from 4.154 ± 0.005 to 4.107 ± 0.008, a 4.6% reduction in perplexity. A control that adds the same number of lookup-table parameters to the same heads as per-token vectors, rather than per-token matrix corrections, reached only 4.148 ± 0.002, indicating that the gain is not explained by the additional parameters alone. At the smaller scale, a sweep over the number of token-specific heads suggests that mixing token-specific and shared heads works at least as well as making all heads token-specific. The main cost is throughput: our unoptimized implementation trains about 30% slower than the baseline. These are small-scale results, and we discuss their limitations in detail.
title: Token-Specific Attention Heads: Mixing Per-Token and Shared Query, Key, and Value Projections in Transformer Language Models

summary: Abstract The Laser Cognition (LC) is a proposed multilevel theoretical framework for investigating how selective attention, conscious access, curiosity-guided inquiry, associative recruitment, and representational integration may contribute to the emergence and evaluation of novel ideas. Its central explanatory metaphor is laser illumination: a complex cognitive field contains multiple thoughts, memories, representations, and potential relationships, while a selected cognitive target receives processing priority. The framework uses this metaphor to organize a proposed mechanism linking cognitive-field activation, attentional targeting, awareness-mediated processing, focus regulation, associative recruitment, integrative recombination, candidate generation, and metacognitive evaluation. LC retains the distinction between the full theory, its default mechanism, and its canonical primary case. The primary case is the Laser-Spotlight Cognitive Genesis Case (LSCGC); the proposed default mechanism is the Laser Cognition Default Mechanism (LC-DM); and its principal operational cycle is the Laser-Guided Cognitive Integration Cycle (LGCIC). The framework is formalized using a weighted cognitive graph, a dual-route attentional-targeting model, a normalized attentional-allocation function, a focus-stability measure, an associative-recruitment equation, a cognitive-integration index, a probabilistic candidate-emergence model, and a feedback-control representation. The mathematical expressions constitute proposed model specifications, not established equations of human neural operation. Awareness, attention, curiosity, affective engagement, cognitive flexibility, and metacognitive monitoring are treated as related but conceptually distinct constructs. The architecture includes eighteen layers, a multidomain research structure, eight initial research hypotheses, explicit falsifiability requirements, a cross-system functional generalization framework, a fourteen-step research protocol, and a twenty-part manuscript structure. Human cognition is the primary explanatory domain. Applications to artificial intelligence, large language models, artificial general intelligence, and possible artificial superintelligence are framed as hypotheses about functional or computational correspondence rather than established claims of shared consciousness or identical mechanisms. LC is presented as a theory-development and validation framework. Its explanatory value, novelty, causal assumptions, parameter identifiability, empirical adequacy, and cross-domain applicability remain subject to systematic literature review, mathematical audit, empirical testing, model comparison, and replication.

title: THE LASER COGNITION (LC): A Multilevel Neurocognitive, Mathematical, and Cybernetic Framework of Awareness-Guided Attentional Illumination, Neural-Pattern Integration, and Novel Idea Emergence

summary: This archive contains the code, derived data, and results of the study " Reported or observed? Satellite-mapped flood exposure reveals a reporting gap that machine-learned impact models inherit."  The study compares the number of people reported as affected by floods in EM-DAT with the population living inside the inundation mapped by MODIS in the Global Flood Database, for 1,266 country-level flood records from 2000 to 2018. It measures how the ratio of reported to observed impact depends on the reporting country at equal hazard, including floods that cross borders; tests whether ridge and gradient-boosting impact models trained on reported labels inherit this dependence; evaluates transfer across continents with importance weighting, the area of applicability and (weighted, Mondrian) conformal prediction; and shows how a small fraction of satellite labels removes most of the inherited bias. Results are expressed in the relative economic value of impact-based warnings. Contents. scripts/: the complete Python pipeline, including Google Earth Engine extraction of observed labels, ex-ante exposure (GHSL, GloFAS, MERIT Hydro) and ERA5-Land forcing on administrative footprints (steps 10-15), statistical and machine-learning analyses (steps 20-25), and figure scripts (steps 30-32). jobs/: the SLURM batch script used on the national supercomputer of Côte d'Ivoire and an equivalent local runner. data/: derived tables at the level of the EM-DAT record (observed exposure and flooded area, quality fractions, exposure and landscape predictors, hydroclimatic forcing, country covariates, EM-DAT-GFD links), GFD event metadata, study regions and a Natural Earth base map. results/: all result tables of the paper (2,000 cluster-bootstrap draws). README.md explains how to reproduce every result and figure. EM-DAT data are not redistributed, in accordance with the CRED terms of use. The derived tables carry only the EM-DAT identifier, country code and year. Users can download the public EM-DAT export of 11 May 2026 from https://www.emdat.be and rebuild the analysis table with two scripts; with that export the rebuilt table is identical to the one used in the paper. Code is released under the MIT licence; derived data and results under CC BY 4.0, without prejudice to the licences of the source products (Global Flood Database, ERA5-Land, GHSL, GloFAS, MERIT Hydro, FAO GAUL, World Bank indicators, Natural Earth).
title: Reported or observed? Flood reporting gap and machine-learned impact models: code, derived data and results

The package contains the raw study inputs (cleaned timing/SQL spreadsheet, hand-coded behavioral proxies, 11 think-aloud transcripts, per-participant notebooks and reports), derived and graded artifacts (execution-based correctness grades, three LLM-judge grades, BIRD gold answers, model/timing CSVs, LLM inter-coder reliability files), and the full analysis pipeline (figure notebook, execution grader, gold-answer fetcher, difficulty-validation and effect-size scripts). See README.md for the layout and steps. The BIRD gold SQLite databases are not included but are regenerated from the public BIRD train split via the provided script. Code is released under the MIT License; data files under CC BY 4.0.
title: Replication Package: Natural Language Interfaces for Databases — What Changes for Users? (SQL-LLM vs. Snowflake User Study)

summary: Audio textures exhibit complex temporal dynamics that are not well represented by single-scale models. We propose a multi-scale latent trajectory approach for audio texture synthesis using latent representations extracted from a pretrained neural audio codec. By decomposing latent trajectories into slow structural and fast stochastic components, we enable direct modeling and interpretation of the longterm temporal structure and fine-grained detail of audio textures. Our experiments on environmental audio textures suggest that the proposed method significantly improves audio quality over a single-scale baseline and achieves performance competitive with a latent diffusion model. Using perceptually motivated summary statistics, we demonstrate that generated continuations preserve texture identity. Through the proposed methods, we enable continuous texture generation from a given context and expose a latent structure that may support control over long-term dynamics.
title: MULTI-SCALE LATENT TRAJECTORY MODELLING FOR AUDIO TEXTURE SYNTHESIS

summary: Аннотация. В статье представлен комплексный лингвистический и историко-дипломатический анализ письма вице-губернатора крепости Анапа Сеид-Махмуда Мусселима от 29 марта 1817 года, которое адресовано русскому адмиралу Алексею Самуиловичу Грейгу. Этот документ рассматривается как важнейшее локальное историческое открытие, который на данный момент формирует вокруг себя уникальный контекст пограничной российско-османской коммуникации и одновременно вписывается в макроконтекст реализации условий Бухарестского мирного договора 1812 г. В ходе исследования подробно изучена композиционная структура документа, выявлены системные графические, орфографические и грамматические девиации во французском тексте. Исследование позволяет реконструировать уровень османских адъютантов и специфику функционирования французского языка как инструмента дипломатии.   Abstract. The article presents a complex linguistic and historical-diplomatic analysis of the letter of the vice-governor of the fortress Anapa Seyid-Mahmud Mousselim dated 29 March 1817, which was addressed to the Russian admiral Alexey Samuilovitch Greig. This document is regarded as the most important local historical discovery, which at the moment forms around it a unique context of the Russian border -Ottoman communication and at the same time fits into the macro context of the implementation of the terms of the Treaty of Bucharest (1812). In the course of the study, the compositional structure of the document was thoroughly examined, systematic graphical, orthographic, and grammatical deviations in the French text were identified. The study allows for a reconstruction of the level of Ottoman adjutants and the specificity of the functioning of the French language as an instrument of diplomacy.
title: ЛИНГВИСТИЧЕСКИЕ ИНТЕРФЕРЕНЦИИ И ПРАГМАТИКА ДИПЛОМАТИЧЕСКОГО ДИСКУРСА В РОССИЙСКО-ОСМАНСКОЙ КОРРЕСПОНДЕНЦИИ НАЧАЛА XIX ВЕКА (НА МАТЕРИАЛЕ ПИСЬМА ИЗ АНАПЫ А.С. ГРЕЙГУ)

summary: Supplementary dataset for three pre-registered buyer-side experiments verifying x402 v2 payments on Base mainnet, executed as scripted protocol runs and committed regardless of outcome; every reported number traces to a committed analysis.json and raw artifacts under experiments/ . Experiment 1: echo-verify A fresh USD 0.01 mainnet happy-path settlement, verified end-to-end via payer-anchored Transfer events on two independent RPCs (paid run 1.11 s; discovery median 0.0388 s over 15 GETs; tx 0xa3143d32319392227c017ce86dceb2a8e377b7e4f32c21f2693a6925e91f201c ). Headline finding: exactly 0.01 USDC settled to payTo per Transfer events on both RPCs. Experiment 2: mock-seller Hostile-seller failure-mode detection, including a same-nonce EIP-3009 replay on an Anvil fork pinned at block 54035433. Headline finding: 4 of 4 hostile-seller failure modes were correctly detected; the replay reverted at EVM state level with FiatTokenV2: authorization is used or canceled . Experiment 3: preflight-external Decode-only compatibility probing of third-party x402 endpoints, with a hard no-payment guard: zero payment-bearing headers sent, guard trips on 0 paid requests. Headline finding: 2 of 3 third-party endpoints returned protocol-compatible v2 402 challenges; agent402.tools diverged with a 404. Findings are about verification of the x402 protocol, not any product.

summary: Analysis and figure-generation code for the manuscript "[title]". The code demonstrates, on a public dataset of student teaching evaluations, why comparing a section's mean rating to a department average is statistically invalid, and shows how the power to detect a real difference collapses at small sample sizes. Scripts: turkiye_simulation_NREP5000.py (Monte Carlo power/breakpoint analysis), turkiye_leaveoneout_analysis.py (structure and leave-one-out benchmark comparisons), turkiye_make_all_figures.py (figures). See README for versions and seeds. Data: Türkiye Student Evaluation dataset (Gündüz & Fokoue), UCI ML Repository ID 262, DOI 10.24432/C5S02S, CC BY 4.0. Not redistributed here; retrieved from UCI at run time. Reproducibility: all draws seeded; results stable to <1 percentage point at NREP = 5000; fast Mann–Whitney routine validated against scipy to machine precision. Requirements: Python 3 with numpy, pandas, scipy, matplotlib, ucimlrepo. License: [MIT/BSD-3-Clause]. Please cite both this code and the dataset (DOI 10.24432/C5S02S). Code is released under the MIT License; figures and documentation are released under CC BY 4.0.
title: Statistics of Course Evaluation Scores

summary: Designing healthcare strategies requires anticipating their clinical and operational consequences before implementation, a task that often relies on health system simulation. Such a simulation necessitates modeling how patient states evolve and generate care demands. However, conventional approaches typically tailor compact state transitions to a single policy question and omit history-dependent dynamics, thus requiring the redefinition of states and transitions when there is a new question that entails different clinical information. We propose to learn a patient world model from longitudinal EHRs using a neural network to provide a shared clinical representation of patient trajectories that can serve simulation questions across scenarios. Taking ICU operations as an example, we train the model on MIMIC-IV, freeze it, and couple its time-queryable predictions to shared ICU calendars, resources, and queues via scenario-specific mappings, so that one model renders admission demand, care tasks, and discharge proposals across simulations evaluating ICU bed capacity, care dispatch, and post-ICU transfer capacity. Experiments show that our model matches Markov and semi-Markov comparators in aggregate occupancy and directional responses to capacity and dispatch policies. It also reproduces policy gains from replayed observed trajectories. For patients entering the same support state from different prior trajectories, the learned representation captures a 24-h recovery difference (-6.4 predicted versus -6.7 observed percentage points), a contrast missed by compact state models, which propagates into distinct simulated care demand, queue burden, and bed use. These results indicate that a learned world model of patient dynamics has the potential to replace question-specific state models, allowing new care policies to be evaluated by reconfiguring the scenario without model rebuilding.
title: Learning a patient world model for health system simulation in intensive care

summary: Imagine an AI that makes so many paperclips it consumes resources needed for human life. Its measure of success has displaced the purpose that made it valuable. This failure shares an optimization structure with Goodhart's law, which arose from human monetary policy. The connection turns the question toward civilization itself. Markets became powerful by responding to dispersed knowledge and changing reality. Yet financial success can increasingly depend on accumulating claims over future production rather than expanding human possibilities. We examine that hypothesis through financial claims, asset revaluation, and housing access. The Declaration of Independence supplies a different account of purpose: life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. Enterprises can preserve market discovery while organizing first to avoid harm, then to create human benefit, and finally to earn returns that sustain their work. Perhaps solving the paperclip problem for machines begins with solving it for ourselves.
title: The Human Paperclip Maximizer: Goodhart's Law, Financial Optimization, and the Preconditions for AI Alignment

summary: AI appears to be accelerating because its benchmark scores are accelerating. Yet the systems being measured are trained and selected through closed procedures, while useful intelligence is ultimately judged against an open-ended world. Object detection provides an unusually direct empirical test of this mismatch. The high-end conventional COCO record reviewed here reached approximately 66 average precision in 2023 and has changed little through 2026 despite sustained research, large models, new architectures, new supervision, synthetic data, prompting, and architecture search. This is not a comparison between obsolete vision technology and modern language AI: object detection now uses the same fundamental machinery—transformers, learned representations, gradient optimization, sequence prediction, and in some systems the same multimodal parameters. Pix2Seq explicitly formulates detection as language modeling; Florence-2 and PaliGemma perform both perceptual and linguistic tasks.   We develop a mathematical model of the closed/open mismatch. Let an open causal state space have effective dimension d while the information admitted by a closed optimizer lies on a codimension-one boundary. At resolution ε, the number of distinguishable open states scales as (R/ε)^d while the boundary scales as (R/ε)^(d−1). The corresponding metric-entropy ratio approaches (d−1)/d. Under a state-identification model, Fano's inequality converts this information ratio into the same asymptotic upper bound on exact identification. For a three-dimensional causal volume and its two-dimensional boundary, the result is 2/3.   The theorem is mathematical: it establishes what follows from the stated information geometry. Its application to AI is scientific: observation determines whether contemporary closed-ended systems serving open-ended objectives exhibit that geometry. The empirical record is strikingly consistent with the resulting two-thirds hypothesis. Closed language benchmarks can exceed two-thirds easily because the objective itself is closed. More reality-coupled end-to-end tasks remain much harder. Recursive self-improvement does not escape the information boundary merely by searching it more aggressively. Under the stated information constraint, additional optimization alone cannot remove the modeled limitation.
title: The Illusion of Accelerating Intelligence: Closed Optimization, Open-Ended Reality, and the Two-Thirds Limit

summary: Integrating contemporary infill architectural projects into historical urban environments presents a delicate challenge between spatial evolution and cultural heritage preservation. Traditional visual impact assessments rely heavily on qualitative, subjective expert evaluations, often leading to procedural delays, public disputes, and compromised urban aesthetics. This paper develops a quantitative, multi-criteria methodology—termed the Visual-Spatial Adaptability Index (VSAI)—to evaluate and optimize the insertion of new architectural objects within historic urban contexts. Combining 3D volumetric viewshed analysis, 2D morphological silhouette integrity, facade solid-to-void rhythm analysis, and computational material texture matching, the VSAI framework establishes an objective metric for context-sensitive design. Empirical validation conducted across 50 infill intervention scenarios in historic urban centers demonstrates that VSAI-guided design optimization yields a 34.2% increase in expert approval consensus and a 42.1% reduction in historical view corridor occlusion compared to conventional baseline proposals. The methodology provides urban planning boards, heritage authorities, and architectural practitioners with a repeatable, transparent computational tool for sustainable heritage conservation.
tags: Historical urban environment, Visual-spatial adaptability, Infill architecture, Viewshed analysis, Urban morphology, Heritage conservation, IMRAD
title: DEVELOPMENT OF A METHODOLOGY FOR ASSESSING THE VISUAL AND SPATIAL ADAPTABILITY OF NEW ARCHITECTURAL OBJECTS IN HISTORICAL URBAN ENVIRONMENTS

summary: We study an extremal problem involving three disks inside the unit disk. Two disks are initially placed so that they are tangent to each other and internally tangent to the unit circle. A third disk of maximum possible radius is then inserted, subject to tangency with both original disks. We prove that the minimum possible sum of the areas of the three disks is 11π/18, attained when their radii are 1/2, 1/2, and 1/3. Surprisingly, the minimizing configuration does not consist of three equal disks, despite the symmetry of the problem. Three different proofs are presented, based on Descartes' circle theorem, geometric inversion, and a parametrization using tangency points.
tags: Circle packing; Descartes' circle theorem; inversion; extremal geometry; geometric optimization
title: Three Circles in a Unit Disk: Three Solutions to an Extremal Problem

summary: This dataset supports the manuscript “Assessing the Interpretability of QM/MM Interaction Energies: A Representation-Aware Diagnostic Framework,” submitted to the Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling (ci-2026-038804). The numerical data describe three retrospective peptide–enzyme case studies: prolyl endopeptidase (PEP; primary nine-peptide electronic-energy analysis, 82 retained configurations), historical beta-secretase 1 (BACE1; 63 audited snapshots, 52 retained after cleaning), and reconstructed angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE; 131 valid QM/MM decompositions, with a distinct 73-configuration GIF/IP/LP core comparison). These data support question-specific representation diagnostics and descriptive configurational-contrast analysis; they do not establish universal applicability or external affinity-prediction performance. Version v4 adds recovered simulation input files, topology and parameter files, preparation and analysis scripts, and file-level provenance manifests. The input supplement contains 8,597 recovered source files, together with the unchanged earlier numerical archive and verification records (8,740 regular files in total). It includes GROMACS run inputs for PEP and BACE1, ACE OpenMM production configurations and Amber input files, Zn-model parameterisation/validation inputs, ORCA component inputs with their coordinate and point-charge dependencies, and separately identified sensitivity, matched-perturbation, and unsuccessful diagnostic branches. The earlier numerical archive is also retained as a separate top-level download for continuity. No scientific numerical results were changed. The computational representations differ among the case studies. Primary PEP uses mixed AMBER03/CHARMM27 production protocols and inherited embedding charges. Historical BACE1 uses dynamically selected gas-phase receptor clusters and is retained for representation auditing. Corrected ACE uses snapshot-specific electrostatic embedding with a documented receptor-QM definition. The three enzymes do not share a single fixed-fragment computational representation. The original structural-analysis program that produced the historical 4 Å contact subsets C–E was not recovered. Curated subset memberships and scripts reproducing the statistics from those memberships are provided. Additional historical provenance limitations, evidence levels, and relocated source paths are documented in the supplement README and manifests. MD trajectories and bulk simulation outputs are not included. File recovery and integrity checks do not imply that the full historical simulation workflow has been rerun in a fresh environment. Third-party force-field distribution files retain their original attribution and licensing terms.
title: Data for: Assessing the Interpretability of QM/MM Interaction Energies: A Representation-Aware Diagnostic Framework

summary: Simulated OCO-2 soundings and everything needed to reproduce the amortized probabilistic retrieval described in the accompanying paper. Version 3 adds the operational a priori of every reference sounding in February, March and July 2020 (oco2_apriori.tar.gz): the a priori state vector and its covariance, and the a priori XCO 2 and its pressure-weighting function. These are the prior baselines added to the paper in its second revision. Every other archive is unchanged from version 2. Version 2 adds, to the February 2020 delivery already in version 1: the reference-disjoint, within-reference, all-February and training-size split tables, each with the standardization constants estimated from its own training partition (oco2_splits.tar.gz); the trained checkpoints of all six models on each of the three splits reported in the paper (oco2_model_weights_v2.tar.gz); the two held-out months, March and July 2020, as the archives the scoring jobs consumed — spectra, ACOS profile covariances, covariates and the month split table (oco2_month_202003_full.tar.gz, oco2_month_202007_full.tar.gz); and the per-sounding predictive artifacts from which every table and figure in the paper is regenerated without a GPU (oco2_scoring_artifacts.tar.gz). Version 1's archives are included unchanged. oco2_model_weights.tar.gz is the original submission's checkpoints, kept for provenance and superseded by the _v2 archive. The paper's numbers come from the reference-disjoint split table group_split_v1_cov.csv and the _v2 weights. CONTENTS.md describes each archive and SHA256SUMS.txt covers all of them. The code that reads them is at https://github.com/acallesalda/oco2-amortized-uq, archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22667577 ; scripts/get_data.sh downloads, verifies and unpacks everything to the paths the code expects. The simulation experiment, its a priori and the operational ACOS L2FP retrievals were produced at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California Institute of Technology.
title: Simulated OCO-2 data, split tables, trained model weights, and predictive artifacts for amortized probabilistic CO2 retrieval

We present DIII-D experiments  validating real-time, ML-enabled controllers in FPP-relevant scenarios under both imposed diagnostic dropouts and real in-shot hardware failures. Conventional equilibrium reconstruction fails when key diagnostics drop out. Our ML-based RTCAKENN recovers plasma profiles under simulated failures of Thomson Scattering (TS), Charge Exchange Recombination (CER), and Motional Stark Effect (MSE) and maintains accuracies above 90%. ECHO, a fault-robust ML controller, coordinates electron cyclotron heating (ECH) by reallocating gyrotron power s and steering across surviving gyrotrons when units fail mid-shot. In a Hybrid scenario with real ECH dropouts, we mitigated heavy-Z impurity accumulation (argon proxy) using core ECH power tracking a real-time ML radiated-power (Bolo-NN) model for pumpout , and Electron Cyclotron Current Drive (ECCD) steering onto the 3/2 tearing mode for MHD amplitude control. Coordinated ML-controlled gyrotron power adjustments (>0.5MW) avoided argon accumulation and MHD-induced confinement collapse. We also accessed Resonant Magnetic Perturbation (RMP) Edge Localized Mode (ELM)-suppressed plasmas at reduced RMP coil current where large sawteeth would otherwise break ELM suppression. The approach was to reduce sawtooth magnitude (and increase frequency) by holding ECCD inside q=1. Control held through the same TS dropouts and ECH failures, with RTCAKENN providing q=1 localization while ECHO maintained aiming. These first-of-a-kind results show integrated ML-enabled fault-tolerant control sustaining FPP-relevant operating points through imposed and unscripted failures, foundational for resilient burning-plasma control.
title: ML-Enabled Fault Resistant Plasma Control on DIII-D

summary: This paper proposes the Zero Principle as a philosophical and ontological framework for understanding transformation, consciousness, experience, dissolution, and the emergence of new possibilities. The central proposition is that Zero (0) should not be understood merely as mathematical nothingness . Within this framework, Zero represents an open conceptual state in which an existing form loses its claim to finality, allowing another possibility, meaning, direction, or form to emerge. The proposed structural cycle is: Form → Dissolution → 0 → Possibility → New Form At the level of human experience, the corresponding process is: Impulse → Witness → Insight → Transformation → New Direction The paper further introduces a Zero-Level Sutra : Word ≠ Truth Word → Sign → Understanding → Beyond Word → 0 The sutra proposes that words, names, colors, forms, and concepts should not automatically be treated as ultimate reality. Different philosophical traditions may use different terms—such as Brahman, Śūnyatā, Nirvāṇa, Neti-Neti, Witness, Silence, Tao, and Fana —but Vedanta 2.0 does not claim that these concepts are identical. Instead, it explores whether they can be comparatively examined at a “zero-level,” where conceptual definitions reach their limits. The paper also examines the relationship between witnessing and transformation, proposing that conscious observation can create a space between stimulus and automatic reaction. The framework is applied metaphorically to failure, loss, death, patience, faith, mystery, natural cycles, renewal, and symbolic interpretations of Diwali. The paper does not present the Zero Principle as an established scientific law. It is presented as an evolving philosophical hypothesis and conceptual framework within the broader Vedanta 2.0 project.   हिंदी यह शोध-पत्र शून्य सिद्धांत (Zero Principle) को transformation, consciousness, experience, dissolution तथा new possibilities के emergence को समझने के लिए एक दार्शनिक और ontological framework के रूप में प्रस्तुत करता है। इसका केंद्रीय प्रस्ताव यह है कि Zero (0) को केवल mathematical nothingness के रूप में नहीं समझना चाहिए । इस framework में Zero ऐसी खुली conceptual अवस्था का प्रतीक है जहाँ कोई existing form अपनी अंतिमता का दावा खो देता है और दूसरी possibility, meaning, direction या form के emergence की संभावना खुलती है। प्रस्तावित संरचनात्मक चक्र है: रूप → विसर्जन → 0 → संभावना → नया रूप मानवीय अनुभव के स्तर पर: आवेग → दृष्टा → अंतर्दृष्टि → रूपांतरण → नई दिशा Paper में एक Zero-Level Sutra भी प्रस्तावित किया गया है: शब्द ≠ सत्य शब्द → संकेत → बोध → शब्दातीत → 0 इस सूत्र का आशय है कि शब्द, नाम, रंग, रूप और अवधारणाएँ स्वयं अंतिम सत्य को सिद्ध नहीं करतीं। विभिन्न दार्शनिक परंपराएँ ब्रह्म, शून्यता, निर्वाण, नेति-नेति, दृष्टा, मौन, ताओ और फ़ना जैसे अलग-अलग शब्दों का प्रयोग करती हैं। Vedanta 2.0 यह दावा नहीं करता कि ये सभी अवधारणाएँ समान हैं; बल्कि यह जाँचता है कि क्या इन्हें एक “zero-level” पर तुलनात्मक रूप से देखा जा सकता है, जहाँ conceptual definitions अपनी सीमा तक पहुँचती हैं। Paper witnessing और transformation के संबंध का भी अध्ययन करता है तथा यह प्रस्तावित करता है कि conscious observation stimulus और automatic reaction के बीच एक space उत्पन्न कर सकती है। यह framework failure, loss, death, patience, faith, mystery, natural cycles, renewal तथा Diwali के symbolic interpretation जैसे विषयों पर भी लागू किया गया है। यह paper Zero Principle को established scientific law के रूप में प्रस्तुत नहीं करता । इसे व्यापक Vedanta 2.0 framework के भीतर एक evolving philosophical hypothesis और conceptual framework के रूप में प्रस्तुत किया गया है।

summary: Complete data workbook, analysis programme, figure scripts and output files for the manuscript on phenylacetylglutamine and beta-adrenergic cyclic nucleotide generation in isolated rat aorta. Thirty Wistar rats (15 healthy, 15 with high-fat-diet/low-dose-streptozotocin type 2 diabetes; 7 males and 8 females per group). The archive contains the nine-sheet data workbook, the analysis programme that reproduces every table, figure and reported number from it, the figure scripts, a numeric audit script, and the complete result files. Both curves of every organ-bath ring are included, so that the fixed-curve-order limitation reported in the manuscript can be verified independently. Files are restricted and available on reasonable request. Version 2.0 (7 November 2026). One correction, affecting free-text annotation only: nineteen cells of the Notes column of sheet 04_OrganBath_Tension read "Data sampled at 40 Hz"; the acquisition rate of the PowerLab 8/35 and LabChart 8 recording was 10 Hz, and those notes now read "Data sampled at 10 Hz", in agreement with the Methods section of the manuscript. The Notes column is free text and is never read by the analysis programme, so no measured value, formula or computed result is affected; every number in the results files is unchanged and the numeric audit still passes 94 of 94.
title: Data and code: phenylacetylglutamine suppresses beta-adrenergic cyclic AMP and cyclic GMP generation in intact rat aorta, in health and in type 2 diabetes
