summary: Background: : Adverse drug reactions (ADRs) are an important concern in clinical practice and can lead to treatment failure, hospitalization and increased healthcare costs. Genetic variations among individuals can influence drug-metabolizing enzymes, transport proteins and drug targets, resulting in differences in drug response and susceptibility to toxicity. Pharmacogenomics (PGx) provides an approach to understanding these genetic differences and supporting personalized drug therapy. Objective: To systematically evaluate the role of pharmacogenomics in predicting and preventing adverse drug reactions, with particular emphasis on clinically relevant gene–drug interactions and pharmacogenomics-guided treatment outcomes. Methods: : A systematic literature review will be conducted using databases including PubMed, Google Scholar, and the Cochrane Library. Relevant studies will be identified using keywords such as pharmacogenomics, pharmacogenetics, adverse drug reactions, genetic polymorphism, drug toxicity and personalized medicine. Studies investigating associations between genetic variations, medication-related adverse reactions and genotype-guided prescribing will be considered. Study selection and reporting will follow PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Expected results: The review is expected to identify clinically important gene–drug associations, evaluate the evidence supporting pharmacogenomics-guided prescribing and examine its potential to reduce medication-related toxicity. It will also explore challenges associated with implementing pharmacogenomic testing in routine clinical practice. Conclusion: : Pharmacogenomics has the potential to improve medication safety by identifying individuals at increased risk of specific adverse drug reactions. Its effective implementation requires reliable genetic testing, clinical interpretation, healthcare professional education and accessible prescribing guidelines.
title: Role of Pharmacogenomics in Predicting and Preventing Adverse Drug Reactions: A Systematic Review of Gene–Drug Interactions and Clinical Outcomes

The protocol (version 1.0) and Amendment A1 were registered on OSF before the search, screening and any access to expression data (https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/GDVJH); Amendments A2 and A3 were registered before data access (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23204360). The archive holds the result tables of the registered analysis (pooled estimates, gates, multiplicity families, per-comparison effect sizes, leave-one-cohort-out, composition sensitivity, alternative arms, gene-level description, per-unit scores, descriptive comparisons), the registered analysis code with its synthetic tests, the data readers and download manifests with the SHA-256 of every input, the read-reprocessing record (nf-core/rnaseq 3.27.0, Salmon, Ensembl 116), the search, screening and extraction records with the author's confirmation and adjudication workbooks, the exposure log of every data access after registration, and the scripts that build the tables, figures and reference table of the accompanying article. Version 2.0 adds the post hoc analyses, which are not registered and not blind and change no registered result: Amendment A4 Part 1 (from the registered result files), Part 2 (programmes, an expression-matched random gene-set null, alternative scores and ranking universes) and the three checks of Amendment A5, each with its code, synthetic tests, outputs, manifest and run record; the record of a post hoc scan of public glycoproteomics data; and the scripts and outputs of the tables and figures of the second version of the article. The scoring code of version 1.0.0 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22884854) is required to rerun the analysis. summary: A sixth-generation (6G) mobile network must share the radio resources of each base station among services with different requirements for delay, throughput, and energy use. Radio access network (RAN) slicing addresses this problem by allocating radio resources among logically separated services, and increasingly autonomous controllers are proposed to manage these allocations. Two proposed enhancements are a learned meta-agent that adjusts the controller’s configuration and a quantum optimizer for difficult discrete allocation decisions. Here we examine when these enhancements add value beyond strong classical controls using SHARP, a safety-preserving multi-cell RAN slicing controller whose per-slot capacity constraint is enforced independently of the added optimization layers. The meta-agent is evaluated against the best static parameter setting and the controller’s built-in adaptation. Its learned policy selects the same value in every observed state, so in deployment it coincides with a fixed setting (V = 3) and does not outperform the best static setting; its role is to locate that setting without a manual sweep. Relative to the default setting inherited from the host study, the located setting improves slot-level power-budget compliance by five to ten percentage points during constrained regimes at a one to two percent goodput cost, while the controller’s Lyapunov virtual queue already provides long-run adaptation of the power constraint. For the discrete allocation problem, plain QAOA does not outperform the classical baselines. The greedy solution remains the fallback when the quantum device does not return within the planning deadline. We therefore formulate a controllerspecific break-even condition relating the expected utility gain, device availability, and quantum-dispatch cost, and derive the corresponding hardware requirements. summary: Higgs-pair production through gluon fusion is sensitive both to the Higgs self-coupling and to additional scalars exchanged in the s channel. We compute gg → hh at leading order in QCD in the CP-conserving two-Higgs-doublet model with Yukawa alignment (A2HDM), keeping the full top-quark mass dependence and every interference term among the box, the light-Higgs triangle and the heavy-scalar triangle. Previous A2HDM studies of heavy scalars decaying to Higgs pairs used the narrow-width approximation. We contrast two benchmark points. When the heavy scalar H decouples from the top-quark loop, the modified couplings of h weaken the destructive box–triangle interference, and the 13 TeV cross section rises to 1.27 times the Standard Model value without any resonance. For m_H = 300 GeV, below the ttbar threshold, the cross section reaches 3.69 times the Standard Model value; interference with the continuum changes the integrated resonant contribution by only about 4%, but turns the parton-level m_hh distribution into a peak–dip structure. The two mechanisms are therefore separated by the shapes of the m_hh and p_T spectra rather than by the rate. Both benchmarks are illustrative and satisfy a simplified set of theoretical and experimental constraints. Code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24029211

summary: Flagship 55/60 Can randomized or justified quasi-experimental intervention isolate the manufacturing effect from cell-lot, material and culture confounding? CAUSAL VERIFICATION AND COUNTERFACTUAL CONTROL IN NANOROBOT-ASSISTED REGENERATIVE MANUFACTURING AT THE LIMIT This 777-page Research Design Working Edition in the STARLI Nano Regenerative Biomanufacturing series investigates intervention-defined causal treatment contrast rather than observational association. Its scientific coupling is causal inference x microscale interventions x biological functional validation. The evidence perimeter is prospective and nonclinical, using closed in-vitro systems, organ-on-chip platforms or authorized ex-vivo material; neither clinical efficacy nor autonomous human intervention is claimed. The falsifiable question is: Can randomized or justified quasi-experimental intervention isolate the manufacturing effect from cell-lot, material and culture confounding? The proposed minimum demonstration is: Randomize tool action within balanced chip batches, retain sham and medium-only controls, and repeat on a second platform. Strong comparators include correlational predictor, nonrandomized matched cohort and randomized sham manipulation. The central competing explanation is shared medium, selection, interference or time-dependent confounding. The noncompensatory stop rule is: negative controls exhibit the claimed effect or modest unmeasured confounding reverses it. Every eligible, stopped, refused and unsuccessful experiment belongs to the full denominator. summary: This repository provides the data, Python scripts, numerical outputs, and reproducibility documentation supporting a methodological investigation of negative multifractal spectrum estimates in stochastic cascades and digital images. The study distinguishes formally negative annealed multifractal spectra, which can arise in stochastic cascade models, from negative finite-resolution estimates that may depend on measurement and preprocessing procedures. The repository includes: 1. Synthetic image datasets generated using hierarchical random maps (HRM), Fourier-based synthesis (FFT), midpoint displacement (MPD), and binary geometric constructions. 2. Numerical experiments investigating uniform background floors, noise, quantization, clipping, scale-window dependence, and grid-phase sensitivity. 3. Analyses of Dirichlet multiplicative cascades, including Genuine, Shuffled, and Decoy controls. 4. Multifractal estimates based on multiplier moments and Chhabra–Jensen procedures, together with whole-image bootstrap uncertainty estimates. 5. Auxiliary experiments concerning finite-ensemble histogram spectra and supersampling. 6. Scripts, CSV result tables, execution logs, and figure-reproduction materials. 7. A manuscript-to-data mapping file (MANUSCRIPT_MAP.csv), documentation, and SHA-256 checksums supporting traceability and integrity verification. The repository documents reproducibility checks, including the comparison of 180 baseline cases and the reproduction of two computational figures. These checks should not be interpreted as independent validation of every numerical experiment or as proof of universal estimator reliability. The results emphasize that formally negative multifractal spectra and negative estimates obtained from finite digital observations have distinct mathematical interpretations. In particular, negative estimated values do not imply negative Hausdorff dimensions. The dataset is independent of any specific journal submission and is intended to support transparent examination, replication, and further methodological research. summary: Dynamic Convex Onion Analysis of Global Armed Violence (1989–2025): C Software, 1,000 Permutation Tests and Cartographic Projection Audit This software and reproducibility package accompanies a computational-geometric investigation of geopolitical centrality based on the Uppsala Conflict Data Program Georeferenced Event Dataset (UCDP GED), version 26.1, covering the period 1989–2025. The study introduces a dynamic application of convex hull peeling (Convex Onion) to the spatial and temporal analysis of global armed violence. The method is grounded in the affine invariance of convex-layer membership and provides a hierarchical representation of spatial depth through successive convex hulls. Unlike conventional measures of centrality based on averages, distances, or event density, this approach examines the innermost geometric structure of the global distribution of recorded conflict locations. The dataset contains 358,130 events with day-level date precision , corresponding to 54,381 distinct geographical locations . The cumulative analysis identifies 1,134 convex layers in the final configuration. Software Components The archive includes four C-based computational components: Dynamic Convex Onion Analysis: Chronological construction and updating of nested convex hulls, enabling the identification and tracking of the innermost geometric core from 1989 to 2025. Monte Carlo Permutation Analysis: A reproducible experiment involving 1,000 random permutations of complete geographical coordinate pairs across fixed chronological event positions, assessing the relationship between historical event ordering and geometric-core trajectories. Interactive Geometric Visualization: Offline visualization of the evolution of the innermost core, including annual configurations and changes in its geographical position. Cartographic Projection Comparison: Comparative analysis of convex-layer structures using planar longitude–latitude coordinates and the nonlinear Mollweide equal-area projection. Principal Findings The 2025 analysis identifies an innermost geometric location in Ethiopia under the original coordinate representation, whereas the Mollweide projection produces a two-location innermost layer in Sudan. The permutation experiment demonstrates that chronological event ordering influences the historical trajectory of the geometric core, although all permutations preserve the same final spatial configuration when the complete set of locations remains unchanged. These findings illustrate the distinction between affine-invariant geometric structure and centrality that depends on nonlinear cartographic representation. Reproducibility and Scientific Scope The package contains the original C source code, Windows executables, execution scripts, input datasets, computational outputs, visualization files, and technical documentation. The archive supports independent inspection, methodological evaluation, replication, and further development of computational-geometric approaches to spatial conflict analysis. The identified geometric core should not be interpreted as the location of maximum conflict intensity, the greatest number of fatalities, or a causal centre of global geopolitical instability. It represents a mathematically defined form of spatial depth whose interpretation depends on the adopted geometrical representation. Associated Research The Cartographic Construction of Geopolitical Centrality: Affine-Invariant Convex Layers and Global Armed Violence, 1989–2025. Data Source Uppsala Conflict Data Program (UCDP), Georeferenced Event Dataset (GED), version 26.1. The UCDP data are attributed to their original providers. Dataset licensing and software provenance are documented separately in the archive.
title: Convex Onion Geopolitical Centrality

summary: The digitalization of banking services in Nigeria has exponentially increased the incidences of electronic fraud (e-fraud) and the regulatory responses thereto, including the freezing of customers' accounts. While banks have a statutory and contractual duty to protect the financial system from fraud under the Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act (BOFIA) 2020, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) Regulatory Framework for Bank Verification Number (BVN), and various anti-money laundering directives, this duty often collides with the customer's constitutional right to property and the contractual duty of a banker to honour its customer's mandate. This article examines the legal basis and extent of a bank's liability for wrongful freezing of a customer's account and for losses arising from e-fraud. It interrogates the tension between a bank's duty of care, duty to obey regulatory directives, and its fiduciary obligations. Using doctrinal and analytical methodologies, the paper reviews some Nigerian case laws as well as CBN's Regulation on Instant Electronic Payments, the Cybercrimes Act 2015 (as amended), and the NDIC framework. The study finds that while banks enjoy qualified immunity when acting pursuant to a valid court order or clear CBN directive, indiscriminate freezing of accounts based on mere suspicion, internal PND (Post No Debit) without due process, or failure to deploy adequate cyber security measures amount to breach of contract and negligence, attracting damages. The paper advocates for a stricter liability regime, statutory timelines for account unfreezing, and mandatory compensation for wrongful freezing.
tags: Bank Liability, Wrongful Account Freezing, E-Fraud, Post No Debit (PND), Banker-Customer Relationship, Due Process, Digital Banking.
title: BANK LIABILITY FOR WRONGFUL ACCOUNT FREEZING AND E-FRAUD: ANY LEGAL REMEDY?

summary: The rational management of water resources and the control of hydroagricultural techniques in the Oued Souf area are complex and crucial to a harmonious and sustainable development. The Oued Souf area is presently facing the problem of upwelling from groundwater, which is harmful to cultures and homes. The problem. Current AI trust mechanisms prove identity and origin, not behaviour: Model signing (OpenSSF Model Signing, led by Google, NVIDIA and HiddenLayer; NVIDIA NGC signed models) proves which file a model is. Attestation and transparency logs (for example Apple Private Cloud Compute) prove which software a server runs. Neither shows what the model actually decides. A model can be fine-tuned, quantised, wrapped in a prompt or proxy layer, or replaced behind the same name or signature, and an AI agent can act on its output before anyone notices. How it works. Fingerprint generation. A compact cryptographic fingerprint of decision behaviour is created without access to source code, model weights or training data. Clean-copy verification on macOS (2026-11-07): the age-corrected package was extracted into an empty local directory, supplied only with the two authorised local cohort inputs, and rerun through scripts 00, 01, 02, 04, 07, 08, 09, 10 (500 simulations for each of 1.20, 1.25 and 1.30), 11 and 12. All hourly and treatment intermediates were re-extracted from source. The comparator reported "11/11 files match." with Python 3.9.6, NumPy 2.0.2, pandas 2.3.3 and matplotlib 3.9.4. The primary interaction was OR 1.14 (95% CI 0.93–1.40), P=0.221. README run commands and REPRODUCTION_LOG.md document the procedure and scope; this analysis rerun is distinct from source reconstruction and does not constitute independent confirmation by the cohort-building author. The deposit remains a draft pending final author approval.

summary: Vacuum is an absolutely static reference system. When light propagates in a vacuum, it moves in an absolutely static reference system. The propagation speed of light in a medium is a constant, which has nothing to do with the motion state of the light source, the observer or the receiver. When light propagates in a medium, it is dragged by the inertia of the medium. While light propagates in a vacuum, the vacuum is absolutely static, which cannot drag the light to move, and the speed, position, and direction of light in a vacuum are fixed. Based on this theory, a light interference experiment can be performed as proof, using a Michelson interferometer. The principle of the experiment is to split the laser into two beams of light at a half-reflecting mirror,one of which passes through a vacuum quartz tube and reaches the Mirror M1,The light reflects back from M1,Passing through a vacuum quartz tube,Project onto the screen through a half mirror; The other beam of light does not pass through the vacuum quartz tube,reaches the Mirror M2,The light reflects back from M2,Project onto the screen through a half mirror.however, both of the beams converge on the screen, forming interference fringes.Because the speed, position, and direction of light in a vacuum are fixed and the absolute motion of the earth will drive the vacuum quartz tube to move,when the absolute direction of the earth's motion and the direction of light propagation are parallel to each other,light will have an extra optical path in the tube; when they are perpendicular to each other, light will not have the extra optical path in the tube, so after the instrument has turned 90 degrees, the interference fringes will move. The key to this experiment is to create a vacuum. The structure of the experiment is simple that I hope someone could make an experimental verification. According to this theory, it can be concluded that the essence of Fizeau experiment , sagnac effect and Hoek experiment is the same. The reverse process of Fizeau experiment is sagnac effect, vice versa. According to this theory, the Fizeau experiment has a calculated result of movement at 0.236 fringes and a measured value at 0.23 fringes; in the case of Ruyong Wang's experiment "Generalized Sagnac Effect", the moving phase difference has a calculated result at 0.000251 and measured value at 0.000246 in the experiment. Obviously, this theory is more consistent with the experimental measurement results and the theoretical explanation is more real and natural. The sagnac effect, Mach-Zehnder interferometer and Michelson interferometer can all be used to conduct experiments based on this principle to verify whether there is an absolutely stationary reference system. Among them, the sagnac effect has the highest accuracy, the Mach-Zehnder interferometer the second and the Michelson interferometer the lowest. If Michelson and Morley had used a 11m-long vacuum quartz tube for the experiment, they might have observed a movement of 0.373 interference fringesand there might have no so-called "dark clouds". This experiment is actually to measure the sagnac effect of the Earth's rotation by using a Michelson interferometer.

summary: Objective. To assess cardiovascular functional reserve in men and identify the major phenotypes of exercise intolerance based on a comprehensive evaluation of clinical and instrumental parameters. Materials and Methods. At the first stage, 400 men without a previously established diagnosis of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) were examined. One hundred participants with relevant symptoms, cardiovascular risk factors, and/or potential indicators of reduced functional reserve were selected for an in-depth assessment. The protocol included clinical evaluation, the six-minute walk test, exercise stress echocardiography, and cardiopulmonary exercise testing when corresponding data were available. Parameters of left ventricular diastolic function and global longitudinal strain, right ventricular function, chronotropic response, and gas exchange were analyzed. Functional stratification was performed according to predefined pathophysiological criteria. Results. Five functional phenotypes were identified: preserved functional reserve (21%), diastolic (17%), impaired right ventricular–pulmonary arterial coupling (15%), chronotropic (14%), and peripheral (33%). The phenotypes differed in exercise tolerance, changes in E/e′, TAPSE/SPAP ratios, heart rate response, and peak oxygen uptake. The lowest Peak VO₂ values were observed in the peripheral phenotype, whereas the most pronounced increase in E/e′ during exercise was observed in the diastolic phenotype. Conclusion. Comprehensive exercise-based assessment makes it possible to characterize the heterogeneity of functional limitations in the examined men and distinguish phenotypes associated with different presumed pathophysiological mechanisms. Further studies are required to establish the diagnostic and prognostic value of the proposed stratification approach.

summary: Biometric authentication has become a primary mechanism for accessing critical systems, from corporate facilities and banking applications to healthcare records and smart home devices. The term bio-key encompas ses both the use of physiological and behavioural traits as authentication keys and the hardware security tokens (FIDO2 keys) that integrate biometric sensors. Despite widespread adoption, there is no formal ontology that in tegrates the full bio-key authentication chain, namely enrollment, biometric capture, template storage, matching, decision, and access grant, with security assurance levels, privacy requirements, and governance mechanisms. This gap produces semantic interoperability failures, inconsistent security assessments, and weak auditability, especially when biometric templates are compromised or when authentication decisions are contested. The critical asymmetry is that biometric traits are irrevocable: unlike passwords, a com promised fingerprint or iris pattern cannot be reissued. Existing ontologies focus on biometric modalities in isolation or on hardware tokens, but none formally models the complete chain as a data governance and privacy problem. This doctoral project proposes two complementary contributions: (i) a formal ontology, built with the OntoView method, that describes bio-key authentication chains, their security levels, privacy constraints, and governance gates, serving as an instrument for interoperability, risk assessment, and regulatory compliance; and (ii) a verification method, based on the on tology, that specifies and evaluates biometric gates and audit requirements, with direct impact on privacy protection and social well-being. For high value targets, the ontology distinguishes single-party authentication from quorum-based authentication (M-of-N), in which M co-present custodians must each authenticate with their own bio-key and the access secret is split among N parties. The ontology and method will be validated by encoding reported cases, by expert evaluation, and by an empirical study on a si mulated multi-modal biometric testbed with scripted spoofing, replay, and collusion scenarios.
title: Ontology for Bio-Key Authentication: Modalities, Security Levels, Privacy, and Governance

summary: Executable analysis pipeline (Jupyter notebook for Kaggle) and complete results for a study on spectroscopic screening of food adulteration with a stated risk of false accusation. Seven chemometric and deep-learning classifiers (PLS-DA, SVM, random forest, ROCKET, 1D-CNN and a multitask 1D-CNN with and without Beer-Lambert mixup) are compared under grouped, repeated cross-validation. Their out-of-fold scores feed three conformal layers: (i) class-conditional (Mondrian) conformal triage into PASS, FLAG and REFER decisions, with an ablation against marginal calibration and an analysis of calibration size and deployment batch shift; (ii) cross-conformal detection of adulterants absent from training (DD-SIMCA, leave-one-adulterant-out, network embeddings) with Benjamini-Hochberg batch screening; and (iii) a leave-level-out audit for level-batch confounding whose threshold is calibrated by a semi-synthetic Beer-Lambert simulation built from real ATR-FTIR spectra. Four public datasets are analysed (NIR hyperspectral imaging of extra-virgin olive oil; ATR-FTIR of turmeric with wheat flour; MIR of strawberry purée; ATR-FTIR of edible oils); they are not redistributed here (see README for sources and licences). The archive contains the notebook with the outputs of the run reported in the article, all result tables (CSV), figures (PNG), a results summary, run logs and environment information.
title: Risk-controlled spectroscopic screening of food adulteration with conformal prediction: code and results

The tradition itself reached for machine images again and again, each fitted to one lesson; computation is this era's addition. summary: A six-gene mineralization-inhibitor score (ENPP1, ANKH, MGP, GGCX, VKORC1, NT5E) in CD90+ dermal fibroblasts reads lower in systemic sclerosis than in controls. The gene set, direction, detection floors and significance threshold were fixed before any expression value was read. In a pre-registered held-out set of 50 donors (25 and 25), the observed difference is -0.2939 at one-sided p = 0.0204. That replication is across platforms within one study (GSE195452), not across studies, and no ambient RNA correction was applied. The score did not replicate in an independent series. In GSE292979, the same frozen genes, direction, floors and threshold were applied under a pre-registration, and a blinded second implementation reproduced every donor score within 1e-6 before the result was unmasked. All four pre-registered contrasts were null (primary -0.0412, one-sided p 0.4955; minimum attainable p 0.0045). The paper offers no explanation for the null and does not claim the effect is absent. The score is a pre-specified composite, not a pathway readout: a leave-one-out shows the signal concentrated in VKORC1, GGCX and NT5E, and the paper makes no mechanistic claim. The osteogenic half of the original hypothesis did not clear its pre-registered detection floor in any dataset examined. This is not a study of calcinosis lesions, not evidence of specificity, and not a mechanism. It is a pre-registered result that held within one study and did not replicate in the one independent series tested, reported with both outcomes.
title: A pre-specified mineralization-inhibitor score separates systemic sclerosis fibroblasts within one study and does not replicate in an independent series

summary: Lectures and practical classes remain the core formats for teaching specialized subjects in medical and dental universities, yet their modernization is often guided by descriptive experience rather than by empirical evidence. This review aimed to synthesize the evidence on the effectiveness of contemporary lecture and practical-class formats and to propose evidence-informed criteria for selecting them in the teaching of specialized subjects. A narrative review of literature indexed in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, ERIC and Google Scholar was performed, prioritizing meta-analyses, systematic reviews and randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Findings were interpreted through constructive alignment, cognitive load theory and Miller's pyramid of clinical competence. Across 225 studies, active learning increased examination performance by 0.47 standard deviations, and students taught by traditional lecturing were 1.5 times more likely to fail. In health professions education, the flipped classroom outperformed traditional teaching (SMD = 0.33); in dental education, problem-based, case-based, team-based and flipped formats together outperformed lecture-based learning (SMD = 0.48; 29 RCTs, 3,502 students). Technology-enhanced simulation was associated with large effects on knowledge and skills (effect sizes 1.09–1.20) compared with no intervention. However, the evidence shows high heterogeneity and focuses mainly on knowledge and learner satisfaction rather than clinical performance. Lectures and practical classes should be designed as a single aligned system in which the teaching format is selected according to the intended learning outcome and level of competence. Locally conducted controlled studies are needed to confirm these effects in medical universities of Uzbekistan.
title: MODERN FORMS OF TEACHING SPECIALIZED SUBJECTS IN MEDICAL AND DENTAL EDUCATION: AN EVIDENCE-BASED NARRATIVE REVIEW OF LECTURES AND PRACTICAL CLASSES

summary: Where is the place of the human being in the physical picture of the world? This question is usually answered from one of two camps: consciousness is a product of the brain and nothing more; or consciousness is immaterial and does not depend on the body. This work takes a different path — forward from the physical foundation, step by step — and looks at where it leads. The foundation is the work “The Birth of Dimensions: A Formal Skeleton” (BD). It contains nothing but a single assumption: everything is a process, an ideal sine wave, and its centre is the observer. Dimensions are born by squaring: first time, then, by iterating the same square, space and mass. Elementary particles turn out to be a resonance of at least three dimensions — time, space and mass. From the same assumption BD obtains the rules of quantum mechanics, the Lorentz transformations and the masses of particles from the speed of light alone. If the foundation is right, its rule should show up everywhere — including in the work of the brain. And it does: the main ranges of brain rhythms approximately form a ladder of squares — 2–3, 4–9, 16–81 Hz — built in the same way as the tower of levels in BD: the width of the levels in logarithms doubles with every step, and the alpha rhythm falls on the boundary between levels. The rhythm bands are blurred, but that is how it should be: the electroencephalogram is a projection of a higher-frequency process onto a single dimension, and within one level the process is smooth. What matters is something else — resonance between frequencies, and in the brain it was measured long ago. This leads to an assumption: the body is a resonator, and since bodies are alike, this answers the question of why different observers see one common world. Consciousness is then built like an elementary particle — as an agreement of three frequencies linked by squares — only on a higher-frequency level. That is why we see its work but cannot weigh it with instruments of our level; and that is why the world is perceived as three-dimensional. The structure is examined: the “I” is the observer; consciousness is time, the “here and now”; the subconscious is space, the “self” and its history; superconsciousness, intuition, is mass, which is born in self-reflection. From this follows an assumption about the meaning of life as the cultivation of intuition. If consciousness is like a particle, the reverse is also true: every particle may contain what we call consciousness. In the calculations of BD the Milky Way is the image of a neutron, and we live inside it; there are neutrons in almost every atom of our body. And the Universe, if it is like a black hole — part of a particle of a larger world — may be an observer. This is a hypothesis, not a proof. At the end there is a list of ways to test it, and what is established is separated from what is assumed. summary: Acute respiratory infections in children comprise etiologically and clinically heterogeneous diseases with overlapping early manifestations, whereas the risk of respiratory failure and other adverse outcomes varies according to age, premorbid conditions, and the causative pathogen. This review aims to analyze current approaches to etiological diagnosis and evidence-based risk factors for severe disease in children. An analytical search covered PubMed/MEDLINE and documents issued by the World Health Organization and the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence for 2015-2026. Priority was given to guidelines, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, diagnostic accuracy studies, and large cohorts. Clinical assessment identifies the anatomical level of respiratory involvement and current severity but cannot reliably establish viral etiology. Nucleic acid amplification remains the most sensitive method for detecting most respiratory viruses. Diagnostic value depends on the timing and quality of specimen collection, panel composition, and clinical context; a positive multiplex result does not establish the causal contribution of every detected agent. Serology has a limited role in an acute episode. Consistently reported baseline risk factors include young age, prematurity, chronic lung disease, hemodynamically significant congenital heart disease, neurological disorders, immunodeficiency or immunosuppressive treatment, and malnutrition. Hypoxemia, apnea, progressive respiratory distress, feeding inability, altered consciousness, and impaired perfusion indicate evolving organ dysfunction and require immediate assessment. Reliable prediction should integrate baseline risk factors with dynamic clinical variables. Any prediction model requires independent validation in the pediatric population for which its use is intended.
title: Acute Respiratory Infections in Children: Current Approaches to Etiological Diagnosis and Prediction of Severe Disease (Literature Review).

F092  Microrobotic Local Collaboration And Global Mission At The Limit — Asks whether agent-to-agent collaboration improves global agreement when robots lack an unmetered global-state feed. Hidden adversarial-neighbor states test dependence on outside tracking; fixed behavior rules with matched energy provide the comparator. F093  Nanorobotic Collective Pheromone Communication At The Limit — Explores prospective chemical-trail or signal-mediated coordination with collision exposure as a primary outcome. Hidden actuator saturation and a matched-actuation single-agent baseline challenge claims that signaling, rather than redundancy or imposed motion, caused the improvement. F094  Microscale Robot Collective Collision Avoidance Control At The Limit — Examines collision-safe motion while monitoring spatial coverage, recovery time and communication burden. A blinded shared-localization bias tests whether apparent avoidance depends on erroneous common position estimates; safety-boundary crossings trigger rejection. F095  Nanorobotic Collective Energy Allocation At The Limit — Tests dynamic allocation of limited energy across agents during dropout and recovery. Hidden agent-loss clusters challenge energy accounting and recovery-time claims against fixed rules with an equal energy budget; persistent unsafe confidence is a stop condition. F096  Microrobotic Distributed Mission Planning At The Limit — Studies task planning without a central controller using communication load, work-per-task and selective abstention as prospective metrics. Hidden network partitions expose plans that depend on unavailable messages, while a matched-actuation single-agent system tests whether coordination adds value. F097  Nanorobotic Collective Localization Uncertainty At The Limit — Tests whether robots can act safely when position confidence is uncertain or neighbors provide deceptive state information. Energy per accepted task, abstention and completion are checked against a full-state centralized benchmark; unrecognized safety-boundary crossings invalidate the claim. F098  Microrobotic Collective Dynamic Topology Control At The Limit — Examines when changing neighbor connections should trigger reconfiguration or justified refusal to proceed

summary: This paper outlines a comparative structural framework for analyzing how judicial rulings from supranational courts (specifically the CJEU under Article 267 TFEU preliminary references and the ECHR) systematically transform domestic policy parameters without explicit legislative mandates.   Adapted specifically to the institutional mechanics of the French legal order, the framework operationalizes four key structural components:   Judicial Displacement (JD): The structural mechanism through which supranational courts assume primary interpretative authority over national policy, constrained in France by Article 55 of the Constitution.   Administrative Gradualism (AG): The incremental realignment of domestic policy through an iterative sequence of secondary executive and regulatory instruments (décrets, arrêtés, circulaires, and administrative guidance) issued by ministries and independent regulatory bodies (e.g., CNIL, ARCOM).   The Mandate Scale (M_0–M_3): A heuristic metric assessing the spectrum of explicit democratic authorization present within electoral manifestos, winning coalitions, or direct referendums regarding supranational constraints.   Four-Step Operational Cycle: A recurring sequence mapping the trajectory from supranational judicial trigger \rightarrow national administrative response (expanding, reclaiming, or accommodating) \rightarrow democratic legitimacy deficits (input, throughput, output) \rightarrow systemic political outcomes (evolutionary pushback via contrôle de conventionnalité or systemic backlash).   The paper includes a comparative matrix contrasting UK statutory mechanism (HRA 1998, Statutory Instruments) against French constitutional pathways (Sarran, Nicolo, Article 38 ordonnances), along with a rigorous methodology defining a "True-Negative Profile" to test boundary conditions against selection bias.  Note on Origin & Systemic Scope: This publication represents an operational draft outline designed to establish baseline terminology, structural mechanics, and theoretical metrics for ongoing comparative legal research.   This work is a direct spin-off and structural adaptation of the foundational framework established in: Davidson, C. K. S., Judicial Displacement and Administrative Gradualism, DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.24023708.    While the original benchmark paper evaluated these dynamics within a dualist, parliamentary context (specifically United Kingdom immigration policy and prisoner voting rights under ECHR jurisprudence), this adaptation recalibrates the core analytical model to the monist-leaning, semi-presidential institutional architecture of the French Fifth Republic under Article 55 of the 1958 French Constitution.    This draft serves as the immediate European adaptation within a broader comparative research agenda, with future planned adaptations extending the framework to examine administrative realignments, executive rule-making, and judicial review dynamics within the United States constitutional framework.

summary: This analysis examines how computational configuration choices shape resource efficiency in confidential genomic collaboration across institutions. A descriptive secondary analysis uses 14 PRINCESS benchmark configurations published in 2017, comprising seven batch sizes evaluated with compression enabled and disabled across three sites. Matched runtime differences, ratios and joint memory comparisons identify configuration tradeoffs. With compression enabled, increasing batch size from 100 to 10,000 variants reduces runtime by 75.49 percent, while expansion to one million variants provides only 0.38 percent further improvement despite requiring 32.69 times as much memory. Without compression, runtime reaches its observed minimum at 8,000 variants and subsequently increases. Compression enabled records longer enclave runtime in every matched pair. These patterns reveal diminishing processing gains and configuration dependent resource tradeoffs, without isolating their underlying mechanisms. The contribution is a comparative interpretation distinguishing faster execution from economical resource use. The findings refine a resource constraint perspective and support joint evaluation of execution time and memory when configuring protected genomic workflows, with numerical recommendations bounded by the observed benchmark environment.
title: BENCHMARKING CONFIDENTIAL GENOMIC COMPUTING EFFICIENCY THROUGH BATCH SIZE, COMPRESSION, AND MEMORY USE ACROSS COLLABORATIVE SITES

summary: This paper proposes Recursive Anticipatory Argumentation-Control Theory (RAACT), an interdisciplinary framework for representing argumentative discourse as a dynamic, par- tially observed, and recursively updated interaction system. Its central mechanism, Recur- sive Anticipatory Argument-Path Interception (RAAPI), combines contextual observation, pragmatic-linguistic encoding, argument reconstruction, opponent-state estimation, proba- bilistic argument-path forecasting, formal refutation verification, anticipatory intervention, and feedback-based model revision. The framework is developed around the Pre-emptive Refutation Fork Case (PRFC), a primary analytical case in which one participant forecasts an opponent's possible argumenta- tive move and presents a logically evaluated counterargument before that move is explicitly advanced. Subsequent responses are classified into continuation, substitution, qualification, forecast challenge, clarification, and novel argumentative pathways. The mathematical specification introduces latent-state models, observation functions, categorical predictive distributions, Bayesian belief updating, intervention-utility functions, estimation errors, and forecast-evaluation metrics. Conditional mathematical propositions identify what can be established under explicit assumptions, while empirical hypotheses dis- tinguish predictive accuracy from intervention effectiveness and strategic response restriction. RAACT is presented as a formal theoretical architecture and a research program, not as an empirically validated universal law. Its principal scientific obligations are to demonstrate incremental predictive value, establish causal effects under an identifiable research design, prove specific mathematical claims under stated assumptions, and identify boundary conditions through counterexamples and independent replication. Keywords: argumentation theory; linguistic pragmatics; anticipatory reasoning; pre-emptive refutation; cybernetics; feedback control; state estimation; Bayesian forecasting; formal logic; strategic discourse; falsifiability.

summary: Two Hamiltonian systems that share almost nothing in their physical origins turn out to behave identically once their local structure near a 2:1 internal resonance is examined. One system models a pair of flexural modes in a micromechanical resonator through coupled Duffing oscillators. The other models the stretch–bend Fermi resonance of a molecule such as carbon dioxide through a Morse oscillator coupled to a harmonic bend. Both possess an elliptic equilibrium, equal Krein signatures, a frequency ratio close to 2:1, and a cubic resonant coupling. These shared features place them in the same resonant normal-form type, a difference resonance that confines energy exchange rather than driving escape. On the conserved polyad fixed by an initial excitation that places nearly all the energy in the higher-frequency mode, the truncated normal form of any such system collapses to a one-degree-of-freedom problem that depends on only two numbers: a scaled detuning and a scaled anharmonic curvature. Consequently the largest fraction of energy that can be transferred to the lower mode is given by a universal curve whose edges are independent of the curvature. All of the necessary invariants are computed directly from each Hamiltonian before any trajectory is integrated. Numerical integration then confirms the predictions. When the curvature is small the systems follow the one-parameter curve; when it is large they follow the two-parameter curve to high accuracy. A beam whose quartic coefficient is deliberately softened until its curvature matches that of the molecular model reproduces the molecular exchange curve directly, even though the remaining normal-form coefficients differ. An ensemble of sixty randomly drawn members of the same type likewise collapses onto the appropriate universal curve. The residual discrepancy grows roughly linearly with excitation amplitude, as expected from the truncation of the normal form. Two controls mark the boundaries of the result. Reversing one Krein signature converts the same frequency window from bounded exchange into unbounded escape. Weak viscous damping reduces the transferred fraction in the manner predicted by a correspondingly damped reduced model. A quantum treatment of the truncated normal form introduces the polyad number as a third invariant; the lowest Fermi dyad therefore follows a distinct quantum curve rather than the classical one. The findings remain local, confined to two-mode models, and classical except where the quantum analogue is stated explicitly. Within those limits they demonstrate that a dimensionless exchange relation established for one physical system can be transferred to an unrelated system once both have been rescaled by invariants computed from their own Hamiltonians.
title: The Beam That Behaves Like a Molecule

summary: This paper develops a scale-spanning account of latent vibration and frequency manifestation within Extended Classical Mechanics (ECM). It examines the relationship between complete latent vibration, the negative and positive displacement domains around the manifestable origin, and the eligibility of positive displacement for progression towards physical manifestation. The development distinguishes the complete latent-vibration interval from the directed displacement associated with manifestation, establishing the proposed Pre-Latent and Pre-Planck threshold relationships in terms of the Planck length. The analysis further develops phase-dependent frequency relations below the Planck threshold and considers the proposed frequency increments associated with the Pre-Latent and Pre-Planck domains. It then presents a state-dependent sequence of energy–frequency transformations across latent, phase, and manifested states, including the reverse progression associated with dissolution. Within this framework, frequency and displacement are treated as related physical parameters whose coefficients depend on the corresponding phase domain. The paper also distinguishes the phase-state potential-energy mass representation from the mass contribution associated with the manifested domain. It formulates the effective-mass relationship and separates this ECM representation from the distinct dark-energy-related mass representation. Taken together, these developments present an integrated theoretical description of latent vibration, manifestation eligibility, threshold transitions, energy–frequency relations, and mass-state transformations within the proposed ECM framework.
title: Complete Latent Vibration and Frequency Manifestation Eligibility in Extended Classical Mechanics

summary: This archive holds the data and code behind the manuscript “Five Inexpensive Checks for Machine-Learned Enzyme Turnover-Number Predictors” by Fatih Aktas and Farida Rahayu. The protocol defines five checks for machine-learned predictors of the enzyme turnover number. They use supplied prediction columns and one measured panel. The five checks are a scale audit, the mutation-response ratio, a kinetics-untrained baseline floor, transfer to external data, and a calibration check. The protocol is applied to six published predictors. The data span 1,571 variants from 130 database-derived campaigns, 23,500 variants from eight deep mutational scans, and two panels of measured turnover numbers. The archive contains the analysis scripts, the JSON output of each script, the extracted datasets, the tables and figures, a README with the execution order, a REPRODUCE guide, and a dated pre-specification note. All kinetic measurements and all model predictions come from the EnzyArena benchmark (Zeng et al., bioRxiv 2026, doi:10.64898/2026.03.29.715152). No new measurements were made. The benchmark release is not redistributed here. Software: Python 3.13, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn, RDKit 2026.9.1, Matplotlib 3.11.
title: Data and code for five checks on machine-learned enzyme kcat predictors

summary: Fuente del Salín (Cantabria, Spain) is one of the few decorated caves where a large assemblage of hand stencils is associated with a Gravettian occupation, including a hearth and evidence of pigment processing. Using a 3D reconstruction of the cave’s Palaeolithic state, GIS-based measurements and multivariate statistics, we analysed the spatial organisation of its 55 hand stencils. All are located near the entrance, in accessible, visible spaces able to accommodate several people, unlike the only other motif, deeper in the cave. The assemblage nonetheless includes distinct spatial groups, compositions and unusual orientations. The hearth could have lit more than half of the hands, and both kernel density analysis and hierarchical clustering single out the group surrounding it. These results strengthen the hypothesis that the hands and the occupation were contemporaneous and, together with Gargas, suggest that hand stencils could be produced in spaces also used for everyday activities.
title: By the Light of the Fire: Characterisation and Spatial Organisation of the Hand Stencils at Fuente del Salín in Relation to their Archaeological Context

summary: This repository contains the analytical datasets, Python scripts, numerical outputs, plots and reproducibility documentation accompanying the manuscript Can strontium isotopes track changing mobility patterns? Evidence from La Tène Central Europe. The repository is intended to support transparent evaluation, replication and further comparative research on Iron Age mobility, life histories and the relationship between human movement and regional geological environments. The repository supports reproduction of the downstream statistical analyses, including: Cemetery-level isotope distributions and local/non-local classifications. Individual-level mobility estimates using two complementary classification rules: Rule A (any sampled tooth potentially non-local) and Rule B (one predefined permanent reference tooth). Mixed-effects logistic models evaluating chronological, demographic and burial material-group associations while accounting for repeated teeth from the same individual. Sensitivity analyses, paired-tooth comparisons and reconstruction of childhood strontium exposure histories. Cross-cemetery isotope comparisons and relationships between lithological diversity and strontium variability at 1, 5, 10 and 20 km spatial scales. Reproducible analytical plots and numerical verification against the published supplementary results.

summary: forelint is an open-source Python library that checks what a forecasting backtest score hides, before anyone acts on it. Leakage between related series: GroupTimeSplit holds out the future of entities the model never saw, and split_optimism reports how much random, group and time-only splits overstate accuracy against it. Run-to-run noise floor: noise_floor measures the spread of repeated runs and the smallest difference that exceeds it. Model comparison across many series: Diebold-Mariano with the Harvey-Leybourne-Newbold correction on long-format panels, and the model confidence set of Hansen, Lunde and Nason (2011). Backtest audit: per-item bias, tracking signal, error concentration, MASE and RMSSE, and forecast value added against a baseline, broken down by demand class (smooth, erratic, intermittent, lumpy), with stockout periods excluded from scoring. On one store of the public M5 data, backtested at ten non-overlapping forecast origins, a gradient-boosting model was 3.9% worse than a 28-day moving average on absolute error and worse on 58% of items. By demand class it added +5.0% on smooth items and lost −10.5% on intermittent and −9.2% on lumpy ones. Source: github.com/davidmashiah/forelint . Author: David Mashiah .
title: forelint: lint your forecast backtests before you trust a score

Shannon's bound makes the variance the currency of the problem: the smooth count of the primes is a first moment, a first moment holds no distribution, and so any statement about the size of the prime fluctuation is a statement about a discarded second moment, which for the primes is the set of zeros of the zeta function. The step is the one Perelman took for Ricci flow; he established the invariant, and here its cause is given: unitarity. The quantum connection is the reason a lock exists in the first place. The prime fluctuation is a state acted on by the matrix M(t) = diag(e^(δ_n t)  e^(iγ_n t)); the variance is its norm, and it is conserved, with a fixed share for every mode, only when M is unitary, that is, when every zero carries the weight ½ , the single fixed point of the two fold symmetry of the functional equation. The Riemann hypothesis is then the statement that the prime fluctuation is a closed quantum system. We measure the second moment directly on 100,000 zeros and on 10,000 zeros each near zero number 10^12, 10^21 and 10^22. Six results follow. With every zero carrying the same weight, the variance of the scaled prime fluctuation is the same in every window of log x: 0.0460 with a spread of 0.0010 over eight windows up to log x = 30, against the closed form 0.0462. A single mode moved off the line by δ grows in variance as x^(2δ). The measured growth factors agree with e^(6δ) per window to within half a percent. The zeros interfere to produce the primes. At the 25 prime powers up to 60 the measured spike is 0.9995 of the predicted height with a scatter of 0.0006, and the smallest spike is 208 times the largest value at any other integer. The zeros are stiff. Neighbours closer than a tenth of the mean spacing occur 120 times less often than without stiffness, the power of the complex amplitude in reciprocal space follows the unitary ramp, and the count variance saturates at a level fixed by the primes: 0.36 at height 4 × 10^4 and 0.52 near 10^21, as predicted. The primes hold each zero in a harmonic well. The measured stiffness agrees with K = (2/|ρ|^2 )⟨(log x)^2⟩ to within one percent for the low zeros. One ancilla qubit, read in X and Y, returns both the primes and the ramp from a register that holds the zeros with equal weight. Forcing one mode off the line is not unitary, and the entropy over modes collapses from log N toward zero. The restoring force acts on the position of each zero. The stiffness between neighbours is a two point property, carried by the square of the prime sum and not by its linear response: that sum, with no zero in it, rebuilds the ramp of the first 100,000 zeros to within 0.006, including their position under the unitary ramp. By sieve to x=10^9 the true primes hold one variance at every scale, 0.0461, where random primes are 338 times louder and growing, and the Möbius sum holds 0.0289 where random signs give 0.61. summary: Delay-Doppler (DD) modulations, such as Zak-transform-based orthogonal time frequency space (Zak-OTFS) modulation, represent the channel as a sparse set of delay and Doppler shifts, which makes them well suited for radar sensing. Sensing with a single DD frame, however, is unambiguous only when the channel spread factor, i.e., the product of the delay and Doppler spreads, is less then one. Long-range mobility scenarios, including drones, airplanes, low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites, and underwater acoustic links, typically violate this crystallization condition, so that a single frame aliases the target delays, Doppler shifts, or both. Existing methods add a time-frequency pilot to a conventional DD frame, resolve the aliasing in only one dimension, and assume integer delays and Doppler shifts. We propose a frame design that combines multiple DD bases with different delay and Doppler periods, which together cover an overspread channel with fractional delays and Doppler shifts, using the same bandwidth and frame size. We show that modular arithmetic on the peak positions uniquely recovers each target by pairing the peaks through their common projection and their gains, and we derive the condition under which this pairing is ambiguous. We implement the design with two superimposed Zak-OTFS frames and propose two receivers: dual-frame sensing (DS), which performs the joint detection directly, and DS with cross-pilot cancellation (DS-XC), which additionally cancels the cross-pilot interference, re-estimates the gains by joint least squares, and removes ghost targets. Both receivers maintain a detection rate close to one as the spread factor grows, and DS-XC also achieves the lowest false-alarm rate and channel estimation error among all the compared systems. In a 100 km drone scenario, DS-XC outperforms all baselines, with a complexity that grows near-linearly with the time-bandwidth product.
title: Sensing Fast and Distant Targets in Fractional Overspread Channels with Zak-OTFS and Modular Arithmetic

summary: The scarcity of labeled underwater acoustic data limits the development of data-driven models for marine acoustic monitoring, motivating the use of self-supervised learning to exploit the abundance of unlabeled recordings. However, large-scale data alone does not guarantee effective representation learning, because model performance is strongly influenced by the distribution of the training data. To facilitate such training data, this study introduces a scalable curation pipeline that curates 3,000 hours from 41 years of raw NOAA hydrophone recordings, producing MarineSet, a large-scale and diverse dataset designed for underwater acoustic learning. A baseline model, MarineNet, trained on MarineSet achieves competitive performance on marine mammal call and ship-type classification, highlighting the value of systematic data curation for developing self-supervised learning models in underwater acoustics.
title: MarineSet: Large-Scale Underwater Acoustic Data Curation and evaluation

summary: The transmission of shock waves generated by underwater electrical foil explosions across solid materials with varying acoustic impedances and thicknesses is investigated. Copper foils with thicknesses of 10 and 18 $μ$m are exploded on planar substrates of aluminum, copper, and 3D-printed PLA with thicknesses up to 5 mm using a multi-gigawatt pulsed-power electrical discharge. The resulting shocks are visualized in water using high-speed shadowgraphy at 5 million frames per second, while high-resolution fiber optic hydrophone measurements provide direct quantitative measurements of shock strength after transmission through the impedance-mismatched materials. One-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic simulations are used to reproduce the foil explosion dynamics and provide insight into the thermodynamic, acoustic, and electrical properties of the foil during the explosion. The results show that shock transmission is governed not only by the impedance mismatch at the solid--water interface but also by the finite thickness and dynamic response of the supporting material. These findings provide a quantitative framework for understanding and controlling shock transmission in underwater electrical foil explosions and establish the feasibility and limitations of using solid substrates as structural supports in complex shock-generating geometries.
title: Shock wave transmission across solid-water interfaces in underwater electrical foil explosions

summary: This dataset provides the numerical inputs, source code, reference results, and reproduction workflow accompanying “Light in Light Bubbles — Gravitational Light in the Phraqtal Field” ( https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23652779 ). Version 2.0 preserves the numerical baseline of version 0.2: stationary-core calculations, regime-channel coupling, integrated gravitational-source calculations, static three-knot comparisons, constrained-curvature diagnostics, and analytical examples for tension-front energy, arrival geometry, and conditional golden-ratio relations. Original numerical programs, input fields, parameters, dependencies, and comparison tolerances remain unchanged. The historical Google Colab replay of October 27, 2026, passed 11 comparison groups and 3,055 checks within the declared tolerances. Its verification records are retained as historical evidence, not presented as a newly executed version-2.0 numerical replay. The extension adds the complete expanded German manuscript and 110 finite exact algebraic controls for magnetic twist organization, the constitutive magnetization readout, source variations, and a conditional magnetic–gravitational response. These controls distinguish directed organization from quadratic source contributions and retain the direct source term in the response calculation. No new core, regime-chain, numerical field-response, or physical-time field-evolution calculations were performed for this extension. The magnetic readout remains an explicit constitutive model choice; its physical calibration and validation against measurements remain open. The algebraic controls do not establish a measured magnetic response or derive the numerical value of Newton’s gravitational constant. The single-cell Colab notebook defaults to integrity checks and the new algebraic extension. Replaying the historical numerical calculations is optional. Release instructions and the new executable interface are in English. The expanded manuscript is in German; the original English manuscript is also retained. The package includes checksums, claim-to-material mappings, and separate historical and extension verification records.

summary: This dataset provides the numerical inputs, source code, reference results, and reproduction workflow accompanying “Light in Light Bubbles — Gravitational Light in the Phraqtal Field” ( https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23652779 ). Version 2.0 preserves the numerical baseline of version 0.2: stationary-core calculations, regime-channel coupling, integrated gravitational-source calculations, static three-knot comparisons, constrained-curvature diagnostics, and analytical examples for tension-front energy, arrival geometry, and conditional golden-ratio relations. Original numerical programs, input fields, parameters, dependencies, and comparison tolerances remain unchanged. The historical Google Colab replay of October 27, 2026, passed 11 comparison groups and 3,055 checks within the declared tolerances. Its verification records are retained as historical evidence, not presented as a newly executed version-2.0 numerical replay. The extension adds the complete expanded German manuscript and 110 finite exact algebraic controls for magnetic twist organization, the constitutive magnetization readout, source variations, and a conditional magnetic–gravitational response. These controls distinguish directed organization from quadratic source contributions and retain the direct source term in the response calculation. No new core, regime-chain, numerical field-response, or physical-time field-evolution calculations were performed for this extension. The magnetic readout remains an explicit constitutive model choice; its physical calibration and validation against measurements remain open. The algebraic controls do not establish a measured magnetic response or derive the numerical value of Newton’s gravitational constant. The single-cell Colab notebook defaults to integrity checks and the new algebraic extension. Replaying the historical numerical calculations is optional. Release instructions and the new executable interface are in English. The expanded manuscript is in German; the original English manuscript is also retained. The package includes checksums, claim-to-material mappings, and separate historical and extension verification records.

summary: When a phone fails and its owner keeps the messaging account running on a second device, the account's history can end up in two archives, each intact and each missing what the other holds. We call this Temporal Communication Fragmentation (TCF), a loss by non-union: no message is deleted, but the platform offers no operation that joins the two halves. WhatsApp's own documentation states that old and new chats cannot be merged. We define TCF by three jointly necessary and sufficient conditions and specify CARTA 1.1, a framework for reconstructing one archive from several. CARTA is an output contract owed to a reader who cannot check the result. Records that cannot be read unambiguously are quarantined with a typed reason, and a report gives each record's provenance, the conflicts and deduplication ambiguities found, and every setting used. We evaluated a reference implementation, CHAMP-Pipeline, on synthetic fragment sets with known ground truth. With its declared date inference it reproduced the ground truth in all 4,500 configurations of a parameter sweep; the invariants and the predicted outcome held in all 5,000 random configurations of two to four fragments; and reconstruction stayed exact at one million messages. A zone-offset advisory, frozen before testing, flagged all 2,800 misdeclared zones in a designed test of overlapping fragment pairs and 1,470 of 1,542 in random configurations, and raised false alarms in 2 of 600 correctly declared runs. A systematic search found 60 chat-merging tools; none fully provides more than 2 of the five output properties CARTA specifies. With a fragment's time zone left undeclared, every benchmarked tool and CHAMP-Pipeline produce the same duplicated and misdated records, and only CHAMP-Pipeline's report says so. All data are synthetic; no real archive has been reconstructed.
title: When Chats Split Apart: Formalizing Temporal Communication Fragmentation and the CARTA Reconstruction Framework

summary: Code, input-distribution parameters, and all Monte Carlo and sensitivity outputs for the manuscript "A multilayer probabilistic influence model of train driver human error probability and system-level failure probability: Monte Carlo simulation and input-factor sensitivity analysis" (submitted to Reliability Engineering & System Safety). The package reproduces every table and figure of the paper. It contains the 17 input distributions of Table 1 (params/inputs.yaml), the link coefficients of Eqs. (3)-(13) (params/links.yaml), the point values of the three deterministic case studies (params/cases.yaml), the model itself (src/model.py), and the scripts for the Latin hypercube Monte Carlo simulation (300,000 iterations, fixed seed), the one-at-a-time and Sobol' sensitivity analyses, the threshold analysis, and the parametric interval analysis. Version 1.1 adds the analyses of the revised manuscript: the decomposition of the mean output, the convergence and bootstrap intervals of the Sobol' indices, the scenario analysis of the structural estimates, a simplified barrier layer (params/comparison.yaml), and a comparison with 27 events from published investigation reports (params/incident_cases.yaml). Running src/run_all.py regenerates all outputs in under two minutes; tests/test_cases.py and tests/test_tables.py check the results against the values reported in the manuscript. Every parameter is traceable to a published open statistic or a literature effect coefficient, listed with its source and access date in data/sources.csv. Code is released under the MIT License; data and outputs under CC BY 4.0. Funding: National Research Foundation of Korea, funded by the Korean government (MSIT), RS-2026-25474388; Korea Institute of Energy Technology Evaluation and Planning (KETEP) and the Ministry of Climate, Energy, Environment (MCEE) of the Republic of Korea, RS-2025-07852969.

summary: We propose the interrogative investment hypothesis: the basic interrogative forms can serve as units for describing how individuals come to differ in cognitive competence. These forms fall into two levels. Questions of object (what, where, who, when, how many) carve reality into aspects; questions of reason (how, why) relate these aspects and underlie methods of inquiry such as the historical and scientific methods. Gardner's theory of multiple intelligences offers a rich description of these differences; we propose a complementary developmental mechanism that may help explain how its profiles take shape. In line with Hayes's (1962) motivational-experiential theory of intelligence, we suggest that its domains are strengthened, at least in part, through investment. A spontaneous preference for one kind of question draws attention and time toward it; because time is scarce, this produces cumulative practice, growing competence and increasing reward, which strengthens the preference in turn. We discuss where such preferences may come from: inherited dispositions, early ability, the answers children receive, and culture. Hayes's experience-producing drives were never operationalised; we suggest that question preferences could provide one possible behavioural indicator of them. We propose a simple task to capture these preferences, a pilot study with explicit criteria for failure, and five testable predictions. Finally, we draw implications for education: questions show where a child's attention goes before competence is visible, one object can be taught through many questions, and the way adults answer may shape which questions grow. The proposal is theoretical; no data have been collected.   Version 5. Adds a section on the origins of question preferences with a fifth prediction, a pilot study with criteria for failure, and a section on implications for education.

summary: Claims about acoustic keystroke side channels, attacks that infer typed content from the sound of a keyboard, are difficult to compare because studies differ in recording conditions, data splits, and how defenses are tested. This paper presents OpenKeystroke, an open source research platform for authorized acoustic side-channel experiments and privacy-defense evaluation. The platform measures how much class information survives in short acoustic transients, and how much signal transformations (defenses) reduce it, under a strict evaluation protocol: session, device, and environment-disjoint splits with leakage checks, train-only fitting of preprocessing statistics, validation-only model selection, cluster-bootstrap confidence intervals, and paired comparisons across repeated seeds. Defenses are labelled effective only when they produce a significant accuracy drop, over at least three seeds, against both a static attacker and an adaptive attacker who knows the defense is applied. The platform ships eight classification models and six defenses behind one experiment lifecycle shared by a command line interface, a Python API, and an interactive dashboard. On a synthetic benchmark, headline accuracy degrades materially under domain shift, and several defenses that appear strong against a static attacker largely fail against an adaptive one, which is exactly the gap the platform exists to expose. OpenKeystroke operates only on predefined, non-sensitive acoustic categories in controlled or explicitly consented data. It does not reconstruct typed text, passwords, or messages.
title: OpenKeystroke: An Open Research Platform for Acoustic Side-Channel Experiments and Privacy-Defense Evaluation

summary: The triangular Lagrange point of the restricted three-body problem and the radial motion of a charged particle in a Penning trap are both equilibria held at a maximum of an effective potential by a gyroscopic force. Each possesses one mode of negative energy, and each loses linear stability when its two frequencies collide—one at Routh’s mass ratio, the other at the trapping limit. Both systems belong to a single family of planar gyroscopic Hamiltonians. On every level of the conserved angular-momentum invariant, the degree-four normal form of any member at such a collision coincides with the reduced Hamiltonian of an axisymmetric Penning trap whose detuning is shifted by a term proportional to the invariant and whose quartic coefficient is fixed by a single normal-form invariant. On the level containing orbits that start at rest, this reduction yields closed-form laws for the largest excursion, the escape threshold, and the escape time. These laws depend only on the sign of the quartic coefficient and on scaled variables. At the triangular point the coefficient is positive, placing the collision in the soft class: orbits remain confined after stability is lost, with an excursion that grows like the square root of the distance past the critical value. Direct integration confirms the soft law to a fraction of a percent at the smallest detunings tested. Two traps whose quartic coefficient matches that of the triangular point reproduce the same law. Traps with the opposite sign escape at the predicted threshold and in the predicted times. A randomized ensemble of members confirms the classification by the sign of the coefficient. Two further results hold for every member of the family. Before the collision the linear transient gain is exactly the inverse square root of the frequency splitting. With isotropic velocity damping the first-order growth rates depend only on the undamped frequencies, and at the collision they scale with the square root of the damping rate. The first of these explains earlier reports of apparent escape just below Routh’s value as ordinary linear transients that reach a fixed radius. The second recovers the classical magnetron-instability formula as a special case. The results are local, planar, and classical. What transfers between the asteroid and the trap is the normal-form dynamics on each level of the invariant, the transient gain, and the damped linear rates. What does not transfer without further work is the behaviour beyond the normal-form neighbourhood, where the gravitational terms of every order cause the triangular point to deviate from any purely quartic trap.
title: An Asteroid in a Penning Trap

These counts describe the publication structure, not validated scientific novelty. A companion publication ZIP includes the ten original PDFs and ten per-book Zenodo introductions. The Ten Research Directions F131  AI-Driven Microfluidic Sampling Strategy Optimization At The Limit — Examines recoverable analyte as a fraction of input under fixed sampling resources. Expert tuning with equal trials is the comparator; hidden human intervention is the rival. Blind recovery audits and out-of-distribution refusal test whether AI planning adds genuine value. F132  Nano-Quantum System Counterfactual Inference At The Limit — Tests held-out, intervention-specific counterfactual prediction error while retaining constraint-violation safeguards. Frozen open-loop policies anchor comparison; training-test leakage and nonreplayable observation-to-action chains can invalidate apparent autonomy. F133  AI-Driven Microrobotic Autonomous Calibration At The Limit — Uses blind-standard calibration bias after autonomous correction as a physical measurement target. Preregistered experimental design is the baseline. Extra experimental trials and any action outside the authority envelope defeat a claimed improvement. F134  Microscale Physical Model and Neural Network Coupling At The Limit — Challenges coupled learning and physical models against independently measured conservation residuals under withheld shifts. Matched expert tuning and hidden manual intervention are alternative explanations; unsafe confidence outside the tested domain is a stop condition. F135  AI-Driven Nanoscale Sampling Failure Prediction At The Limit — Proposes prospective fault warning lead time, in seconds, at a fixed false-alarm rate. Frozen open-loop policies and unselected failure cases distinguish early warning from hindsight leakage. Recovery outcomes and complete action replay remain necessary. F136  Quantum Sensor Interpretable AI At The Limit — Asks whether AI explanations agree with mechanism-specific physical ablations, rather than merely producing plausible narratives. The proposed witness is an agreement fraction, with counterfactual error and calibrated sensing as safeguards. More experimental trials are a competing account. F137  Microrobotic Closed-Loop Control Latency At The Limit — Measures the full sensor-to-physical-action delay, in seconds, inside a declared operating envelope. Expert-tuned controls under matched resources establish the comparison. Hidden human intervention and high-confidence out-of-domain action must be ruled out. F138  AI Multi-Agent Sampling Mission Coordination At The Limit — Evaluates calibration-adjusted joint sampling mission completion as a fraction under fairness and safety vetoes. Frozen open-loop coordination and identical observation
