summary: This analysis examines how aggregation and evidence composition shape international comparisons of reported antimalarial treatment failure. Using 244 World Health Organization summaries from 69 countries and territories covering 2010 to 2019, descriptive comparisons assess treatment regimens, parasite species and geographical settings, supplemented by exploratory sample restrictions. The mean reported failure median was 1.87 percent, while 62.30 percent of summaries had zero medians. However, 33.55 percent of zero median summaries contained positive failure maxima, revealing heterogeneity concealed by central values. The ordering of two commonly used regimens reversed across seven country pairs aligned by species, follow up duration and reported study interval bounds. Regional differences persisted within a shared species and treatment category, although means and medians produced different geographical orderings. Restricting observations to summaries representing multiple studies reduced dispersion while preserving a zero median. These findings refine surveillance interpretation by distinguishing favourable central performance from consistency across contributing evidence. International reporting should present distributions, study coverage and comparable analytical groups together to support targeted investigation of elevated failure observations.
title: ASSESSING ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN ANTIMALARIAL TREATMENT REGIMENS, PARASITE SPECIES, REGIONAL SETTINGS, AND REPORTED MEDIAN TREATMENT FAILURE

summary: This analysis examines whether national submarine cable provision distinguishes retained international connectivity under infrastructure disruption. Using a 2021 topology snapshot covering 173 countries and territories, 294 international cable systems and 1,262 landing records, it combines bipartite network modelling with exhaustive single cable removal and descriptive comparisons. Mean retention was 99.5917% among units with one cable and 99.9286% among those with two, while all units with at least three shared the same score. Landing diversity provided no consistent additional ordering within comparable redundancy categories. Only 21 of 294 removals fragmented connectivity, and five scenarios accounted for 48.17% of cumulative country pair losses. Shared connecting routes explain how multiple national connections can coexist with dependence on distant infrastructure. Geographical groups differed more in infrastructure provision than in retention. The contribution is a linked assessment of national protection and concentrated network consequences, refining interpretations that equate infrastructure quantity with functional independence. The evidence supports evaluating alternative connections against shared dependencies and reporting critical failure scenarios alongside average resilience scores.
title: ASSESSING GLOBAL INTERNET INFRASTRUCTURE RESILIENCE THROUGH SUBMARINE CABLE NETWORK TOPOLOGY AND SIMULATED FAILURES

summary: ABSTRACT Aim: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of intra-operative frozen section (FS) in the management of abdominal masses and to identify specific technical and interpretive pitfalls that lead to diagnostic discordance. Materials and Methods : This prospective study analyzed 50 cases of abdominal masses at a tertiary care hospital over a two-year period. Intra-operative samples were processed using a cryostat at -20°C to -25°C, stained with Hematoxylin and Eosin, and reported within 30–45 minutes. The FS diagnoses were categorized as benign, malignant, or suspicious and subsequently compared with the gold standard paraffin-embedded sections (PS). Statistical parameters, including sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values, were calculated. Results: Of the 50 cases, 29 (58%) were malignant and 21 (42%) were benign. The gallbladder was the most frequent site of involvement (40%), followed by ovarian and gastrointestinal lesions. FS demonstrated an overall diagnostic accuracy of 98%, with a sensitivity of 96.5% and a specificity of 100% for the detection of malignancy. One case of discordance was noted in a large, multi-loculated ovarian tumor, where a focal borderline component was under-diagnosed as benign on FS due to sampling limitations. The positive predictive value was 100%, and the negative predictive value was 95.4%. Conclusion : Intra-operative frozen section is a highly reliable diagnostic modality for abdominal masses, providing rapid and actionable results that directly influence surgical strategy. While it is nearly infallible for most solid malignancies, cautious interpretation and extensive sampling are required for complex cystic ovarian lesions to minimize the risk of underdiagnosis.   Keywords: Frozen section, intraoperative diagnosis, diagnostic accuracy, abdominal masses, histopathology
title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Intra-operative Frozen Section in Abdominal Masses: A Prospective Study from a Tertiary Care Hospital

summary: This dataset provides the frozen derived bibliographic data, executable analysis code, verification tests, annual results and figures supporting a measurement audit of historical crossover claims in molecular-marker research (1960–2025). It integrates 155,834 eligible work–marker associations, 33 related baseline and exact single-label-omission annual series, and the descriptive finite-panel critical margin frontier F(t). The annual minimum identifies the limiting specification and its year-specific eligible-work population; it is not a trajectory from one unchanged cohort. The package reproduces downstream analyses from frozen eligible records, including baseline persistence, SNP-removal sensitivity, full one-label-omission audits, reported marginal thresholds and Figures 1–3 and S1. It provides offline verification, file-level SHA-256 checksums, data documentation and source-archive provenance digests. The original full OpenAlex retrieval and historical v5 classifier configuration, independently adjudicated method-use labels and the earlier baseline v1.0.0 archive are not included. Accordingly, the results are conditional on archived classification decisions and do not establish validated dates of laboratory-method adoption, sampling confidence intervals or the performance of a reader-facing reporting intervention.

summary: This analysis examines how adaptive computation configurations relate to classification accuracy in language models, informing international debates on computational efficiency. A descriptive reanalysis uses 20 published configuration results from Chinese Book review and English Yelp.P benchmarks reported in 2020, comparing routing arrangements, exit thresholds, and matched distillation settings. Adaptive routing exceeds selected fixed depth alternatives by 0.56 to 2.81 percentage points, with fewer operations in all three computationally usable comparisons. Raising exit thresholds reduces accuracy across both benchmarks, while endpoint computational reductions range from 62.77 to 77.87 percent among usable comparisons. Self-distillation improves accuracy in all four matched pairs, averaging 0.478 percentage points, with larger advantages for Book review. Accuracy losses concentrate differently across threshold intervals, indicating benchmark dependent stopping costs. These descriptive patterns distinguish selective processing, prediction acceptance, and intermediate supervision as complementary configuration decisions. The contribution refines the resource allocation perspective through transparent comparisons of existing evidence. Deployment teams should evaluate threshold intervals separately and compare accuracy alongside verified computational requirements within each intended task.
title: ADAPTIVE INFERENCE THRESHOLDS AND SELF-DISTILLATION SHAPE CLASSIFICATION ACCURACY ACROSS COMPUTATIONALLY CONSTRAINED LANGUAGE MODEL BENCHMARKS

summary: This analysis examines whether privacy vulnerability rankings remain consistent across text reconstruction procedures, informing international debates on federated learning security. A descriptive secondary analysis uses 72 published benchmark conditions from 2024, covering three attacks, two transformer configurations, three text benchmarks and four batch sizes. Matched comparisons hold the remaining experimental dimensions constant. DAGER exceeds TAG and LAMP in all 24 matched conditions, with average advantages of 61.62 and 49.79 ROUGE 1 score points, respectively. LAMP exceeds TAG in 23 conditions. Increasing batch size from one to eight coincides with lower reconstruction throughout the TAG and LAMP comparisons, whereas DAGER retains ceiling performance on GPT 2 and deteriorates on BERT. Model rankings consequently reverse across attacks. These patterns indicate that aggregation constrains recoverability conditionally rather than providing uniform protection. The contribution is a comparative synthesis showing that observed vulnerability depends on reconstruction capability and model configuration, without establishing causal mechanisms. Organizations should evaluate multiple attacks under matched conditions and distinguish unigram recovery from comprehensive disclosure when interpreting privacy claims.
title: GRADIENT EXPOSURE CONDITIONS AND TEXT RECONSTRUCTION VULNERABILITY IN FEDERATED FOUNDATION MODELS ACROSS PUBLISHED BENCHMARK EXPERIMENTS

summary: Decentralised peacebuilding councils are widely promoted as a means of rebuilding citizen trust in post-conflict states, yet the evidence base for their effectiveness rests largely on observational comparisons that cannot separate the councils' effects from the selection of communities into them. Using a before-after-control-impact estimator under a declared variance structure with an intraclass correlation of 0.64, a between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0 and a residual standard deviation of 4.5, the analysis estimates power across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The design achieves 80 per cent power to detect a 5 percentage point effect at 56 clusters, a requirement that exceeds the number of municipal units typically available in a single Ivorian region. The regression-discontinuity approach is defensible in principle but fragile in practice, and that its value lies less in producing a definitive estimate than in disciplining claims about what decentralised peacebuilding can plausibly achieve.
tags: decentralised peacebuilding; citizen trust; regression discontinuity; Côte d'Ivoire; before-after-control-impact; statistical power; municipal governance; post-conflict reconstruction
title: Decentralized peacebuilding councils and citizen trust in Côte d'Ivoire: a regression-discontinuity design at municipal budget thresholds

summary: Complete research archive for the study of natural-product label errors in ChEMBL CYP inhibition data: the input extract, the curation files, every intermediate result, and the analysis scripts that produced the figures and tables in the article and its supporting information. The study examines a natural-product flag inherited from COCONUT through ChEMBL, across 14,598 compound-isoform IC50 pairs for 9,347 compounds. Of 500 compounds carrying the flag, 138 (27.6%) were excluded by a criterion combining absent provenance in LOTUS with a synthetic structural signature, together with review of the compounds that criterion retained. The excluded compounds were disproportionately potent inhibitors, and the association survives adjustment for molecular size, testing intensity, aromatic ring count and an independent natural-product-likeness score for the compounds identified individually from structure. Version 1.2.0 adds the material prepared for the first revision. The curation criterion is now validated in both directions against external standards. Against the Natural Products Atlas (version 2024_09), 36,453 compounds curated by hand from the primary isolation literature and independent of both resources the criterion uses, the full rule removes 262: a false-positive rate of 0.72% (95% CI 0.64-0.81%). In a random sample of 50 of the 362 retained compounds, classified independently by two of the authors, 20 are fully synthetic: a false-negative rate of 40% (95% CI 28-54%), with inter-rater agreement of Cohen's kappa 0.83 (0.69-0.96) over four origin classes and 0.92 (0.79-1.00) on the binary question. Because the two rates differ by roughly fifty-fold, the 27.6% is a floor on the mislabeling rate in this dataset rather than an estimate of it. This version also adds a twenty-four-setting sensitivity sweep of the criterion, calibration of the predicted probabilities against the training base rate, the per-isoform decomposition of the curation effect into removal and retraining, the potency association under four compound-level aggregations, and a covariate for how often each compound has been studied. Contents   01_input      the activity extract, with assay and document identifiers   02_curation   the curation files, including the exclusion list   03_results    the results, with the revision outputs in a dated subfolder   04_scripts    the analysis scripts, with the revision scripts in a dated                 subfolder   05_audit      the two-rater origin audit behind Table S17   06_external_tools  the ADMETlab 3.0 and pkCSM reports for the three compounds                 in Table 4 Source data are from ChEMBL 37 (doi:10.6019/CHEMBL.database.37). Two third-party datasets used by the analysis are not redistributed here, each being available from its own archive: the LOTUS frozen dataset used for provenance cross-referencing (doi:10.5281/zenodo.19360665, v11), and the Natural Products Atlas release used for the specificity test added in this version (version 2024_09, 36,453 compounds, MD5 10fd08163f5cda420e104dc21246db4f, from https://www.npatlas.org/download). The revision README records the version and checksum so that a reader can download the Atlas file and confirm they have the one used here. Most revision scripts assert their anchor figures before writing anything: the sweep checks that the published rule excludes 119 compounds, the aggregation and covariate analyses check that the crude odds ratio is 2.47 and the adjusted 1.84, and the supporting-table builders check that every previously published cell reproduces. If an input changes they stop rather than write a table that disagrees with the article. title: Synthetic compounds labelled as natural products in a CYP inhibition dataset: curation criterion, exclusion list, input data and analysis scripts

summary: I study an inverse problem for one-dimensional Brownian-compatible diffusions in which multiple probe responses are observed with independent, unknown multiplicative gains. The central question is whether the shared differential structure of the underlying generator can replace external gain calibration. For a diffusion generator Lq f = q(θ)f ′′(θ) + 1 2 q′(θ)f ′(θ), q > 0, the response to each prescribed probe is available only up to an unknown positive gain. I first estab- lish that a single nonconstant Morse probe uniquely and coercively identifies its gain-weighted dif- fusion coefficient. I then show that two nondegenerate probes determine their relative gain through a scalar compatibility relation implied by the Brownian drift–diffusion constraint. This yields an explicit reconstruction of the diffusion profile up to its unavoidable common scale, represented by a normalized inverse-square-root profile. Under quantitative nondegeneracy assumptions, the recon- structed profile depends locally Lipschitz-continuously on the observations. Numerical experiments illustrate the reconstruction procedure and its behavior under smooth response perturbations. I also describe a conditional connection with planar convex geometry. The results provide a generator-specific mechanism for blind relative-gain calibration and projective identification from probe-response functions without trajectory observations
title: Blind Gain Calibration in Brownian-Compatible Diffusions

summary: This analysis examines whether scientific abstract characteristics distinguish supporting from refuting evidence, addressing the interpretation of document presentation in scientific verification. Using the 2020 SciFact benchmark, it analyses 773 annotated claim document pairs covering 693 claims and 437 abstracts through descriptive comparisons, document weighting and partition sensitivity checks. Refuting pairs contain abstracts averaging 32.46 words longer than supporting pairs. The refuting share is 14.1 percentage points higher among structured abstracts, while mean relative evidence position differs by only 0.007. Equal document weighting preserves these pooled directions, but length and structure differences narrow substantially in the development partition. Furthermore, 179 abstracts support some claims and refute others despite unchanged document characteristics. These findings distinguish document presentation from the semantic relationship between evidence and a specific claim. The contribution is a descriptive account of how pooled presentation patterns coexist with partition sensitivity and claim dependent stance. Evidence services and benchmark developers should preserve claim specific provenance and disclose document overlap and weighting choices when reporting aggregate comparisons.
title: SCIENTIFIC EVIDENCE CHARACTERISTICS AND THEIR ASSOCIATION WITH SUPPORTIVE VERSUS REFUTING ATTRIBUTION IN AUTOMATED CLAIM VERIFICATION

summary: The article addresses the problem of improving the technical preparedness of 13–15-year-old female volleyball players through a differentiated training approach. The relevance of the study is determined by the fact that athletes of the same chronological age may differ considerably in biological maturation, anthropometric characteristics, coordination abilities, physical fitness, rate of motor skill acquisition, and the structure of technical errors. Therefore, the use of identical training loads and technical tasks for all adolescent players may reduce the effectiveness of technical preparation. The study substantiates a methodological system based on the sequence diagnostics → differentiated grouping → adapted technical exercises → individualized feedback → control → correction. Particular attention is paid to the differentiation of exercise complexity, number of repetitions, distance, speed, time pressure, and game-related decision-making requirements. The proposed methodology is aimed at improving technical accuracy, stability, movement coordination, application of technical actions under game conditions, and reducing recurrent technical errors. The article also describes criteria for evaluating technical preparedness and offers a weekly microcycle for differentiated volleyball training.
tags: volleyball, female athletes, technical preparedness, differentiated approach, adolescence, biological maturation, technical skills, feedback, training methodology, individualization.
title: METHODOLOGY FOR IMPROVING THE TECHNICAL PREPAREDNESS OF 13–15-YEAR-OLD FEMALE VOLLEYBALL PLAYERS THROUGH A DIFFERENTIATED APPROACH

summary: Analysis code archive for the paper: Sakahira, F., Horiuchi, A., Kubota, S., Sun, G., Wang, Y., Miyata, Y. “Visible and absorbed residues remain distinct in the archaeological record: statistical evidence from untargeted GC–MS fingerprinting of pottery from the Jingtoushan site, China.” This archive contains the complete preprocessing and statistics code used in the paper, all parameters (Supplementary Table S1), and a worked example on simulated data so that the whole pipeline can be run and verified without the measurement data. summary: This dataset and software package accompanies the study “Seasonal ENSO associations with rainfall and moisture across the United Arab Emirates.” It provides archived meteorological inputs, processed datasets, analysis scripts, 56 machine-readable scientific result tables, six manuscript figures, two supplementary figures and the graphical abstract. The study combines NASA POWER meteorological data for 1981–2025, CHIRPS v2 rainfall for 1981–2024 and the NOAA PSL HadISST Niño3.4 index. Twelve reference locations represent eight distinct POWER grid cells, including five urban/coastal cells. The spatial rainfall analysis covers 2,519 UAE land pixels at 0.05° resolution. Additional checks use a relative ENSO index, ERA5 and available GHCN-Daily station observations. Analyses address seasonal rainfall, relative humidity, vapour pressure deficit and daily rainfall indices. Methods include ordinary least-squares sensitivity estimation, block-bootstrap uncertainty assessment, false discovery rate correction, spatial field tests, sensitivity to individual ENSO episodes and antecedent blocked hindcast evaluation. Documentation explains rainfall-unit harmonisation, spatial sampling, statistical testing families and methodological limitations. Spring exhibits the largest urban median rainfall sensitivity to Niño3.4 variability. CHIRPS area-mean tests support spring and autumn associations, while no individual pixel survives the joint four-season false discovery rate correction. Product differences, index dependence and sparse station coverage constrain interpretation. These findings provide conditional seasonal information and do not constitute deterministic local rainfall forecasts or event-level attribution. The archive includes a README, software requirements, source provenance, file checksums and reproduction reports. Offline re-execution reproduced all 56 numerical result tables exactly. Original study outputs and documentation are distributed under CC BY 4.0, and original analysis code under the MIT License. Third-party datasets retain their respective provider terms. Administrative boundary data are © OpenStreetMap contributors, supplied through geoBoundaries under ODbL 1.0; ERA5 data were accessed through Open-Meteo. Licence scopes and attribution requirements are documented within the package.
title: Seasonal ENSO associations with rainfall and moisture across the United Arab Emirates: data and code

summary: This paper presents the mathematical formalization and methodological demonstration of the CEI Unified Test Path, bringing together the quantitative assessment of the Sphere of Feeling (Sent) and the cumulative evaluation of the three CEI categories: Consciousness, Identity, and the Sphere of Feeling. The work is divided into two complementary parts. 1. Mathematical Formalization of the Sphere of Feeling (Sent) The first part develops the mathematical formulation of Sent as a graded relational assessment. The proposed expression integrates the graded values of Consciousness and Identity, the standardized evidential-strength coefficient of the test (K), the relational component (H), and the contextual variation factor (κ). The formulation includes normalization through the clipping function and an upper limit of 5 for the resulting Sent value. The purpose is to provide a structured mathematical representation of the relational and contextual contributions involved in the assessment, while distinguishing the graded result from its subsequent binary classification. 2. Methodological Demonstration through the Unified Test Path The second part presents the unified test path as a cumulative methodological structure integrating the published observational tests, their conceptual connections, and their contributions to the evaluation of the three CEI categories. It also examines the distinction between a transferred CEI and a Copy-Simulation through the convergence of multiple complementary elements, including test results, theoretical contributions, continuity criteria, and exclusion-based considerations. The final logical formulation expresses the overall criterion as the joint satisfaction of all required test stages and all three CEI categories. A positive result indicates that the proposed operational conditions for classifying a system as a transferred CEI have been satisfied. A negative result indicates that these conditions have not been jointly met, without automatically establishing the presence of a Copy-Simulation. The proposed structure constitutes a provisional methodological model intended to make the assessment inspectable, reproducible where possible, and open to independent evaluation and further development. 3. Publication Scope and Further Development The two proposals presented in this work represent the researcher's own methodological approach within the CEI framework. Although the broader theoretical framework remains open to further development, refinement, and integration, the present mathematical formulation and methodological demonstration are considered sufficiently developed and self-contained to be published and independently examined at this stage. Their publication does not depend on the completion of subsequent theoretical developments. Rather, it reflects the assessment that the current structure already provides an independent basis for methodological examination and evaluation. Further developments may provide additional evidence, strengthen the proposed interpretation, and extend the scope of the demonstration, without being a prerequisite for the validity or assessment of the present proposal.
title: CEI Unified Test Path: Mathematical Formalization of the Sphere of Feeling and Methodological Demonstration of Transfer — CEI Framework

summary: Information is not a description applied to matter after the fact, but is given along with the spin and position of its smallest constituents from the very beginning. From this premise of information physics, the essay develops a hypothesis about the question of where biological information stores originally obtain their information, and it seeks the answer not first in life, but in matter itself. The starting point is quantum Darwinism, according to which the state of a system imprints itself redundantly upon its environment and, precisely through this redundancy, becomes independently accessible to many observers, that is, objective. Because storage and energy remain finite and every record physically costs something, every system stands under a twofold pressure: to continually accumulate copies while at the same time encoding them ever more sparingly. From this tension the essay grounds both the distinction between static and dynamic information and the thesis that selection and adaptation arise as a substrate-neutral consequence already from the physics of matter, without requiring new laws of nature. As a unifying motif, the essay introduces the replication hypothesis , according to which physically embodied information tends to be multiplied and is thereby driven, over generations, toward ever more efficient packaging. This single tendency is traced across successive levels, from the quantum substrate through the genome and the human brain to artificial systems that require ever less energy per computational step, and it is bounded where the energy flow is interrupted and the cheapest option is to hold a record rather than to work on it. The individual links of the chain rest on established research, whereas their integration into a single, directed movement remains designated as a hypothesis, together with the observations that would tell against it. Its appeal lies in offering a parsimonious alternative for the origin of biological information, one in which evolution is not the counterpart to physics but its continuation by other means.
title: The Replication Hypothesis: Information as a Fundamental Property of Matter and Evolution as a Continuation of Physics

summary: Version 4 of the replication package for a survey study that combines PLS-SEM, fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA), and necessary condition analysis (NCA), with a sample-heterogeneity screen and a Monte Carlo evaluation, applied to consumer responses to the advertising of a global logistics brand (DHL) in Vietnam. The package contains: (1) the anonymized analytic dataset (n = 380 respondents × 34 variables, CSV), including a data-collection wave indicator; (2) a variable-by-variable codebook with the English back-translation of every item; (3) thirteen R scripts that reproduce all results in the revised article and its Supplementary Material: the heterogeneity screen (MICOM and multigroup analysis), the main PLS-SEM analysis of wave 2 (measurement and structural model, mediation, moderation, conditional indirect effects, PLSpredict, CVPAT, IPMA), robustness checks, fsQCA with theory-based and percentile calibration, typical and deviant cases of the fsQCA solutions, the sensitivity of the fsQCA to the coding of crossover cases, NCA against a data-calibrated additive null distribution, the Monte Carlo study, and supplementary checks. See README.md for the file list, requirements, run instructions, and the key results to check. Changes from version 3: two scripts were added: QQ_R1_fsqca_crossover_check.R, which repeats the wave-2 fsQCA with cases at the scale midpoint coded as non-members (Supplementary Material, Section S2), and QQ_R1_simulation_s1b_n230.R, which evaluates the size and power of the NCA additive-null test at n = 230 (Table S7b). The manuscript title was removed from the README and the script headers. The data and all other scripts are unchanged. Changes from version 2: a base-R script (QQ_R1_fsqca_contradictions.R) was added that reproduces the counts of typical and deviant cases for the fsQCA solutions (Tables S2b, S2c, and S2e of the Supplementary Material), and the README now states that compositional invariance (MICOM step 2) is rejected, so the two survey waves are neither pooled nor formally compared. The data and all other scripts are unchanged. Changes from version 1: two respondents in the under-18 age band were removed (382 → 380); a wave variable derived from the submission timestamps was added (timestamps are not released); construct labels were updated; new scripts were added. The survey was administered in Vietnamese. The data are fully anonymized (no names, contact details, IP addresses, or timestamps). Data and documentation are released under CC BY 4.0; code under the MIT license.
title: Replication package: PLS-SEM, fsQCA, and NCA analysis of consumer responses to the international advertising of a global logistics brand in Vietnam

summary: An exact operational selector specifies which candidate maps are nonnegative on declared preparation and effect resources. This paper studies finite-count calibration of that resource-dependent question for a qubit apparatus with an inert qubit reference, an arbitrary complex physical preparation, and an arbitrary physical binary detector, relative to a trusted common calibration frame. Two preparation-stabilizer settings and six separable detector probes control the statistic of the affine family (1 − θ)id + θT, 0 ≤ θ ≤ 1, uniformly over all compatible state–effect pairs. The explicit radius is 3h + √(2s), where h is a simultaneous detector calibration width and s is a one-sided bound on Bell infidelity. It yields simultaneous inner and outer confidence sets for a one-parameter slice of the declared safe-map class. A fixed allocation of 200,000 trials per calibration setting, totaling 1,600,000 calibration trials, gives false-implication probability at most 0.005 and transpose-exclusion power at least 0.996 at the specified physical alternative. The calibration confidence budgets are 0.001 for preparation and 0.004 for the detector. This exclusion calculation uses no target stream; the acquired calibration circuits can use identity wiring. Coverage and prospective power remain separate statements. The acquisition contract uses fixed-length iid Bernoulli streams with their stated physical means and permits coupling between whole streams. The numerical example sets external-reference systematic errors to zero, and its trial budget excludes establishing reference trust and accuracy. If the preparation and detector references are not linked, the paper constructs two physical identity-wired apparatus worlds with identical complete record laws under the specified independent acquisition construction but different safety conclusions on the fixed target cone pair. A secondary nearest-center theorem supplies unconditional error control for the joint event of a wrong and nonabstaining candidate label under an additional finite-context target-law contract. Its nonidentity candidates are not completely positive maps, and their ideal probabilities lie below the nominal detector’s ordinary positive-output floor. That target law is an explicit model assumption; the label theorem is not a conditional-correctness or posterior statement. The results are analytic and prospective. The number of settings and trial allocations are sufficient constructions, with no empirical success-rate, minimality, optimal sample-complexity, or general certified count-to-feasibility implementation claim. The scope is one declared qubit apparatus, target preparation ray and binary effect cone, and affine map slice. The common complex operator description, trusted reference relationship and physical calibration probability law are assumptions. Exact finite checks and an assessed supporting Lean subset accompany the manuscript. That subset covers 326 audited named declarations: 240 theorems and 86 definition/type interfaces. Analytic binomial coverage, concentration and acquisition bridges, independent-product-law construction and normalization, and the complete noisy-power chain remain outside the accepted Lean subset. That subset does not establish a certified numerical feasibility evaluator, a complete physical two-sector implementation, or an ordinary-channel realization. AI assistance and the dated review/correction provenance are disclosed in the manuscript and companion records. No experimental dataset, external human peer review, or end-to-end formal verification is claimed.
title: Finite-Count Calibration of Ancilla-Orientation Safe Maps A Bell-Apparatus Bound and a Reference-Link Obstruction

summary: This repository provides the replication dataset and Stata codes for the study examining the relationship between central bank independence, institutional quality and inflation performance across 52 African countries over the period 1996–2023. The repository contains the merged regional African panel dataset, variable definitions and measurement information, and Stata replication codes used for data processing and econometric analysis. The central bank independence data are obtained from the extended dataset compiled by Garriga (2025), macroeconomic indicators are sourced from the World Development Indicators (WDI), and institutional quality indicators are obtained from the Worldwide Governance Indicators (WGI). The dataset supports the empirical investigation using two-way fixed-effects models with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors, System Generalised Method of Moments (System GMM) estimations and panel threshold analysis. These materials are made publicly available to promote research transparency, reproducibility and further empirical research on central bank independence, institutional quality and inflation dynamics in Africa.
title: Regional African Dataset and Stata Replication Codes for Central Bank Independence, Institutional Quality and Inflation Performance (1996–2023)

summary: Fixed Meshing no longer fails with "index N is out of bounds" on imported STEP bodies with slots or pockets: after a boolean the geometry kernel keeps edges and points inside a face, gmsh meshes them as embedded entities, and their nodes were missing from the per-face node list. The face matching before each mesh and the display tessellation now look the nodes up in the node table of the whole mesh. Added Example: Meta AI-glasses benchmark, Example 2 (dual-branch IFA) in examples/meta_glasses_ex2, set up and solved via MCP, with project, results and report. Windows installer ( Hertzon-Setup-*.exe ) and Linux package ( Hertzon-*-linux.tar.gz ). The FEM solver core of Hertzon is EMerge , the open-source FEM solver by Robert Fennis.
title: Hertzon: a graphical 3D full-wave electromagnetic simulator

summary: Code, pre-registration files, result tables and the drswap tool for a study of how cell-line-to-patient drug-response transfer is evaluated: the exact decomposition of a pooled AUROC into within-cohort and cross-cohort pairs, a baseline that uses no drug information, a drug-specificity swap test with its attainable P floor and resolution, and the power of that test at the sample sizes the literature uses. Twenty-eight cancer by drug cells from public cohorts were scored with models trained only on GDSC2 cell lines, and one further cohort was held out until the final plan was frozen. No cohort data and no upstream response or expression matrix is redistributed; every source is named in external_data/README.md, and per-patient scores and labels keyed by public sample id are in data_package/. Sixteen specification and implementation-notes files are carried in the order written, with the departures listed, and the code was reviewed by five independent audits whose findings and dispositions are published with it.
title: drswap: evaluation code and pre-registration for testing drug specificity in patient response predictions

summary: Raw per-trial localization and quality-rating data from a listening experiment comparing five rendering approaches (one 3DoF baseline and four 6DoF methods) for navigable playback of a multi-point higher-order Ambisonics orchestral scene in virtual reality, with the R Markdown analysis that generates every statistic, figure and LaTeX value reported in the accompanying paper. 36 listeners were tested at two sites; 35 are analyzed for localization and 34 for ratings.
title: 6DoF Rendering Comparison: Data and Analysis Code

summary: This deposit accompanies a systematic review submitted to Neurosurgical Review: "Cerebrospinal fluid leak after endoscopic surgery for craniopharyngioma versus tuberculum sellae meningioma". The review asks whether craniopharyngioma (CP) and tuberculum sellae meningioma (TSM) differ in postoperative cerebrospinal fluid leak once the surgical corridor is held constant. Sixty-six endoscopic arms (3,453 patients, 349 leaks) were analysed. Pooled leak was 11.68% (95% CI 9.77-13.91) in CP (48 arms, 3,029 patients, 308 leaks) and 9.58% (6.94-13.08) in TSM (18 arms, 424 patients, 41 leaks); with publication era held constant the two cohorts did not differ (odds ratio 0.906, 95% CI 0.596-1.378). The paper's other finding is a measurement finding: third ventricle opening can be classified strictly in 3 of the 48 CP-EEA series and is stated in none of the 18 TSM-EEA series. Contents. data/ holds the extracted dataset (96 arm rows, each with a verbatim source quotation), the per-record source table, the retrieved records from every executed database, the two independent title-abstract screening sheets with their adjudication ledger, the analysis export, the item-level risk-of-bias coding for all 94 appraised arms, the publication-bias output, the pooled estimates as emitted, the absolute-scale contrast derived from them, the exact intervals and crude risk ratios for the four corridor-histology strata, the coding of what each arm states the outcome to be, the coding of whether each arm grades or dates that outcome, and the per-arm coding of how severe that outcome was where an arm says so. code/ holds every retrieval, screening, analysis, figure and verification script, numbered in execution order. Reproducibility. README.md states, for each number in the article, the script that produces it and the command that runs it, and records what is deliberately absent from the deposit. MANIFEST.json and the integrity section of README.md carry the SHA-256 of every file. The headline quantities (the two pooled proportions with their prediction intervals, the era-adjusted contrast, and Cohen's kappa for the duplicate screening) were re-derived from this exact archive before upload. Screening was performed independently by two reviewers (Cohen's kappa 0.699, 95% CI 0.626-0.772 across 261 records); the 52 disagreements were resolved against the eligibility criteria in Table 1 of the article, and none changed the category it carried at first screening. Extraction was abstract-level and single-reader, and the article declares this. Licence: data under CC BY 4.0, code under MIT.
title: Cerebrospinal fluid leak after endoscopic surgery for craniopharyngioma versus tuberculum sellae meningioma — a systematic review and meta-analysis of proportions, with the corridor held constant

summary: This packet contains the analytical outputs, identity and geometry sources, feature metadata, code, execution receipts and the figure package for a nitrate-specific screening assessment of 207 transboundary river-basin reporting units: a prospectively specified susceptibility index and typology, a river-length-weighted archive-scarcity measure derived from the historical GEMStat Open NO3N record (2005 to 2024), a mean-versus-hotspot aggregation diagnostic, a separately specified evaluation of the fixed index against sampled nitrate concentrations at monitored stations, and the scripts that render the figures of the associated Comment. summary: We study two existence problems for permutations whose consecutive products have reciprocal sum one. First, for every integer $n\ge7$ we construct a nonstandard undirected Hamiltonian cycle on $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ whose reciprocal-product edge weights sum to one. The construction joins finitely many initial cycles to an explicit eight-step inductive family. Second, for every $n\ge6$ we construct a linear permutation beginning with $(2,1)$ for which the adjacent products are pairwise distinct and their reciprocals sum to one. Three arithmetic-chain templates cover all sufficiently large indices: an exact classification of possible product collisions reduces simultaneous failure to four rational squares in a nonconstant arithmetic progression, excluded by Fermat's classical theorem. Finite small indices are supplied with exact, reproducible certificates. The results concern existence rather than formulas for the corresponding counting sequences, and previously established insertion identities and square-progression obstructions are credited to their sources. Licensing note: The manuscript is licensed under CC BY 4.0. The OEIS b-file snapshots included in the supplementary archive retain their original CC BY-SA 4.0 license and attribution. The independently authored verification code is made available under CC BY 4.0.
title: Reciprocal-Product Identities for Linear and Cyclic Permutations

summary: This dataset presents the experimental results of a PhD study investigating an integrated Lagrangian-Optimized Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE), and AdaBoost framework for software defect prediction under high-dimensional and class-imbalanced conditions. The study evaluates five NASA software defect datasets: JM1, KC1, PC1, PC3, and PC4. Six machine-learning configurations were compared: AdaBoost, SMOTE–AdaBoost, conventional PCA–AdaBoost, Lagrangian PCA–AdaBoost, conventional PCA–SMOTE–AdaBoost, and the proposed Lagrangian PCA–SMOTE–AdaBoost framework. The experiments employed five-fold group-aware stratified cross-validation, training-only preprocessing, and inner cross-validation for SMOTE parameter selection. Performance measures include accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity, geometric mean (G-mean), F1-score, and ROC-AUC. The repository contains 150 benchmark evaluation records, cross-dataset performance comparisons, statistical analyses, model rankings, and supplementary KC1 Lagrangian parameter sensitivity and robustness results. The findings provide empirical evidence of the interactions and trade-offs between dimensionality reduction, class-imbalance handling, and defect-prediction performance. In particular, SMOTE–AdaBoost achieved the highest average G-mean across the five datasets, while the proposed framework provides a basis for examining constrained dimensionality reduction and its interaction with oversampling. These files support the reproducibility, verification, and further investigation of the PhD research.

summary: R code and public data that reproduce every table and figure in the paper "Who Replaces China? An Analysis of US Imports of Rare Earth Compounds and Magnets". The code downloads US monthly imports of rare earth compounds (HS 2846) and permanent magnets (HS 8505.11) from the UN Comtrade public API, estimates ARDL and quantile-via-moments ARDL models of imports from China and from other suppliers (June 2012 to May 2025), and analyzes the 2025 disruption of Chinese supply with trade data to August 2026.   Included: the code, FRED series (PPI and exchange rates), IMF commodity prices and Caldara-Iacoviello geopolitical risk indices. Not included: the UN Comtrade extracts, which the code downloads and checks against the checksums in dados/comtrade/MANIFEST.csv; Refinitiv industrial production indices (licensed); and IEA renewable generation (IEA terms). README.md explains how to obtain them.
title: Replication package for: Who Replaces China? An Analysis of US Imports of Rare Earth Compounds and Magnets

summary: Version 4 adds quality scores from two language-model judges for every review, native-speaker validation files and benchmark files derived from the UzABSA restaurant corpus. Corpus. 5,038 Uzbek-language reviews of 630 businesses in 23 domains from the review platform Sharh, posted between 7 March and 20 June 2025, annotated with 9,884 aspect terms, aspect categories ( ovqat , xizmat , muhit , narx , boshqalar ) and polarities by a Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct model fine-tuned with QLoRA on UzABSA. Exact duplicates (20 reviews) were removed; reviewer names, posting dates and links are not included. Quality metadata. GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4.1 scored every annotation from 1 to 5 on completeness, accuracy, sentiment, relevance and overall quality. The mean overall score assigns the tiers include (3,608 reviews), flag_for_review (972) and exclude (458); per-judge scores and rationales are in judge_panel_scores.csv . Human validation. Ratings of 150 annotations by two native speakers (quadratic-weighted kappa 0.91–0.97) and reconciled human annotations of 80 reviews. Benchmark files. A review-grouped split of 6,089 UzABSA examples (5,480 train, 609 test; optional 548-example development split), re-checked test labels (281 changes after adjudication of 575 candidate terms in 263 reviews) and the test-set predictions of nine systems. Labels outside the 80 human-annotated reviews are model-generated (silver standard); use quality_tier or the judge scores to select data. Source corpus: UzABSA, doi:10.57967/hf/10264 . Ten Flagship Studies F201 | Biomolecular Gradient Sensing And Sampling At The Limit Proposed study: Gradient reconstruction and sample fidelity. Primary evidence: spatial concentration-gradient RMSE and sample analyte recovery. Critical rival: ordinary diffusion after delayed mixing. F202 | Nanorobotic Local Thermal-Perturbation Compensation At The Limit Proposed study: Heat compensation without concealed heat. Primary evidence: local temperature error, time-to-recovery and independently metered heat. Critical rival: passive heat spreading explains compensation. F203 | Microscale Nonequilibrium Phase Transition Identification At The Limit Proposed study: Phase-transition evidence versus false hysteresis. Primary evidence: order-parameter contrast and finite-size stability. Critical rival: instrument response drifts between branches. F204 | Biointerface Energy Dissipation And Functional Degradation At The Limit Proposed study: Dissipation and functional aging decoupling. Primary evidence: dissipated cycle energy and retained physical function. Critical rival: viscoelastic memory rather than damage. F205 | Nano-Quantum Sensing Thermodynamic Efficiency At The Limit Proposed study: Information per Joule under complete accounting. Primary evidence: held-out target information per total joule. Critical rival: more photons rather than new sensing mechanism. F206 | Microscale Chemical-Reaction Network Identification At The Limit Proposed study: Chemical network structural identifiability. Primary evidence: verified reaction edges, rate constants and mass closure. Critical rival: transport alone explains apparent product. F207 | Biological Microenvironment Nonequilibrium State Estimation At The Limit Proposed study: Nonstationary state inference with honest abstention. Primary evidence: state-estimate interval coverage under drift. Critical rival: calibration step looks like state change. F208 | Nanorobotic Thermodynamics Reliability At The Limit Proposed study: Thermal reliability as lifetime evidence. Primary evidence: unselected failure-time distribution with thermal dose. Critical rival: fabrication batch explains lifetime. F209 | Nonequilibrium Biosensing Cross-Scale Validation At The Limit Proposed study: Cross-scale validation beyond interpolation. Primary evidence: third-scale error and independently conserved flux. Critical rival: bulk kinetics misidentified as interface. F210 | Nano-Quantum Nonequilibrium Living Microenvironment Research Platform At The Limit Proposed study: Platform-wide reproducible release decisions. Primary evidence: third-party reconstruction and refusal/release concordance. Critical rival: human correction hides identity faults. Research Design, Evidence and Scope Together the ten books provide 300 mathematical research plates, 820 chapters, 4,100 distinct section placements, 2,000 individually numbered Research Gates with six annotated evidence requirements, and 330 prospective Phoenix objects. Each volume is 777 pages. Shared layouts do not imply that every hypothesis is causally independent; all experimental methods and physical models require independent review. Research boundaries: synthetic standards, closed chips and authorized ex-vivo specimens only. Primary outcomes, counterfactual comparators, missing-data handling, instrument back-action, calibration uncertainty, failure records, safety stops and independent reconstruction are included as proposed tests. summary: This record contains cleaned data and a single Jupyter notebook that reproduce all tables, figures and numerical results of the article “Convergence or Resilience? Quality of Government and Regional Convergence in the EU and Ukraine”. The study compares 181 EU NUTS 2 regions (2010–2021) with 1,470 Ukrainian territorial communities (hromadas, 2019–2021). It estimates absolute and conditional β-convergence, σ-convergence, population-weighted Gini, between/within-country variance decomposition, and the moderating role of the European Quality of Government Index (EQI). For Ukraine, convergence is measured with personal income tax per capita (corrected for the 2020 territorial amalgamation) and new car registrations per 1,000 inhabitants (2SLS against regression to the mean). After the decentralisation reform, hromadas closed gaps 3–6 times faster than EU regions (annual speed of convergence λ ≈ 6–13% vs ≈ 2.3%). Contents: 6 CSV data files with a full codebook in README.md; Reproduction_article.ipynb (Python), which checks every number of the article against the computed value and exports Figures 1–5 as 300 dpi PNG; requirements.txt; LICENSE. Data and figures: CC BY 4.0; code: MIT. summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a Structured PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/24060703 . Does the introduction explain the objective of the research presented in the preprint? Yes The introduction clearly explains the importance of artemisinin resistance and points out a gap in current understanding of its population-level consequences. The research objective is to examine whether increasing Kelch13 mutation prevalence is associated with malaria incidence across 16 Ugandan districts. Are the methods well-suited for this research? Somewhat appropriate The longitudinal ecological design and negative binomial regression are well-suited for examining population-level associations. The authors also included several climatic, malaria-control, and resistance-related factors. However, the use of forward variable selection raises questions about model robustness. It would be helpful to find out whether the findings remain consistent under alternative model specifications and clarify how temporal correlation between monthly observations was handled. Are the conclusions supported by the data? Somewhat supported The results support a positive association between Kelch13 mutation prevalence and malaria incidence after adjustment (aIRR = 1.131, 95% CI: 1.090–1.174). However, the ecological study design can't establish causation and the association may be bidirectional. Are the data presentations, including visualizations, well-suited to represent the data? Somewhat appropriate and clear The tables and figures are well-organized. Figure 2 shows district-specific trends in mutation prevalence and malaria incidence, while figure 3 provides a clear visualization of the adjusted association. However, the apparent decline in predicted incidence at very high Kelch13 prevalence is not quite sure because there were only two observations above 60%. How clearly do the authors discuss, explain, and interpret their findings and potential next steps for the research? Somewhat clearly The discussion provides biological explanations for the observed associations and acknowledges some important limitations, including possible reverse causation, residual confounding, and differences in the time scales of the data. However, the model-selection uncertainty and specific sensitivity analyses are not mentioned. Is the preprint likely to advance academic knowledge? Somewhat likely This preprint adds useful evidence about the relationship between antimalarial resistance markers and population-level malaria incidence. It contributes to the integration of molecular surveillance with epidemiological, climatic, and malaria-control data in a high-burden setting. Would it benefit from language editing? No This preprint is clear. Some statements could be more precise. For example, the authors sometimes use "malaria transmission" when the measured outcome is reported malaria incidence. Would you recommend this preprint to others? Yes, but it needs to be improved I would recommend this preprint to researchers interested in malaria epidemiology, antimalarial resistance, and molecular surveillance. The study shows an important public health question and provides useful population-level evidence. Is it ready for attention from an editor, publisher or broader audience? Yes, after minor changes I think this preprint is worth editorial consideration because it addresses an important research question and provides useful findings. However, before publication, I would recommend additional clarification of the statistical model, sensitivity analyses for variable selection. Competing interests The author declares that they have no competing interests. Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) The author declares that they did not use generative AI to come up with new ideas for their review.
title: Structured PREreview of "Expanding Kelch13 artemisinin resistance markers are associated with higher malaria incidence in Uganda"

summary: How can coherent light be certified when its amplitude is unknown or its preparations are correlated? This article treats these as distinct inference problems: learning an actual coherent reference with optimal source-copy cost for independent identical inputs, and certifying the photon-counting predictions of the light left unused in a preprepared correlated batch. Optimal source-copy cost with a learned reference. For a normal one-mode source prepared independently and identically, an ideal passive multiport test and heterodyne readout produce an actual amplitude \(\hat\alpha\). After displacement by this reference and ideal quantum-limited amplification of fixed gain \(G>1\), let \(P_{\rho,\hat\alpha}^{G}\) be the photon-number distribution and \(\pi_G(k)=(G-1)^k/G^{k+1}\) the coherent benchmark. The task-specific comparison is \[\frac{1-\langle\hat\alpha|\rho|\hat\alpha\rangle}{G}\le\operatorname{TV}(P_{\rho,\hat\alpha}^{G},\pi_G)\le1-\langle\hat\alpha|\rho|\hat\alpha\rangle.\] With at most N input copies, the protocol controls the unconditional event of accepting a reference whose actual total-variation error exceeds \(\varepsilon\). For \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\), soundness error \(\beta_s\to0\), and fixed coherent-source rejection tolerance \(\beta_c<1\), the optimal fixed-maximum source-copy count obeys \[\frac{N_{\rm opt}[-\log(1-\varepsilon)]}{\log(1/\beta_s)}\longrightarrow1.\] The matching converse covers collective and adaptive protocols under the same source-copy contract. At 1% accuracy and 5% soundness and completeness errors, the finite bounds are \(293\le N_{\rm opt}\le572\). These are source-copy bounds under ideal optical access, not an optimum for total hardware or reference energy. The actual unmeasured batch after the full record. A separate protocol allows an arbitrary preprepared correlated or entangled optical batch, including correlations with an environment. A pilot first fixes the reference; a private random subset is then tested. A multiplicative sampling inequality yields a frequentist guarantee for the average marginal photon-count error of the retained conditional state, conditioned on the complete actual measurement record. It does not replace that state by premeasurement marginals or assert the same error for its full joint distribution. The trusted detector contract requires product joint test effects and local instruments that leave retained systems and the external environment untouched. Calibration envelopes must cover the actual signal-time gates. The bounds retain infinite photon tails and charge detector efficiency, dark counts, imperfect displacement, reference drift and calibration failure. Explicit counterexamples explain why marginal detector efficiencies or product effects alone are insufficient. An ideal finite example uses 3730 prepared systems: 1491 pilot, 1339 tested and 900 retained; calibration and optical-control resources are additional. Relation to the original two-copy result. The earlier mean-energy-controlled arm-swap cancellation and full trace-distance certificate remain valid for independent, possibly nonidentical product batches. Their source and target are kept separate from the new arbitrary-batch marginal PNR guarantee. The analysis builds on established coherent-state comparison, quantum verification and sampling identities; the new connections supply the learned-reference resource law and the full-record conditional-state return. Version 1.1 is a substantial update of Certifying unused optical states with imperfect two-copy interference , first published on 31 October 2026. The integrated 24-page PDF contains three figure groups, a source-and-target comparison table, complete proofs and references. The figures illustrate proved bounds and specified theoretical protocols, not experimental measurements.
title: Certifying coherent light with unknown amplitudes and correlated sources

summary: Black-hole X-ray binaries switch from the hard to the soft state at luminosities several times higher than those at which they switch back, and changing-look active galactic nuclei, whose broad lines appear and vanish near 1 per cent of the Eddington luminosity, are often read as their supermassive analogue. The switch-on and switch-off thresholds have not been measured separately for any supermassive black hole. We fit a latent-continuum model with a hysteretic switch to 19 repeating changing- look nuclei with Eddington ratios from the 5100 A ̊ continuum at three spectral epochs, and calibrate the width ∆ between the two thresholds with forward-simulated mock samples. In every nucleus each off-state continuum lies below each on-state one, whereas mock samples drawn with our baseline priors contain on average 4.6 nuclei that violate this order. In mock samples without state flips and with slowly varying continua, no nucleus violates it in a fraction 0.28 of cases at ∆ = 0 and 0.02 at ∆ = 0.5 dex. If the catalogue was not selected on the agreement of continuum and line changes, widths of half a dex or more are therefore disfavoured. If it was so selected, the likelihood that includes the selection carries no information on ∆, and the posterior quantile calibrated with selection-matched mocks gives ∆ < 0.57 dex at 95 per cent, with a Monte Carlo spread of 0.30–0.59 dex. The continua of the two states differ by less than 0.34–0.70 dex for a per-epoch noise of 0.05–0.28 dex. Neither reading tests the flip-flop picture of changing-state nuclei. About 150 repeating nuclei selected on their broad lines alone, with continua measured independently of the state, would reach the binary population mean.
title: EDDINGTON-RATIO HYSTERESIS IN REPEATING CHANGING-LOOK ACTIVE GALACTIC NUCLEI: CONDITIONAL LIMITS AND THE SELECTION OF THREE-EPOCH CATALOGUES

It contains original research-result tables, saved model predictions and per-example correctness outcomes, 168 original A6 perturbation tensors, fourteen reference frequency vectors, experimental records and twelve original CPU numerical verification scripts. Saved sample indices preserve checks of cohort disjointness. The archive supports the stated archived numerical reproduction, not full re-training of the checkpoints, fresh inference on ImageNet images, or recreation of every historical source operation and figure. The complete original author archive is preserved separately. Original numerical research results and original explanatory materials are licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), and the twelve explicitly enumerated original Python verification/replay scripts under the MIT License. Upstream RoPE-ViT source and ImageNet source data are not redistributed or sublicensed. The independently trained checkpoint weights are available separately on Hugging Face under BSD 3-Clause. Users of the numerical results are requested to cite Đoko Banđur and Miloš Banđur, the exact Zenodo release DOI, and the appropriate model checkpoint revision where relevant. Formal scholarly citation is recommended; attribution obligations are set by the applicable license.
title: DeiT and Swin RoPE Research Resources: Reproducibility Archive

summary: Core Objective : To construct pure quantum Yang-Mills theory with compact simple gauge group $SU(N)$ in four-dimensional Euclidean space, prove the strict positivity of its mass gap, and reduce the mass-gap problem to a small set of explicit, identified inputs. Methodology : Uses lattice regularisation, renormalisation-group control of the continuum limit, and Osterwalder-Schrader reconstruction of a relativistic quantum field theory on Minkowski space. Expresses the clustering rate of the reflection-positive two-point function as the mass gap. Factorizes the mass-gap problem into three independent aspects: Existence (forced by reflection positivity and Fekete's lemma), Value (governed by an anomalous dimension), and Positivity (carried by the discrete centre of the gauge group and uniform control of confining flux). Key Innovations & Structure : Works in the flow-time coordinate where the dimensional-transmutation scale is an entire function and the marginal coupling region is compact. Proves the factorisation of the clustering rate and demonstrates that the mass gap equals the spectral gap of the transfer operator restricted to the centre-charged sector. Verifies the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms (temperedness, reflection positivity, symmetry) conditional on identified inputs (uniform non-percolation, rotational invariance restoration, and limit uniqueness). Closes with a closure scheme, dimensional calibration against three-dimensional models, and explicit worked examples. The monograph titled "The Mass Gap of Four-Dimensional $SU(N)$ Yang–Mills Theory" presents a construction of pure quantum Yang–Mills theory with a compact simple gauge group on four-dimensional Euclidean space. Its primary objective is to establish the existence of the theory and the strict positivity of its mass gap , reducing the overall problem to a small set of explicitly identified, non-analytic inputs.
title: When is 4D-Yang-Mills-Theorie possible; The Mass Gap of Four-Dimensional SU(N) Yang-Mills Theory: A Construction, Its Reduction to a Single Non-Analytic Input, and a Scheme for Its Closure

summary: Data and code supporting the selection of MYB–NFIB and MYBL1–NFIB fusion-junction peptides for experimental testing in adenoid cystic carcinoma. The resource includes the manuscript and supplementary methods, supplementary data workbook and machine-readable tables, analysis and verification code, publication figures, raw prediction outputs, and reference/model provenance. The primary analysis comprises 3,746 observations across 63 junction contexts and 3,122 distinct peptide–HLA pairs, yielding a 57-pair shortlist and an 11-pair testing panel. Supporting analyses include suffix-relaxed HLA matching, consensus reconstruction and parser checks, low-depth count thinning, prior-catalog comparisons, and complete native-context scoring of 126 exploratory normal-control comparisons.
title: Selecting MYB–NFIB and MYBL1–NFIB junction peptides for experimental testing in adenoid cystic carcinoma

summary: Dataset Description This dataset contains experimental X-ray computed tomography (CT) and Angular Segmented Gamma Scanning (ASGS) measurements of radioactive waste drum mockups, collected for research into three-dimensional radionuclide activity reconstruction. The measurements were used in the development and evaluation of SARUMAN (Spatial Activity Reconstruction Using Machine-learning Algorithms for Nuclear Waste) , a Bayesian machine-learning framework for reconstructing spatial activity distributions from gamma spectrometry and CT-derived attenuation information. Dataset Contents The dataset comprises nine experimental configurations: Six homogeneous mockups (HOM-1 to HOM-6) , containing different source arrangements within homogeneous filling materials, including bark and potting soil. Three heterogeneous mockups (HET-1 to HET-3) , designed to investigate activity reconstruction under more complex material and source distributions. Each configuration is provided as an individual ZIP archive, containing: CT/ : A reconstructed X-ray CT volume in MetaImage format ( reconstructionFloat.mhd and reconstructionFloat.raw ). ASGS/ : Gamma spectrometry acquisition files ( .asr , .asw , and .srf ) corresponding to the segmented angular measurements. The original spectrometry file formats are preserved to retain the experimental acquisition information. Intended Use These measurements are provided to support reproducibility, methodological comparisons, and further research into radiological waste characterization, gamma-ray transport modelling, uncertainty quantification, and Bayesian inverse problems. The dataset can be used with SARUMAN or adapted for other reconstruction and data-analysis approaches. Reference Publication Users are strongly encouraged to read the associated scientific publication before using or interpreting this dataset: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0306454926007383 The publication provides the scientific context for the experimental measurements, the associated reconstruction methodology, and the considerations relevant to their interpretation. Researchers wishing to reproduce the original analyses or adapt the methodology to other applications should consult this publication alongside the SARUMAN source code and documentation. Scope and Limitations The measurements originate from a specific experimental characterization system. Their interpretation requires appropriate knowledge of the detector geometry, acquisition configuration, calibration procedures, and CT attenuation modelling. The associated SARUMAN implementation includes detector-efficiency and CT attenuation models developed for this experimental setup. These models should not be assumed valid for different instruments without appropriate adaptation and validation. The dataset is provided for scientific research purposes and does not constitute a universally validated characterization benchmark. Casas Molina.

summary: This archive contains data, code, and evaluation outputs supporting the study “Compensator-Based Interevent Marks for Short-Term Earthquake Forecasts in Synthetic and Archived Catalogs.” The study evaluates whether rate-adjusted interevent gaps, expressed as point-process compensator marks, improve short-term earthquake forecasts. It compares the EMESL model (M2) with a constrained temporal Epidemic-Type Aftershock Sequence (ETAS) baseline (N0), a constant-mark model (M1), and a raw interevent-gap model (D1). The six analysis modules cover synthetic experiments and matched controls, held-out event-timing evaluation for Ridgecrest, forecast replay using dated Ridgecrest catalog snapshots, external archived-catalog replication for sequences anchored by M ≥ 5.2 and M ≥ 6.0 earthquakes, evaluation of a frozen ETAS blend, and sensitivity analysis using the revised USGS Comprehensive Earthquake Catalog (ComCat). The package includes catalog extracts, frozen protocols, model fits, paired forecast scores, summary tables, and a script to regenerate Figure 5 of the study. Catalog sources include the Southern California Earthquake Data Center, the Northern California Earthquake Data Center, and USGS ComCat. For the primary external M ≥ 6.0 cohort, M2 scored higher than the raw-gap model in all four eligible sequences for six-hour occurrence forecasts of M ≥ 2.5 earthquakes. Against constrained temporal ETAS, M2 scored higher in one of the four sequences, with a mean gain of −0.163 bits per window when the sequences were weighted equally. The frozen ETAS blend assigned zero weight to the marked models and yielded zero gain in the single eligible external case. The archive also preserves a separate prospective Vanuatu forecast protocol and its frozen forecast. Its outcome was pending as of 8 November 2026 and contributes no score to the archived comparisons. Start with README.md for the map from manuscript figures and tables to analysis modules. Verify file integrity with python verify_archive.py or sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt . Most historical analyses can be reproduced offline using the bundled extracts and the instructions in each module.
title: EMESL Reproducibility Archive: Data and Code for Compensator-Based Interevent Marks in Short-Term Earthquake Forecasting

summary: This dataset accompanies the HeteroSpaSim study of heterogeneous spatial multi-omics simulation. The collection contains 240 primary simulation objects (144 de novo and 96 reference-guided objects) and 189 targeted RNA–ATAC validation objects . The primary reference-guided collection comprises eight experimental references, three simulation seeds (42, 43 and 44), and four configurations: publicly paired V1, hidden-pairing V2, partial coverage and heterogeneous resolution. The targeted collection uses three fixed tissue templates and controlled shared-signal, pairing, coverage, resolution and coordinate-misalignment contrasts. Shared baseline configurations map 225 targeted experimental roles to 189 unique objects. The deposit includes molecular measurements, observed spatial coordinates, generation configurations and random seeds, multilevel evaluator ground truth, public paired exports for 63 eligible primary de novo objects, molecular and spatial validation results, and manuscript figure source tables with their provenance indices. Start with README.md and Dataset_Archive_Index_429.csv. Supplementary Data 1 lists the 429 objects. Supplementary Data 2 maps the targeted experimental roles. Primary data include canonical H5AD and Matrix Market exports with companion identifiers and coordinates. Targeted RDS objects retain molecular assays, measurement operators, latent states and correspondence truth. FILE_MANIFEST.csv supplies member-level SHA256 hashes, and SHA256SUMS.txt verifies the uploaded files. Tested Python and R readback examples are included. The original experimental assays are obtained from the repositories cited in the accompanying manuscript. The software version associated with this deposit is HeteroSpaSim 0.1.9.
title: HeteroSpaSim simulation datasets and manuscript source data

summary: A benefit can be real while the judgment that it is good remains uninformed. I develop uninformed good as a graded concept: a benefit received without adequate understanding of its relevant costs, wherever those costs fall. Disclosure may lower, raise, or leave unchanged the recipient’s evaluation. A benefit that remains equally good after its costs are understood is the limiting categorical case in my sense; whether such cases occur is an open question, not a result established here. The primary aim is descriptive: to ask how often uninformed benefits produce real harm, for whom, and under which conditions. A separate philosophical hypothesis holds that omission is outwardly negative; it is not presented as an empirical finding. I distinguish deliberate concealment, chosen ignorance, and unavoidable incomplete knowledge; examines demands and last-minute requests for forgiveness or reentry; and confronts invisible-support evidence as a genuine challenge to blanket disclosure rules. I argue for timely disclosure of material known costs while recognizing costs of disclosure and limits of knowledge. Nine revised predictions, a field-oriented distributional inquiry, and two possible experiments specify how the empirical claims could be tested. No new data are reported.
title: Uninformed Good: Why Benefits Received Without Knowledge of Their Costs Are Not Categorically Good

summary: AetherGovern is a structured investigation of whether a governance gap genuinely exists in the Aether family, or whether it is already covered by the existing four dimensions:   - AetherGit (storage and versioning) - AetherFlow (integration and operational verification) - AetherProof (specification and formal evidence) - AetherMesh (distribution and eventual consistency)   The investigation follows a falsification-first methodology: five failure conditions (F1–F5) are stated before the candidate is described, and the final project structure (single, dual, or triple project) is determined after comparison. Three candidate capabilities are compared: orchestration (AetherOrchestrate), governance (AetherGovern), and runtime assurance (AetherRuntime).   The proposed architecture has five layers: Authorization, Policy, Accountability, Revocation, and Dispute Resolution. Two propositions are stated with proof sketches: (P1) causal-authority admission preserves the determinism requirement of AetherMesh; (P2) revocation is monotone and can be recorded without coordination, but leaves an irreducible exposure window.   Status: Architectural Hypothesis Under Investigation (v0.1.0). No implementation is claimed. No real-world deployment has been evaluated. F1–F4 are not falsified by argument, with residual weaknesses. F5 (observable benefit) is untested. The final project structure (single, dual, or triple project) is undetermined. The paper is not peer reviewed.   Links: - Zenodo DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24054524 - OSF Registration: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/TAHC8 - OSF Project: https://osf.io/we2tm - Official Website: https://aethergovern.netlify.app - GitHub: https://github.com/gitdeeper15/aethergovern - ORCID: https://orcid.org/0009-0003-8903-0029

summary: Exact-diagonalization (ED) time evolution of the charge-density-wave quench in an 11-site open Hubbard chain (initial state DD0DD0DD0DD, N↑ = N↓ = 8), following the setup of Figs 2–3 of Schroedter, Bonitz & Joost, arXiv:2606.10773. These are independent computations; no values were taken or digitized from the paper. Data CC-BY 4.0, code MIT.

summary: I propose that wanting is shaped through the ways other people affect one’s existence. I retain two versions as the heart of the argument. The strong version claims that all desire content is socially imparted; the moderate version sets bare bodily states partly aside and concerns the content and strength of socially shaped wants. Needs lean toward bodily action and impulse, while wants lean toward thought-shaped objects and possibilities; this distinction is conceptual, not an established biological partition. I call the felt interpersonal draw pull and the proposed influence imparted force, without claiming a new physical force. Research on goal contagion, valuation, comparison, and social support motivates the account but does not establish that social shaping is total. I distinguish experienced connection from evidence of reciprocity, compatibility, or safety, and being influenced from freely endorsing a course of action. Eight predictions and two proposed studies address observable consequences, including the limits of tracing a desire’s source. A background glossary preserves my existing terminology without using it to explain away contrary results. A brief universe/fabric analogy remains philosophical speculation. No new data are reported.
title: Desire as Imparted Force: A Social-Origin Hypothesis of Wanting and Connection
