The first (“Faith, Unbelief”) examines the essence of man and the meaning of life outside the categories of good and evil: questions of immortality, of imperfection as a source of striving, of reason, of freedom of choice and of the idea of the Creator. The main conclusion of this part is that the principle of life is preserved regardless of what a person believes in. The second part (“Spirit and Matter”) draws on the physical model of the work “The Birth of Dimensions: A Formal Skeleton” and draws analogies between the physical and the spiritual: consciousness is considered as a resonant structure that cannot be reduced to matter but is inseparably connected with it. Consciousness and matter appear as different frequency manifestations of a single process, which suggests a possible way of overcoming the traditional opposition of the “spiritual” and the “material”. The structure of the observer, the connection between consciousness and the brain, the soul, attention and the role of life as the medium in which the observer develops are discussed. The work is interdisciplinary and hypothetical in character and is open to critical analysis. Revision dated 2026-11-10: The chapter “Man and Woman” now specifies what the reverse combination of roles means and what price the system pays for the rearrangement; it adds that roles can intertwine: a woman as muse gives the impulse, and a man gives birth to an idea or a work — birth passes to the next level. These roles are not tied to sex and must be balanced by the manifestation of our phase.     Размышления: ВЕРА, НЕВЕРИЕ. ДУХ и МАТЕРИЯ. Скрынник Сергей Николаевич Республика Казахстан, г. Алматы, science@ast-1c.kz Аннотация Настоящая работа представляет собой философско-теоретическое исследование, направленное на построение целостной модели реальности, объединяющей физические и субъективные аспекты бытия. Она является исходной, «манифестной» частью цикла из одиннадцати статей; именно здесь впервые сформулированы идеи, развитые в последующих работах. Работа состоит из двух частей. В первой («Вера, неверие») рассматриваются суть человека и смысл жизни вне категорий добра и зла: вопросы бессмертия, несовершенства как источника стремления, разума, свободы выбора и идеи Создателя. Основной вывод части — принцип жизни сохраняется независимо от того, во что верит человек. Вторая часть («Дух и материя») опирается на физическую модель работы «Рождение измерений: формальный скелет» и проводит аналогии между физическим и духовным: сознание рассматривается как резонансная структура, не сводимая к материи, но неразрывно связанная с ней. Сознание и материя предстают как различные частотные проявления единого процесса, что предлагает возможный путь к преодолению традиционного противопоставления «духовного» и «материального». Обсуждаются структура наблюдателя, связь сознания и мозга, душа, внимание и роль жизни как среды развития наблюдателя. Работа носит междисциплинарный и гипотетический характер и открыта для критического анализа. Правки от 10.11.2026:  В главе «Мужчина и женщина» уточнено, что такое обратная комбинация ролей и какую цену система платит за перестановку; добавлено, что роли могут переплетаться: женщина-муза даёт импульс, а мужчина рождает идею или произведение — рождение переходит на следующий уровень. Эти роли не закре
title: Reflections: BELIEF, DISBELIEF. SPIRIT and MATTER.

summary: Pyralysis (PYthon Radio Astronomy anaLYSis and Image Synthesis) is an open-source Python library for radio-interferometric simulation, gridding, and image reconstruction. Imaging is stated as an explicit optimization problem — chi-squared (and closure / bispectrum terms) plus regularizers you choose — solved with modern first-order methods (e.g. FISTA, L-BFGS, SDMM). It is not a black-box CLEAN imager.

summary: Museum of One working paper · Version 1.0 · 10 November 2026 · 16 pages · 21 references A work can retain its title and historical date even when its materials, arrangement, or means of presentation have changed. This working paper examines four Korean archival and museum cases: Kim Yong-Ik’s Plane Object photographs and the history of “plain” and “place”; the differing production years assigned to Park Suk-won’s Jeok–Eungnyeok; the 1975 historical reference and 2016 materials of Lee Kang-so’s Untitled 75031; and Kim Kulim’s Mediator, used by the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea, to exemplify compound dating. MMCA’s acquisition narrative and publication guidance acknowledge remaking as part of collecting an experimental past. The paper reads that institutional practice alongside scholarship on the relations among images, material traces, and artwork identity. Aga Wielocha’s discussion of Danh Vo’s chandeliers provides a particularly revealing comparison: a title can date an object’s removal and transformation into art rather than its fabrication, just as a museum’s leading year can identify an earlier work rather than the age of its present components. These different histories require the event dated by each title or caption to remain explicit. Neither artist authorisation nor institutional recognition settles every claim about an earlier condition. The paper credits the overlapping demonstrations in the author’s Relational Archival Investigation papers and develops their implications for collecting, editorial preference, and historical inference. Its contribution is a comparative account of how names and dates sustain continuity without making the evidence for that continuity interchangeable. Evidence limits. The source base is documentary. Physical artworks, original versos, complete printing proofs and object-specific acquisition and conservation dossiers remain unexamined. Park’s two published dates establish a discrepancy without determining the original year or a sequence of database changes. A shared series title cannot identify an individual Kim Yong-Ik work. The eight- and ten-image accounts do not establish a sequence of additions to Lee’s work. Jung Eun Young is cited through the published abstracts. The four selected cases establish no national rate of discrepancy. This working paper has not undergone independent peer review. Relationship to Relational Archival Investigation. The RAI main paper , Documentary Supplement and Extended Case Studies already report the shared naming and date comparisons, the limits of series-title identification, and the difference between Lee’s photographic accounts. This paper extends that work through MMCA’s acquisition narrative and compound dating of Mediator , a sustained comparison with Korean scholarship and conservation research, and analysis of what later objects and records establish about earlier works. Its bibliography points to the cited OSF file versions. 김용익(평면 오브제), 박석원(적-응력), 이강소(무제 75031), 김구림(매개항)의 사례를 통해 한국 실험미술에서 작품의 제목과 연대, 재제작, 소장 기록이 어떤 역사적 주장을 뒷받침하는지 살핀다. 작품의 역사적 정체성과 현존 구성 요소의 제작 시기를 구분하며, 네 사례의 자료 범위와 기존 RAI 연구와의 관계를 명시한다.

summary: Manuscript and CSV data behind the figures and tables of Xu (2021), Halo mass functions from maximum entropy distributions in collisionless dark matter flow, arXiv: 2110.09676 . Contents: the manuscript (PDF) and 19 CSV files with the data of the figures and of the tables that are generated from the simulation data. Companion datasets: doi:10.5281/zenodo.6541231 (Part I, halo-based statistics) and doi:10.5281/zenodo.6757654 (Part II, correlation-based statistics). The earlier record of this work is zenodo.org/records/6640325 . Major findings (friends-of-friends halos of a cosmological N-body simulation, z = 0 unless stated): The velocity distribution that maximises the entropy of a self-gravitating collisionless system (the X distribution) is a scale mixture of Gaussians of halo groups; without halo motion its mixing distribution is exactly the generalised inverse Gaussian distribution H∞. H∞ is a maximum entropy distribution only for potential exponent n = 0, not for gravity. A Gaussian mixture built from the measured halo-particle dispersions reproduces the velocity distribution of the halo particles to 0.03 dex (rms over |v| < 6σ 0 ) and its kurtosis (5.10 against 5.12), yet no halo particle has a total dispersion below 0.51σ 0 ², where H∞ places 0.28–0.34 of the particles. For any halo velocity dispersion bounded away from zero, the exact equation for the mass function has no solution; its push-forward solution leaves a fraction 0.27 of the mixture unassigned. The simulated mass function in ν = σ v ²/σ̄ h ² is described by the two-parameter P form with rms 0.18 in ln f, comparable to the fitted double-λ (0.18) and Sheth–Tormen (0.21) forms. The mass function is not independent of redshift: the mean ν rises from 0.56 at z = 2 to 1.14 at z = 0.
title: Halo mass functions from maximum entropy distributions in collisionless dark matter flow

summary: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) rollouts interleave model reasoning with tool calls in persistent workspaces. Scaling these rollouts incurs substantial memory costs for concurrent environments, while slow tool calls delay entire rollout batches. We present BunshinRL, an agentic RL rollout system that exploits shared environment state and recurring tool calls through three techniques: memory sharing across environments, tool-prefix caching, and speculative tool execution. These techniques build on BunshinFork, a novel live whole-workspace forking mechanism for containers. BunshinFork reconstructs process trees, shares memory copy-on-write, and preserves file, communication, and GUI state, enabling cached-state reuse and rollback after incorrect speculation. We implement BunshinRL and BunshinFork through Linux kernel module and CRIU modifications. BunshinRL reduces peak memory by up to 43%, total memory consumption by up to 51%, and end-to-end rollout latency by 23%.
title: BunshinRL: Splitting Live Agent Workspaces for Memory-Efficient Agentic RL

Breaking: predictions are no longer stored in the project, new recipes drop the Savitzky-Golay edges, and the score plot needs models fitted with this version (older runs show a placeholder until refitted). Install with uv add enginir or pip install enginir (Python 3.12 or newer). Documentation: https://enginir.readthedocs.io Added Choosing the number of components: every PLS and PCR model stores its component curve (RMSECV with standard error, Q², Q²(cum), R²X, R²Y against the number of components, computed with the model's folds), and project.fit(..., n_components="auto") chooses the number by a rule ( one_se by default, min_rmsecv , q2_limit ); model.component_curve , enginir.validation.choose_components , PLSRegression/PCR.predict_components . Fit statistics and training diagnostics of every model: RMSEE and adjusted R² (per pixel and per ROI), CoeffCS, Hotelling T² and DModX of every training pixel with their limits. Model runs store the projection data they need ( prediction_model : x_mean , x_std , rotations , loadings , score_variances , s0 , limits); models fitted before have no maps until they are fitted again. Prediction.dmodx_map , .t2_map , .diagnostics , .provenance . Wavelength warning at prediction: when the scan and the model both have a real wavelength axis and they differ, the prediction logs a warning with the largest difference and records it in provenance["wavelength_warning"] (Predict summary: Wavelengths ); it never blocks or changes the prediction. enginir.prediction.wavelength_mismatch . Viewer: Layer selector in the Predict map (Prediction, DModX, T²) with the pixels above the limit marked, and the applicability summary. summary: The World on Record Index (TWR) — version 1.2.0 Released 9 November 2026. Concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23997606 resolves to the latest version. What is new: the sector layer 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 published one score per country-year. This release adds  goal_level  — one score per country-year  per SDG goal  — so the measure can say  what  a government stopped reporting, not only that it reported less. Sixteen goals are scored.  Goal 7 is not : it has three series, too few to identify a factor. That is a structural fact about the goal, not a judgement on it. Each goal is a  separate  unidimensional 2PL fit on that goal's own series, drawn from the same 524 that build the overall index. A goal's score therefore owes nothing to the other fifteen, and both layers sit on the same scale. The layer is not a restatement of the overall index. Across the sixteen goals a median of  64%  of the variation in goal-level reporting is not explained by a country's overall level — from 18% for goal 17 to 99.9% for goal 15. What it is checked against Check Result Convergence 16 of 16 goals, 19–73 EM cycles each Reliability 0.772–0.953, median  0.844 ; every goal above 0.70 Median posterior SD 0.338 (overall index: 0.114) Bootstrap, 500 replicates 0 failed replicates ; sampling SD is 7–42% of the posterior SE, median 13% Held-out series Fit on 70% of a goal's series, predict the held-out 30%: median AUC  0.725  against a per-series permutation null at  0.500 The bootstrap result means the published standard errors are  conservative  — they already cover item-parameter uncertainty with room to spare. Report the posterior SE, not the bootstrap SD. The held-out test is the first direct check that a goal score predicts reporting it was not fitted on. Thirteen of sixteen goals score 0.649 or better. The three weakest — goal 17 (0.618), goal 15 (0.526) and goal 6 (0.479) — are precisely the three already set apart on content grounds, which the test did not know. Disclose, do not gate Every goal fitted is published.  Nothing is excluded for imprecision, and 0.70 (Nunnally) is reported as a reference point, not applied as a cut. Each goal ships with four numbers a reader can weigh it by: reliability  — 0.772 to 0.953 se_median  — the typical error bar on that goal's scores weight_top5_pct  — how concentrated the score is in its five heaviest series weight_agency_pct  — how much of the score rests on series the custodian agency produces rather than the country Two goals carry  release = hold_content . The hold is on  content  grounds and for  different reasons , never on precision: Goal 6  is largely satellite measurement of lakes, wetlands and river flow. "Reported" there mostly records whether an agency published a dataset, not a country's choice. Goal 15  is overwhelmingly country-produced, but a third of its series are treaty and policy instruments (Nagoya Protocol, Aichi targets, NBSAP), which may track commitment status rather than reporting effort. An error bar cannot warn a reader about either, so the flag travels with the data. Both goals are published in full. Known limitations Weight concentration.  Within a goal, small groups of series that are always reported together can carry much of the score — in goal 10 the five heaviest series carry 80%, in goal 1 75%. These groups are near-duplicates that the variant rule does not collapse, because they are not reported identically: in goal 1, India, Sri Lanka and Malaysia report the education and health breakdowns but never the aggregate, every year from 2015 to 2023. Collapsing them would erase those reporting choices, so they are disclosed in  weight_top5_pct  instead. Modelling the dependence directly is deferred. Provenance.   weight_agency_pct  records h
title: The World on Record: statistical reporting across countries, policy sectors, and time

summary: Did the places that lost most men in the First World War turn to Labour? The question runs through accounts of Labour's replacement of the Liberals, and studies of Italy and Germany link local war losses to post-war radicalism, but its link to party support has not been tested for Britain, where there is no record of deaths, or map of seats, at constituency level. I link 717,287 First World War names on community memorials in the Imperial War Museums' War Memorials Register, counted once per place, to every Great Britain constituency contest from 1906 to 1924, using 176 county and borough units as a common geography, and test hypotheses fixed before any outcome model was run. Contrary to the radicalisation hypothesis, a one standard deviation higher memorial rate (22 names per 1,000 electors of 1918) is associated with a 2.9 percentage point smaller Labour gain between December 1910 and 1918 (95% CI 0.1 to 5.7; p=0.040; Holm-adjusted across four primary outcomes p=0.16; N=131). The gap widens to 4.8 points by 1922, mirrored by Liberal resilience, and is not present in pre-war changes in six placebo tests. All 21 robustness variants give negative estimates, but only 8 have intervals excluding zero. Exploratory analysis points to where Labour fielded candidates. The design is correlational: recorded losses track volunteering and occupational structure, for which no data exist here. The data do not support a larger Labour advance where recorded losses were heavier; the negative association itself is modest and should be treated as suggestive. Interactive version: https://maps.tristanhotham.com/war-dead-labour/ . Data and code: https://github.com/Tristan-Hotham/war-dead-labour . Blog post: https://blog.tristanhotham.com/2026/10/31/war-dead-labour/ . Sources: Imperial War Museums War Memorials Register (non-commercial reuse); general election results from UK Parliament (Open Parliament Licence v3.0), matched to Wikidata; ONS boundaries (OGL v3). Text, figures and derived data CC BY-NC 4.0 (the register's terms); code MIT.
title: The War Dead and the Rise of Labour: First World War Memorial Names and the British Vote, 1910 to 1924

summary: CRISPR-TRIAGE is an open-science computational biology research archive evaluating parameter-efficient off-target prioritization under budget-constrained experimental validation budgets (K <= 50). This package contains the complete trained model checkpoints, multi-seed training pipelines (5 random seeds), biophysical feature extractors, pre-registered baseline models (LightGBM GBDT, Pairwise 1D-CNN, Logistic Regression, crispAI architecture), and evaluation results across two external cellular benchmarks (Listgarten 2018 GUIDE-seq and K562 cellular compilation). Key Scientific Findings & Methodological Disclosure: Algorithmic Parity with Gradient Boosted Trees: On the deduplicated independent cellular benchmark (K562 retrospective multi-assay compilation from DeepCRISPR / Yang et al. 2023; 11 guides, 16,172 unique candidate pairs, 110 confirmed positive guide-target sequence pairs without genomic coordinates), standard gradient boosting (LightGBM GBDT) trained on 15 simple biophysical mismatch features achieves Macro Recall@20 = 0.6350 vs 0.6416 for CRISPR-TRIAGE (margin +0.0066 / +0.66%; paired Wilcoxon W = 18.0, p = 1.0000; 95% bootstrap CI [-0.0979, +0.0900]). LightGBM runs 2.39x faster with 0 neural parameters. While lack of statistically significant superiority does not prove biological equivalence or disprove neural-network utility, the empirical evidence failed to reject the null hypothesis of no difference vs LightGBM under available statistical power. Multi-Seed Volatility in CRISPR Modeling: Retraining across 5 independent random seeds reveals substantial Macro Recall@20 fluctuations (+-6.5% standard deviation on identical data), demonstrating that single-seed reporting in the CRISPR machine-learning literature frequently reflects random seed-selection noise rather than genuine algorithmic superiority. Dataset Deduplication Importance: Forensic auditing documented the impact of 1,613 duplicate candidate rows (and 2 duplicate confirmed positive sites) in the K562 compilation, showing how uncleaned duplicates distort evaluation metrics. Two-Tier Reproducibility Scope: Tier 1 (Saved-Model Inference & K562 Cellular Benchmark Reproduction): 100% self-contained in this archive. All 5 trained seed weights, baselines, scalers, predictions, metric summaries, and the K562 cellular cohort execute fully offline without internet access. Tier 2 (Full Retraining on Primary Assay Datasets): Full retraining from raw sequence reads and complete Listgarten raw dataset reproduction requires separately downloading the 4 un-subsampled raw assay datasets (>20MB each), registered with authoritative accessions and cryptographic SHA256 checksums in DATA_MANIFEST.csv. Licensing, Provenance & Third-Party Rights: CRISPR-TRIAGE code, models, and documentation are licensed under the permissive MIT License. The crispAI architecture code (src/crispai_official/) is under MIT License (Copyright 2023 Furkan Ozden; reference: Özden & Minary, NAR 2024). Pretrained third-party weights for crispAI are omitted from the archive to ensure compliance with conflicting upstream documentation, with archive extraction utilities provided for the authors' official Zenodo records (13335960 / 12609337). Bundled K562 benchmark datasets are distributed under CC BY 4.0 (Yang et al. CSBJ 2023; Chuai et al. Genome Biol 2018). Raw CFD scoring lookup matrices (Doench et al. 2016 Supplementary Table 19) are strictly omitted from the release archive for third-party rights compliance; tested user-side acquisition and verification utilities are provided via scripts/download_cfd_matrices.py. See the root LICENSE file for full details.
title: CRISPR-TRIAGE: Evaluation of Parameter-Efficient Bi-Modal Off-Target Prioritization Under Budget-Constrained Screening

summary: Health Building Lifestyle Guidelines (2026 Comprehensive Edition) is a practical, referenced, comprehensive guideline for lay readers and health professionals. It BUILDS ON, and does NOT rename, replace or supersede, the 2025 Health Building Lifestyle Guidelines (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.15814357, 5 July 2025). The main PDF is a 9-page LANDSCAPE BROCHURE with enlarged body type throughout, one topic per page and clickable links. It reproduces the 2025 guideline IN FULL (English, Hindi and its own reference list) on pages 2-4, each captioned with the 2025 DOI; the 12 reference URLs on reproduced page 4 are live links as well. The Title uses a SINGLE ACLM blue header in two lines, and EVERY URL link in the brochure uses that same deep blue. The three PURE traffic-light colours appear as three disks on page 1 (the 21-point key) and on ALL content headers (Spices = YELLOW, Yoga = RED); the Six-pillars page carries the brighter original ACLM six-pillar chips, with published ACLM pillar language in roman type, the 2025 21-item guideline in italics, and an explicit attribution footnote. Two images from the Sutra Health YouTube channel (infusion, Yoga) sit on the right of their pages. Page 8 is one merged evidence table listing the CONDITIONS for which there is evidence and THE PRACTICES THAT WORKS, colour-coded PREVENTION / TREATMENT / REMISSION-REVERSAL (refs [30] DiRECT, [31] Ornish), followed by two selected meta-analyses on prevention ([32] Kyu, [33] Reynolds); the separate evidence pages and the redundant Safety page were consolidated into it. summary: Factoring and supply chain finance (SCF) allow firms, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises, to obtain liquidity against receivables and other trade assets, but they expose financiers to the credit risk of suppliers, buyers and their relationships. This study maps the scientific literature on credit risk management in factoring and SCF through a bibliometric analysis. A Scopus search conducted on 12 October 2026 and screening following the PRISMA 2020 flow yielded 288 articles and reviews published between 1995 and 2025. Performance analysis was combined with science mapping in VOSviewer, including keyword co-occurrence, country co-authorship and co-citation analyses of references and sources. The results show that the field has grown rapidly since 2019, with 87.2% of the documents published in 2019–2025. China dominates research output, while studies from the United Kingdom, the United States and Italy attain higher normalised impact, and operations management and operational research journals are the main publication venues. Three research streams are identified: analytical operations–finance models of risk allocation in capital-constrained supply chains, conceptual and empirical research on SCF adoption and reverse factoring, and machine learning-based credit risk assessment of SMEs. Research attention has shifted from traditional factoring and receivables financing towards SCF, machine learning, blockchain and, most recently, artificial intelligence and sustainability. The accounting, financial reporting and internal control dimensions of these arrangements, the allocation of risk among multiple financiers, and evidence from under-represented regions emerge as the main gaps.
tags: factoring, supply chain finance, credit risk management, reverse factoring, bibliometric analysis, VOSviewer.
title: CREDIT RISK MANAGEMENT IN FACTORING AND SUPPLY CHAIN FINANCE: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS OF SCIENTIFIC PUBLICATIONS

summary: We study cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) problems in which agents evolve under decoupled noisy dynamics but share a population objective. A canonical example is a mobility operator that orchestrates a fleet of vehicles to meet customer demand. The stochastic and time-varying nature of these problems calls for learning approaches, yet existing MARL algorithms do not scale: learning assignment and routing jointly over the full state-action space becomes prohibitive as the number of agents grows. Formulating the problem over the space of probability measures, we prove a separation principle: the population cost-to-go function is upper bounded by an optimal transport problem whose transportation cost is the target-conditioned single-agent cost-to-go function. This simplifies the multi-agent problem to learning a single-agent policy and coordinating the agents via optimal transport. Building on this principle, we introduce SALT (Separation-based Assignment and Learning via optimal Transport), a family of algorithms that learn a target-conditioned single-agent policy using any standard reinforcement learning algorithm, and then coordinate the agents via optimal transport. Since learning occurs at the single-agent level, SALT scales to fleet sizes where MARL baselines become intractable and transfers without retraining to fleet sizes unseen during training. In a vehicle-delivery experiment on the southern Manhattan road network, where MARL baselines are computationally prohibitive, SALT improves travel time by 15-21% over a shortest-path routing heuristic. In stochastic grid worlds, SALT reduces average travel times by 23-61% relative to MARL baselines and scales to population sizes where these methods fail.
title: A Separation Principle for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

summary: LLMs excel at language tasks, but long-meeting QFS remains difficult due to complex speaker dynamics, sparse key information, and limited data. Meetings involve disfluencies, long transcripts and complex discourse. QFS have high risk of information omission, hallucination, even for advanced models such as GPT-4-mini and Gemini. Existing end-to-end methods compress retrieval, evidence extraction, and summary generation into a single pass, failing to handle the complex reasoning required for targeted meeting summaries. We propose ReSUM, a modular multi-LLM framework coordinated by a planner that orchestrates retrieval and summarization agents. By distilling teacher reasoning into query- and plan-conditioned retrievers and summarizers, ReSUM enhances long-context robustness, minimizes irrelevant exploration, and generates more faithful and comprehensive query-focused summaries. Experiments show consistent gains on query-focused meeting summarization benchmarks.
title: ReSUM: Reasoning-Driven Multi-Agent Framework for Query-Focused Summarization

summary: Geometric assembly requires fine spatiotemporal coordination to place parts without causing collisions or deadlocks under tight clearances. To address this, we present an object-centric reinforcement learning framework that treats each part as an agent and learns a shared policy for continuous assembly control. A graph neural network represents the pieces, their target poses, and their spatial relationships, and predicts translational and angular velocities for each component. Per-agent proximal policy optimization with a centralized graph critic directly learns motion and temporal coordination within a single feedback policy. We study this formulation through planar Tangram assembly, where pieces must slide and rotate into a given configuration while remaining on the assembly surface. Procedural generation of target configurations and randomized initial arrangements support training and evaluation across diverse assembly problems. Our experiments isolate the roles of relational structure and multi-agent optimization, and compare learned control with sampling-based planning. We demonstrate concurrent assembly in simulation and transfer the policy to sequential execution on a real robot, as our object-centric formulation decouples learned assembly coordination from low-level physical control. Project page: https://tangrambench.org/
title: It Takes Two to Tangram: Multi-Agent Object Centric Reinforcement Learning for Assembly

summary: Conversational recommender systems often treat user sessions in isolation, limiting their ability to capture how user intent evolves over time. While large language models (LLMs) have improved semantic understanding, they are typically used as isolated components, without addressing how memory, retrieval, and decision-making should be integrated at the system level. In this work, we propose a memory-aware multi-agent architecture for conversational recommendation, in which LLMs act as orchestration layers that coordinate intent refinement, query construction, and interaction flow. A key design principle is the integration of long-term memory as a first-class component, influencing both routing decisions and semantic query formation. We evaluate the system through cross-session memory experiments, multi-turn conversational simulations, and supervisor-driven interaction studies on the Amazon Reviews dataset. Results show that memory-enabled interactions recover up to 63\% of the gap toward explicit-query scenarios and prevent semantic degradation in extended dialogues. In addition, supervisory orchestration increases user acceptance by +28.9 percentage points, highlighting the importance of structured orchestration in guiding interaction and output quality. We also observe an exposure bottleneck between retrieved candidates and displayed recommendations. While LLM-reranking does not improve Hit@K, it consistently enhances semantic consistency and diversity. To capture these effects, we introduce the Semantic Consistency Score (SCS), a complementary evaluation measure. Overall, the results emphasize the importance of system-level design choices, suggesting that effective conversational recommendation benefits from explicit memory integration, orchestration, and evaluation beyond traditional ranking metrics.
title: Memory-Aware Multi-Agent Architecture with LLM-based Orchestration for Conversational Recommendation

summary: Groups can achieve more than individuals in the same amount of time, but only if their members coordinate: they must decide who works on what and what to share. However, this organization in multi-agent systems today usually comes from arbitrary, static harnesses designed a priori without adapting to agent behaviors or task specifications. We ask whether agents can instead learn to organize themselves. We introduce s$^3$, the first multi-agent reinforcement learning method in which agents decide for themselves how long to work alone and when to share findings or read teammates' messages, with no predefined organization or roles. Our s$^3$ agents learn to take different approaches, read each other's work, exhibit emergent roles that complement each other in the swarm, and generalize to bigger teams. We study both coordination, where agents must combine private information, and parallel exploration, where sharing discoveries can make search more efficient. With matched training and inference budgets, s$^3$, swarms evaluated with twice as many agents as in training solve over 25$\times$ more coordination problems than the strongest baseline, and in exploration, communicating agents reduce repeated work by nearly 50% and outperform best-of-N by up to 9.4 percentage points. Rather than being designed in advance, s$^3$ enables organization to emerge from a shared goal. This opens the door to capable systems built from many models that learn to work together.
title: s$^3$: Simple Scaling of Swarms via Cooperative Multi-agent RL

summary: Version 1.0.0 research artifact for JISA-N03. The archive provides selected original packet captures, native command/state observations, independent receiver records, retained failure evidence and standard-library Python scripts for offline reanalysis of packet-size validation under different probe orders. The first qualification retains six trials, twelve related phases, sixty service probes, forty-five intact receiver records and twelve separate capture fences. The follow-up retains twelve fresh histories, twenty-four service transfers, seventeen intact receiver records and twelve separate fences. Its designed pairs distinguish TCP-before-UDP from UDP-before-TCP in routed IPv4 and IPv4-in-IPv4 paths, with correct-static-limit and blocked-feedback controls. The default offline command verifies selected input bytes and regenerates reported structures and three figure sources using 27 scientific comparisons. An optional local TeX/Poppler command reconstructs the three PDF figures. The English README maps folders, fields and units, prerequisites, exact commands, expected outcomes, retained failures and limits. No network, account, administrator privilege, model, GPU or experimental infrastructure is needed for default reproduction. Native source is included for method inspection and is not executed by the reproduction command. One realization per designed order cell, bounded observations and shared parsing do not establish population reliability, an exclusive kernel/cache cause, a new discovery protocol or a selector advantage. Third-party tools retain their own licenses and executables are not redistributed. No manuscript, reference-paper library, internal editorial/AI history, governance, cache or access credential is included.
title: Probe-order effects on packet-size validation in routed and encapsulated Linux paths: research artifact

summary: Overview The Earth Surface Anomaly dataset (v1.0) is a five-class, event-grouped Sentinel-2 benchmark for immediate disaster and surface-anomaly detection. It contains 622 samples grouped into 46 event or spatiotemporal observation units (17 source-named/inventory units and 29 observation groups, 2017–2025, globally distributed): 129 fire, 58 flood-context, 54 landslide, 204 crop-residue-burning and 177 retrogressive-thaw-slump samples. 595 samples carry source polygon-derived binary masks; 27 carry weak point inventories only; all 54 landslide samples include pre/post paired observations. Industrial heat sources (208 candidates) are excluded from this release and 17 visually ambiguous candidates are withheld, both enumerated in quality/excluded_samples.csv . Sample structure Each sample ( data/CODE/EVENT/SAMPLE/ ) provides a six-band Sentinel-2 L2A chip (declared bands B2, B3, B4, B8, B11, B12; aligned grid spacing does not imply native 10 m for every band), a 0/1 binary mask, RGB/NIR/SWIR previews, annotation.json and measured facts.json (CRS, transform, WGS84 bounds, geometry statistics, spectral indices, SHA256 checksums). Annotation-conditioned vision-language tasks (4–6 per sample depending on label strength and pairing) cover event classification, factual captioning, spatial reasoning, visual grounding, spectral comparison, and for suitable samples temporal reasoning and label provenance. Splits Group splits are precomputed: default splits/event_disjoint (443/102/77 train/val/test) and inherited splits/site_disjoint (433/114/75). Event-disjointness does not guarantee site-disjointness (1 measured case); use site_disjoint when required. Never randomly split patches from the same event. Screening and quality All 639 non-industrial candidates underwent AI-assisted visual screening of RGB, SWIR and target crops with review sheets and per-sample geometry/text audits retained in the release ( quality/ , visual_review.csv ). This is not independent expert pixel adjudication, field validation, or new external verification of every event identity. Limitations (documented in README, README_zh and DATA_DICTIONARY) Flood-context masks often follow existing river channels; no paired baseline establishes incremental inundation. Fire annotations can cover smoke, scars or hotspots and are not universally burned-area boundaries. Crop-residue burning is a source label; imagery alone does not establish fuel identity. Thaw mechanism/onset and landslide onset cannot be established from the supplied views alone. Point inventories (27 samples) are weak localization, not segmentation truth; polygon provenance does not guarantee exact pixel boundaries. Radiometric scale/offset and the inherited non-landslide band mapping have not been independently traced to every source product; facts.json indices are stored-DN calculations, not validated physical reflectance. External event-match references in index/external_verification_ledger.csv were not newly re-verified during release preparation. summary: Overview The Earth Surface Anomaly dataset (v1.0) is a five-class, event-grouped Sentinel-2 benchmark for immediate disaster and surface-anomaly detection. summary: Data and code for the manuscript "Auditing source dependence in clinical variant interpretation benchmarks" (under peer review).   The archive (one zip file) contains the frozen inputs (ClinGen Evidence Repository records retrieved on 29 August 2026; GeneBe output captured on 29 August 2026, reduced to the applied criteria with strengths, point sums and verdicts; ClinVar review status; per-variant extracts of ten annual ClinVar GRCh38 archives, 2017-2025), a per-variant identifier table (ClinGen Allele Registry and ClinVar identifiers, GRCh38 coordinates, HGVS descriptions), per-variant and per-target result tables, source masks, the historical-archive and source-intervention outputs for BIAS-2015 and InterVar, the BRCA2, LDLR and GCK functional extensions, the pre-registration of the temporal analysis, and the analysis, verification and figure code with replay instructions.   README.md maps the folders to the analyses and gives the commands that reproduce the results. MANIFEST_SHA256.tsv lists the size and SHA-256 of every file. THIRD_PARTY_SOURCES.md identifies the third-party code and data that were used but are not redistributed (BIAS-2015, InterVar, raw ClinVar releases, author functional datasets) by location, version and SHA-256.   Only public, de-identified variant records are included; there are no patient data.   Files are restricted during peer review; reviewers receive an access link through the journal's submission system. The files will be made public on publication.   Version v14 replaces the contents of version v13, which accompanied an earlier manuscript; the frozen inputs are byte-identical to those in v13.
title: Data and code for: Auditing source dependence in clinical variant interpretation benchmarks

summary: Attention to notable people rises sharply when they die and then fades, but how far it fades, and for whom, has rarely been measured at scale. I follow the English Wikipedia articles of 16,397 people who died between 2016 and 2023 (a 30% hash sample of Wikidata), measuring monthly user pageviews (looking someone up, not remembering them) as a share of all English Wikipedia traffic relative to each person's own level in the year before death. In an analysis pre-specified in a written plan, the median peak is 16.5 times the pre-death level. The decay is best described by two phases, with half-lives of about 11 days and 6.9 months, although a power law predicts later cohorts slightly better. Two to three years after death, the median person receives 0.98 (95% CI 0.97 to 0.99) of their pre-death share; an exploratory comparison with the drift before death places this about 5% above a no-death path. Age at death is the strongest correlate: people who died under 50 retain 63% more long-run attention than those who died at 65 to 79 (95% CI 51 to 77), a gap absent at a placebo date and present in all 21 robustness checks. Performers are the only occupational group whose typical attention settles above its baseline, but placebo tests show that the occupational gaps partly predate the deaths. Estimates for women and for citizens of English-speaking countries depend on specification and are not robust. The design is descriptive and observational. Interactive version: https://maps.tristanhotham.com/fame-half-life/ . Data and code: https://github.com/Tristan-Hotham/fame-half-life . Blog post: https://blog.tristanhotham.com/2026/10/31/fame-half-life/ . Sources: English Wikipedia pageviews (Wikimedia pageviews API, CC0); Wikidata (CC0); Natural Earth (public domain). Text, figures and data CC BY 4.0; code MIT.
title: The Half-Life of Fame: How Attention to Notable People on English Wikipedia Rises and Decays after Their Deaths

summary: Version 1.8.4 carries the manuscript as resubmitted after the major revision and pairs with code tag v1.1.2 . It adds an ethics statement on the independent annotators to the manuscript (Section 3.9 and the Declarations) and updates expected.json for the new results archive. All data, results, code and reproduce.py are unchanged from version 1.8.3; only the manuscript files in the results archive differ. Version 1.8.3 (superseded by 1.8.4) carries the manuscript as resubmitted after the major revision and pairs with code tag v1.1.2 . Release identities are now also classified with tag evidence from the time of each change: an archive visit or an immutable release dates a tag binding, while a mutable release record does not ( reports/release_timing.json , release-timing-v2). The matched-control comparison covers months 13-18 ( reports/control_comparison.json ), and reports/revision_checks.json adds the tail window after day 540, the repository-month units of the repository share, commit-level ratios of the second wave and the dependents list against the measured endpoint. The results archive now also holds, under data/ , the cached API responses, stage-freeze scripts, source-frame files and run manifests that the full formal entry point ( python -m pintrace.formal_stats --working ) checks, so it runs from the code tag and the two archives. JOIN_MEASUREMENTS.md corrects the verification directory and the part names and adds a streaming extraction. reproduce.py with expected.json runs the whole reproduction in an empty working directory and compares every output with the archived bytes. The measurement archive is unchanged from version 1.4. Version 1.8.2 (superseded by 1.8.3) carries the manuscript as resubmitted after the major revision: the pipeline's precision and recall by class against the annotators' consensus, the timing of the annotator replacements, the second wave qualified as carried by organization-owned repositories, and corrected denominators. It adds a note on line endings with the list of files whose implementation hashes were recorded with CRLF line endings ( docs/crlf_hashed_files.txt ). The manuscript sources moved to paper/jsep_v2/ . All data and result files are unchanged from version 1.8.1, and the measurement archive is unchanged from version 1.4. Version 1.8.1 carries the final revised manuscript (data and code availability, design history, and wording of the second wave) and adds means to the covariate summaries of the coverage audit. All other data are unchanged from version 1.8.0, and the measurement archive is unchanged from version 1.4. Version 1.8 accompanies the major revision of the manuscript. The results archive adds the dependency-graph coverage audit with its crawl, sample and eligibility records, the stratified sensitivity of the two waves, and the independent two-annotator validation of 400 items (packets, codebook, freeze records, the final annotators' pseudonymous answers, consensus and score). It also archives the cohort baselines, maintenance-scope entries and three table files that these analyses bind. The measurement archive is unchanged from version 1.4. The record contains two archives. pintrace-measurements-v1.tar.zst holds the per-repository measurement snapshots for 457 measured repositories and 301 matched control repositories, the archived upstream release evidence and the matched-control assignments. pintrace-results-v1.tar.zst holds the published result files, the formal-statistics outputs, the 150-item gold set, the research documentation, the manuscript PDF and LaTeX source, and the claim ledger that maps every rendered number to a result file and JSON pointer. Each archive includes a SHA-256 manifest and a README with extraction and reproduction instructions. The measurement files contain repository identifiers but no commit author names, commit messages, e-mail addresses or credentials. The code is at https://github.com/JunjieChen0/PinTrace under the MIT license. Replicatio

summary: arXiv:2109.12244 is the preprint of this work. This record holds the revised paper, the data of its figures and tables, and the fitted profile parameters. Major findings If a halo grows self-similarly, with mass and radius both proportional to time at fixed concentration c, mass conservation fixes the mean radial velocity inside it for any density profile: outward in the core and inward beyond about twice the scale radius. For an NFW halo the net radial momentum vanishes at c 0 = 3.48. Growth adds surface and kinetic terms to the virial balance. At c 0 they give an effective virial exponent n e = −1.42 instead of −1. A halo radius that grows by random accretion events follows geometric Brownian motion. For a simple osmotic flow the particle Fokker–Planck solution is a generalized gamma profile that contains the Einasto profile as a special case. Tested on composite haloes (all haloes with the same particle number, 4–6326 particles) of a 256 3 SCDM simulation, the generalized gamma profile fits the cumulative mass profiles with a median rms residual of 0.006 dex and a r /b r = 1.41 ± 0.05; the flat inner part lies within about one softening length. The measured mean radial velocity is inward at all resolved radii, between −0.39 H r and −1.24 H r, where self-similar growth predicts about +0.53 H r at the scale radius. The radial velocity dispersion exceeds the isotropic Jeans value by 1.11–1.90 times. Self-similar growth describes the profile shapes, but not the instantaneous kinematics, of these haloes. Contents. P21_revised.pdf (the paper) and csv/ (15 files: the data of Figs 2–9, Fig. A1 and the composite-halo fit tables). The dark matter flow statistics of the simulation are in 10.5281/zenodo.6541231 (Part I), 10.5281/zenodo.6757654 (Part II) and 10.5281/zenodo.6586213 (full dataset).
title: Inverse mass cascade in dark matter flow and effects on halo deformation, energy, size, and density profiles

summary: Manuscript and CSV data behind the figures and tables of Xu (2026), Inverse energy cascade in self-gravitating collisionless dark matter flow and effects of halo shape , arXiv:2110.13885 . The earlier data record of this work is zenodo.org/records/6640331 . Contents: the manuscript (P17_revised.pdf) and the folder csv/ with the data plotted in the figures and tables of the paper: subsystem energies, flux functions of the specific energies, halo-group energies and coherent motion, virial ratios and halo shapes at z = 0. The statistics of the simulation are in the dark matter flow datasets, doi:10.5281/zenodo.6541231 and doi:10.5281/zenodo.6757654 , and the full dataset is doi:10.5281/zenodo.6586213 . Major findings (Einstein–de Sitter simulation of 256³ particles): The flux of any specific quantity V through the halo mass scale is ε V = −(μ + λ V − s) M h H⟨V⟩, where M h ∝ a μ is the mass in haloes, ⟨V⟩ ∝ a λ V its mass-weighted mean and s the growth exponent of V in haloes of fixed mass; with the measured exponents it reproduces every energy flux to within 2 per cent at z < 2. Kinetic energy, both of the motion of haloes and of the motion inside them, is carried to larger haloes (inverse cascade), while the inter- and intra-halo potential energies are carried to smaller haloes (direct cascade); the fluxes are independent of halo mass for haloes of up to a few hundred particles, only at z ≤ 0.3. The steady state of the cascade picture, in which M h ∝ a 1/2 and the energies grow as a 3/2 , is not reached by z = 0: M h grows as a 1/2 only near z = 0 (local exponent 0.47), and the total kinetic and potential energies grow as a 1.13 and a 1.19 at z ≈ 0. The simplest steady-state exponents fail for the inter-halo potential and for the radial kinetic energy of the haloes, so the measured exponents are needed in the flux formula. Haloes are elongated, with r λ3 /r λ1 ≈ 2–3, but their moment of inertia exceeds that of a sphere of equal volume only by a median factor 1.60 (1,674,583 haloes at z = 0). The spin axis lies within 30° of the plane perpendicular to the major axis for 70 per cent of haloes with n p ≥ 20 (isotropic: 50 per cent). Shape change therefore cannot drive the energy cascade; mass accretion does.
title: Inverse energy cascade in self-gravitating collisionless dark matter flow and effects of halo shape

summary: Changing an objective does not automatically revise agents' earlier plans or delegated tasks. Acknowledgment can coexist with obsolete execution, while misleading instructions can redirect work or discard retained constraints. We present a Strategic World simulation testbed that separates authoritative objectives, local plans, notice receipt, and consequential action. Six intervention families vary objectives, conditions, authority, membership, and communication. Matched protocols and deadlines establish feasibility for the tested disturbances. Controlled trajectories demonstrate that identical completion and acknowledgment summaries can conceal uninformed obsolete work, obsolete work after receipt, or blocked unsafe intent. Local language-model trials and instructed action probes reveal competence limits that constrain interpretation of dynamic failures. A further 16-episode comparison evaluates an engineered guard that prioritizes pending notice submissions over local work. It completes 4/4 held-out settings, compared with 1/4 for a calibrated assisted baseline. Each episode contains one large language model actor and two fixed peers. These results establish diagnostic distinctions and bounded policy feasibility under explicit simulation assumptions; they do not establish frontier-model reliability or autonomous team adaptation.
title: When the Plan Changes: A Strategic World Testbed for Dynamic Multi-Agent Coordination

summary: LLM-based multi-agent systems solve complex tasks through collaboration, but their growing, simultaneously resident key-value (KV) caches create a memory bottleneck. Applying single-model quantization policies independently ignores differences in agents' precision needs, potentially degrading collective reasoning. We introduce Coordinated Mixed-Precision KV Cache Quantization (CoMixKV), which combines online sensitivity estimation with joint agent-layer bit-width allocation under a shared memory budget. To our knowledge, CoMixKV is the first mixed-precision KV-cache quantization framework to jointly allocate precision across simultaneously resident agent caches under such a budget. The estimator derives sensitivity from a local attention-error bound using recent queries, keys, and values, without calibration data, trial quantization, or additional model passes. A shared controller combines these scores with remaining quantizable capacity and byte-level storage costs to minimize total estimated error. Allocations are refreshed as agents start or finish and new observations become available. Selected widths apply only to newly quantized blocks; recent states retain native precision and previously quantized blocks remain unchanged. Across four benchmarks and three LLM backbones at average 2-bit, 3-bit, and 4-bit settings, CoMixKV achieves strong accuracy against the evaluated quantization baselines. At the average 3-bit setting on Gemma-4-31B-it, it achieves 68.35% average accuracy, exceeding the strongest quantized baseline by 0.59%. On Qwen3-32B, it reduces peak KV-cache memory by 32.08% and achieves a 1.38x inference speedup over FullKV.
title: Coordinated Mixed-Precision KV Cache Quantization for Efficient LLM-based Multi-agent Systems

summary: Local-first security tools let organizations analyze code without sending it to third-party services, but the small language models they can run locally are weaker than hosted ones and are hard to improve without breaching the privacy guarantee that motivates them. We present Tantular Cyber, an open-source, read-only repository security analyzer that keeps deterministic scanner findings authoritative and confines a locally served language model to advisory explanations in Bahasa Indonesia. We report its measured v0.3.0 baseline on a synthetic, ground-truth benchmark: combining Semgrep with an interprocedural call-graph scanner yields precision 0.843 and recall 0.915 (Semgrep alone: 0.818 and 0.766). The advisory layer is the weak point: 57% of explanations met an evidence-grounding check, against 95% for a different 8B model under identical prompts. A forensic re-scoring of retained outputs shows that every grounding failure cites a code identifier absent from the evidence shown, and that a prompt change which appeared to raise grounding from 0.56 to 0.72 did so partly by citing nothing. We document two evaluation-validity hazards we encountered: silent model-file migration during a run and non-reproducible published figures. Building on these lessons and on constraint-aware evaluation from security operations research, we propose a governed self-improvement loop (code-free feedback, curated data, a cheapest-first intervention ladder from prompts to LoRA and weight-space edits, hard gates, and human release approval) and preregister the protocol by which its first cycle will be judged. We report no results for the loop itself.
title: Governed Self-Improvement for a Local-First Security Analyzer: Baseline Measurements and a Preregistered Evaluation Protocol for Tantular Cyber

summary: Visuomotor policies can handle many robot manipulation tasks, but understanding their failures remains difficult. Unfamiliar conditions and small action errors can lead to failure, yet watching the robot alone tells us little about what went wrong inside the policy. We introduce MIND (Mechanistic Interpretability for Neural Diagnosis), a method that looks inside a trained policy to detect failures during execution and identify the internal concepts involved. MIND uses a sparse autoencoder to break down the policy's internal activations into features that can be studied individually. We give meaning to these features by linking their activity to the robot's position, movement, and surroundings, and by steering their activations to examine how they affect the robot's actions. From successful and failed executions, we learn how the features behave on the way to a failure. During execution, MIND flags deviations from these patterns and uses the meaningful features contributing most to the change to describe the problem. Experiments in simulation and on a physical robot show that changes in these internal features help detect and explain failures. By using the same features for detection and diagnosis, MIND connects failure signals to understandable changes inside the policy.
title: Detecting and Explaining Robot Policy Failures from Sparse Internal Features

summary: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are an important tool for fMRI prediction, where empirical functional connectivity matrices serve both as features and for graph construction. However, recent studies and our own experiments show that these methods often fail to outperform simpler graph-agnostic baselines. We propose a statistical explanation for this failure by formulating connectome prediction as an errors-in-variables (EIV) problem: the true connectome is latent, while the observed covariance matrix is a noisy finite-time-series estimate. In a linear asymptotic setting, we decompose the effect of graph convolution into three mechanisms: smoothing-induced bias and variance reduction, graph estimation error, and a double-dipping effect arising when the same noisy matrix determines both graph and features. Under a latent community model adapted to neuroscience, we identify a narrow favorable regime, set by the brain community structure, the predictive signal, the graph construction and the recording length, in which message passing can improve prediction. Simulations validate this decomposition, while real-data experiments illustrate that connectome GNN pipelines often fall outside this regime. Our results provide a first step towards explaining when graph convolutions can help brain connectome prediction, and why they often do not.
title: Bias, Measurement Error, and Double-Dipping: When Can GNN Convolutions Help Brain Connectome Prediction?

summary: Local large language model (LLM) inference is often described as private, verified, or reproducible without separating the technical claims behind those terms. This paper presents Caleta, an Apache-2.0 process supervisor and evidence layer around llama.cpp rather than a new inference engine. Caleta combines versioned manifests, exact-size and SHA-256 verification, controlled backend construction, a restricted OpenAI-compatible proxy, prompt-free execution records, benchmark reports, and a small conformance suite. Its contribution is the composition of these mechanisms into explicit contracts that distinguish integrity from authenticated provenance and privacy controls from operating-system isolation. We evaluate the implementation through static checks, 22 unit tests, deterministic end-to-end tests on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows, and a pinned real-model experiment on Windows CPU using Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct Q4_K_M and llama.cpp b11981. The real experiment validates artifact verification, startup, model listing, non-streaming and server-sent-event chat, and conformance. Three independent benchmark invocations produced fifteen successful warm requests with no failures. In this single configuration, median time to first token was 18.066 ms and median decode throughput was 54.394 tokens/s. These descriptive measurements do not establish cross-engine superiority, output quality, energy efficiency, or hardware-general performance. Raw JSON, commands, and environment metadata are published. Remaining challenges include signed manifests, time-of-check/time-of-use replacement, operating-system containment, proxy-overhead measurement, and broader experimental matrices.
title: Caleta: An Evidence-Oriented Trust Layer for Reproducible Local Large Language Model Inference

summary: Long-term conversational question answering can require several separated dialogue turns that support an answer only together. We introduce EviCover, a retrieval approach designed to retain this complementary evidence. It converts questions into observable evidence requirements, checks requirement coverage using retrieved source identifiers, and selects turns jointly. We track annotated support sets - the benchmark-labeled dialogue turns associated with each question - through retrieval, reranking, and final answer-generation context. We evaluate the baseline memory pipeline on generated, human-verified LoCoMo conversations and human-written REALTALK conversations, and examine EviCover on REALTALK's 108 multi-hop questions. Compared with the hybrid lexical/dense baseline, support-turn recall among 60 candidate turns rises from 0.526 to 0.575, and recall in the final ten-turn context rises from 0.349 to 0.379. The evidence funnel identifies separate discovery and selection failures, while paired answer evaluation shows that greater evidence recall does not yet establish a correctness gain. This analysis locates where complementary evidence is lost and distinguishes evidence retrieval from its use in answer generation.
title: Where Did the Evidence Go? Diagnosing Proof-Set Loss in Long-Term Conversational Memory

summary: # A Spectral Construction of Natural-Number Arithmetic [Archival DOI](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22512592) ## Arithmetic with its construction history retained This paper constructs natural-number arithmetic from a correlation spectrum and then resolves its values into the expressions by which they are generated. Its central achievement is to connect three levels that are usually studied separately: arithmetic values, the histories of arithmetic operations, and an evolution acting on those histories. The resulting system retains both the familiar numerical laws and information that numerical evaluation alone removes. The source is minimal unbiased compositional change. The least-dimensional faithful irreducible real orthogonal carrier is a rotation plane. Independent composition, exact same-shape self-similarity and unit covariance determine square-root scaling and a Gaussian law. Local information and normalized total correlation give the characteristic local and global lengths. Preservation of constants selects Neumann closure within the stated separated nondegenerate homogeneous local boundary class. Spectral projections are ordered by their Gaussian response before an integer enumeration is introduced. Orientation selects the positive analytic modes. Pointwise modulation and circle-map composition define their addition and multiplication; modulation by the first positive mode defines successor. The paper proves the Peano recursion structure, unique prime factorization and canonical transport under scale and orientation changes. Winding degree certifies the resulting natural-number arithmetic. ## Resolving how a value is generated The next construction retains ordered, bracketed addition and multiplication expressions. Only the specified zero, unit and absorbing reductions are imposed at this level. Arithmetic evaluation identifies expressions with the same value, while each value has a finite expression fibre. This gives a precise space in which the construction of a number can itself be observed. The simplest example is six. Adding six unit leaves and multiplying an additive expression for three by an additive expression for two give the same root value and the same root energy. Their leaf counts are six and five, while their accumulated internal quadratic defects are thirty and thirty-one. In both cases leaf energy plus accumulated defect is thirty-six. The equality at the root coexists with a measurable difference in the construction. A recursive positive law gives equal weight to the admissible root channels and assembles their subhistories independently. This law differs from uniform counting of all complete expressions. Phase invariance determines a finite phase extension. Summing the resolved source over histories and phases recovers the original Gaussian mass of each mode exactly. Expression multiplicity therefore enriches the source without changing its original partition function. Weighted amplitude readout, probability pushforward and conditional expectation have distinct definitions. Exact variance and entropy identities separate the information in the root value from the information remaining within its fibre. The example of six has strictly positive conditional leaf-count variance, giving a concrete instance of information preserved by the resolved construction. ## A complete operator on generation histories The same source weights determine a parent-child assembly response. The paper constructs a nonnegative self-adjoint trace-class operator on the complete counting history space. Its trace tail has an explicit Gaussian bound independent of the number of expressions in each fibre. Finite root cutoffs converge in trace norm, and the full operator generates a contraction evolution with a dissipation identity. The decisive result is a nonzero transfer from an initially invisible history difference to a later value response. A difference supported on the six histories of four has zero initial value readout,

summary: Reflections: BELIEF, DISBELIEF. SPIRIT and MATTER. Skrynnik Sergey Nikolaevich Republic of Kazakhstan, Almaty, science@ast-1c.kz Abstract This work is a philosophical and theoretical study aimed at building a holistic model of reality that unites the physical and subjective aspects of being. It is the original, “manifesto” part of a cycle of eleven articles; it is here that the ideas developed in the subsequent works were first formulated. The work consists of two parts. The first (“Faith, Unbelief”) examines the essence of man and the meaning of life outside the categories of good and evil: questions of immortality, of imperfection as a source of striving, of reason, of freedom of choice and of the idea of the Creator. The main conclusion of this part is that the principle of life is preserved regardless of what a person believes in. The second part (“Spirit and Matter”) draws on the physical model of the work “The Birth of Dimensions: A Formal Skeleton” and draws analogies between the physical and the spiritual: consciousness is considered as a resonant structure that cannot be reduced to matter but is inseparably connected with it. Consciousness and matter appear as different frequency manifestations of a single process, which suggests a possible way of overcoming the traditional opposition of the “spiritual” and the “material”. The structure of the observer, the connection between consciousness and the brain, the soul, attention and the role of life as the medium in which the observer develops are discussed. The work is interdisciplinary and hypothetical in character and is open to critical analysis. Revision dated 2026-11-10: A chapter “Esotericism and Psychology: The Search for Balance” has been added after the chapter “Man and Woman: The Family as a Structure” — an analysis based on the author’s own example. Esotericism and psychology often describe the same things in different languages, and BD can serve as a bridge between the approaches from the side of spirit and from the side of matter. Esotericists can suggest the direction of development, but understanding what they say often comes after the fact, through experience, which is not a failure but the very process of development. From any source the author keeps only what withstands analysis and looks like a manifestation of balance. The chapter “Man and Woman” now notes that the roles of man and woman can intertwine: a woman can be a muse, and a man the one who gives birth to an idea or a work.       Размышления: ВЕРА, НЕВЕРИЕ. It is the original, “manifesto” part of a cycle of eleven articles; it is here that the ideas developed in the subsequent works were first formulated. The work consists of two parts. The first (“Faith, Unbelief”) examines the essence of man and the meaning of life outside the categories of good and evil: questions of immortality, of imperfection as a source of striving, of reason, of freedom of choice and of the idea of the Creator. The main conclusion of this part is that the principle of life is preserved regardless of what a person believes in. The second part (“Spirit and Matter”) draws on the physical model of the work “The Birth of Dimensions: A Formal Skeleton” and draws analogies between the physical and the spiritual: consciousness is considered as a resonant structure that cannot be reduced to matter but is inseparably connected with it. Consciousness and matter appear as different frequency manifestations of a single process, which suggests a possible way of overcoming the traditional opposition of the “spiritual” and the “material”. The structure of the observer, the connection between consciousness and the brain, the soul, attention and the role of life as the medium in which the observer develops are discussed. summary: This record provides supporting numerical data and code for the study "Entry, reciprocity, and severity in self-consistent wrong-motion optical flow." The study investigates a known optical-flow failure in which mutually consistent forward and backward estimates can correspond to an incorrect motion layer. Using controlled two-layer translations, it separately evaluates appearance-dependent alternate-side assignment, reciprocal wrong-motion consistency, and conditional error severity under near alternate-layer substitution. The supporting materials include source-level and pair-level numerical tables, plotted data, representative example arrays, figure-generation scripts, frozen experimental specifications, selected generator and evaluation code, verification scripts, and SHA-256 references to archived experimental results. The experiments use pretrained RAFT-Small, RAFT-Large, and GMFlow with STL-10 and BSDS500 image appearances. Reproducibility scope: The deposited materials support figure regeneration and examination of reported numerical summaries. Complete model prediction archives, original image archives, pretrained model checkpoints, and a complete inference environment are not included. Full prediction-to-metric verification requires the separately identified experimental archives. Original third-party image datasets remain subject to their respective providers' terms. No nuclear-decommissioning footage is included. File access is restricted pending review of publication rights and licensing.

summary: LLM-based agents extend LLMs with tool calls, memory, planning, and retrieval to act in external environments, but they are vulnerable to attacks at different workflow steps. Existing defenses, including prompt engineering and post-training alignment, primarily improve LLM-only safety and often overlook risks that arise from multi-step execution. External verification adds guardrails to check each step separately, but it typically ignores how risks can propagate across steps. We argue that we should consider risk transitions across dependent steps through the agent workflow, rather than separate verification on a single step. In this paper, we propose \textbf{T}ail-risk-aware \textbf{A}gent \textbf{S}afety (TAS), a tail-risk-aware safety framework that models agent workflow safety as a sequence of dependent safety states and constrains the rare but extreme risks (i.e., tail risk) with a shared budget. TAS first models safety-state transitions sequentially along the workflow as an MDP to trace risk propagation, then measures a tail-sensitive risk to target rare but high-cost risks (i.e., tail risk), and constrains the risk with a shared budget to derive a step-wise safety strategy. By constraining tail risk rather than the overall average, TAS suppresses rare high-cost failures while preserving utility in normal cases. Experiments show that TAS achieves better performance compared with eleven baselines across three benchmarks.
title: Tail-risk-aware Agent Safety: Constraining Tail Risks Across Multi-step LLM Agent Workflows

summary: We study group-conditional conformal risk control (CRC) for disjoint and overlapping groups under bounded monotone losses. For disjoint groups, we establish exact finite-sample conditional risk control, two-sided bounds on the group-restricted risk, and fundamental limitations arising from local support and calibration-rank granularity. For overlapping groups, we study two exactly valid approaches: group-restricted calibration followed by union deployment, and direct calibration of the deployed prediction-set family. We characterize the union's limiting reconciliation gap, identify conditions for its disappearance, and establish sharp lower bounds for structured losses in specified product-form models. We also demonstrate a strict size advantage for direct calibration in an ordinal model. Experiments show that direct calibration can reduce prediction-set size, but its efficiency depends on group structure, loss type, and shape fitting. Results on historical diabetic-retinopathy scores further illustrate these tradeoffs. Overall, local support, reconciliation slack, and threshold heterogeneity determine efficiency, with neither approach uniformly dominating.
title: Group-Conditional Conformal Risk Control: Exact Guarantees, Limits, and Overlapping Extensions

summary: Information-flow control (IFC) is a promising approach to enforce policy in agentic AI systems. However, IFC suffers from label creep, a phenomenon where monotonically increasing security labels propagate through a system and progressively limit its utility. Label creep in agentic AI systems can be mitigated using two major strategies: (1) improved system design and (2) label declassification. In this paper, we characterize how far system design alone can mitigate label creep in agentic systems. Specifically, we measure how system topology, scale, and agent composition affect utility loss and security enforcement cost proxies for conservative IFC enforcement in a stateful agentic system simulator. We develop a pipeline to systematically vary these features and measure their impacts on label propagation. Our results demonstrate strong associations between structural graph features and our IFC utility loss metric (up to a Spearman correlation $|ρ|$ of $0.96$) and show that system size and tool allocation substantially affect how labels propagate. These findings identify design choices to reduce IFC utility loss, but they also demonstrate that system design alone cannot fully prevent utility loss due to monotonic label propagation. This motivates the development of label declassification mechanisms that aid these design choices and diminish IFC utility cost.
title: The Limits of Information-Flow Control Enforcement for Agentic Systems

summary: Supervised fine-tuning over a large pool of heterogeneous tasks is often computationally expensive, leading practitioners to train language models on a fixed training budget of carefully chosen SFT tasks. Thus, achieving strong downstream performance hinges on selecting an effective subset of tasks, or equivalently, identifying an optimal task mixture under a fixed budget constraint. In practice, supervised finetuning mixtures are often determined using simple heuristics (e.g., uniform or size-proportional sampling) that ignore task interactions, which can hurt transfer and waste budget on redundant task sources. We introduce TASKMIXPGM, a framework for learning continuous task mixtures through energy-based modelling over SFT tasks. Each task forms a node in a Markov random field, with unary potentials capturing task utility and pairwise potentials modelling inter-task relationships via behavioral divergences between predictive distributions of single-task fine-tuned models. Optimizing this objective yields task mixtures that balance utility, coverage, and redundancy. We further show that the induced set function defined over the set of such tasks is weakly submodular under budget constraints, enabling approximation guarantees for discrete task selection. Empirically, we provide a fixed, benchmark-independent mixture that improves over heuristic mixing across multiple model families and different training budgets. TASKMIXPGM also uncovers interpretable structure in task interactions, revealing complementarities and redundancies that inform effective SFT mixtures.
title: From Task Affinities to Optimal Allocations: Probabilistic Graphical Modelling for Supervised Finetuning

summary: Wildland urban interface (WUI) fires increasingly threaten communities and infrastructure, motivating the need for rapid visual assessment. Recent research has focused primarily on detecting fire and assessing post-event damage. However, structure-level fire threat identification during active WUI fire events remains underexplored. This study evaluates Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct for this active-fire decision using two separately scored tracks: 1,824 synthetic images from 491 designed WUI scenarios and 45 frames from a controlled-burn experiment conducted in collaboration with Columbus Fire & EMS Department. Under zero-shot prompting, the model returned valid target fields for 1,808 synthetic images and 39 controlled-burn frames. Accuracy among valid outputs was 94.0% for the synthetic track and 69.2% for the controlled-burn track, compared with a 16.0% random-selection baseline for the latter. On the synthetic track, the model generally identified the intended target across varied designed WUI scenarios when the relevant fire-spread cues were visually distinct. Controlled-burn performance was well above random selection, but errors showed difficulty interpreting spatial relations in complex scenes. The dual-track protocol provides scalable stress testing in designed scenarios and a controlled-burn reference for assessing model behavior under physical fire conditions. Future work can use the synthetic data for VLM post-training and then evaluate the adapted models on larger and more diverse real WUI fire datasets.
title: Vision Language Models for Primary Structure Threat Identification in Wildland Urban Interface Fires

summary: Widely used dimensionality reduction methods prioritize neighborhood or distance 1 preservation, yet planar coordinates alone cannot certify the homological type or 2 sample-level support of higher-order structures. Obtaining this evidence directly 3 is costly because simplicial complexes grow rapidly with dimension. We propose 4 Certified Homology-Aware Reverse-scale Mapping (CHARM), which combines 5 two-dimensional coordinates with certified homology records and sample-level 6 localization. Diffusion coordinates guide cover proposals; safe contractions and a 7 Cover Quotient Tower reduce the domain of structural computation; exact algebra 8 certifies and tracks homology representatives; and reverse-scale layout places their 9 supports in shared coordinates. Safe contraction preserves the homotopy type of 10 the input flag complex. The quotient tower is multiplicatively 3-interleaved with 11 the coarse-graph hop-distance Rips filtration. Verifiable distance-distortion bounds 12 give an additive guarantee between the original Euclidean and coarse-graph Rips 13 filtrations, and composite multiplicative guarantees for the tower on positive scales. 14 Across 22 datasets and 41,637 samples under a fixed configuration, CHARM 15 ranks among the top two on all 15 sample-weighted metrics for nonsynthetic data, 16 including the smallest values on all four Euclidean persistence-diagram distances. 17 It also provides 957 traceable support records across the full benchmark. On a 18 spherical shell, one certified H2 record identifies 1,578 original samples in the 19 two-dimensional view. CHARM thus combines geometric exploration with explicit 20 evidence of homological type and location.
title: CHARM: Certified Homology-Aware Reverse-scale Mapping via Diffusion-Guided Quotient Towers
